   232→def _shallow_steps(plan: dict) -> list[tuple[str, int, int]]:
   233→    """Return (cluster_name, bare_count, total_count) for clusters with steps lacking detail."""
   234→    results: list[tuple[str, int, int]] = []
   235→    for name, cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).items():
   236→        if cluster.get("auto") or not cluster.get("issue_ids"):
   237→            continue
   238→        steps = cluster.get("action_steps") or []
   239→        if not steps:
   240→            continue
   241→        bare = sum(
   242→            1 for s in steps
   243→            if isinstance(s, dict) and not s.get("detail") and not s.get("issue_refs")
   244→        )
   245→        if bare > 0:
   246→            results.append((name, bare, len(steps)))
   247→    return results
   248→

   508→    stages: dict,
   509→    has_only_additions: bool,
   510→    si,
   511→) -> bool:
   512→    if has_only_additions:
   513→        _print_new_issues_since_last(si)
   514→        return True
   515→    if "observe" not in stages:
   516→        print(colorize("  Cannot confirm existing: observe stage not complete.", "red"))
   517→        print(colorize("  You must read issues first.", "dim"))
   518→        print(colorize('  Run: desloppify plan triage --stage observe --report "..."', "dim"))
   519→        return False
   520→    if "reflect" not in stages:
   521→        print(colorize("  Cannot confirm existing: reflect stage not complete.", "red"))
   522→        print(colorize("  You must compare against completed work first.", "dim"))
   523→        print(colorize('  Run: desloppify plan triage --stage reflect --report "..."', "dim"))
   524→        return False
   525→    return True
   526→
   527→
   528→def _confirm_note_valid(note: str | None) -> bool:
   529→    if not note:
   530→        print(colorize("  --note is required for confirm-existing.", "red"))
   531→        print(colorize('  Explain why the existing plan is still valid (min 100 chars).', "dim"))
   532→        return False
   533→    if len(note) < 100:
   534→        print(colorize(f"  Note too short: {len(note)} chars (minimum 100).", "red"))
   535→        return False
   536→    return True
   537→
   538→
   539→def _resolve_confirm_existing_strategy(
   540→    strategy: str | None,
   541→    *,
   542→    has_only_additions: bool,
   543→    meta: dict,
   544→) -> str | None:
   545→    if strategy:
   546→        return strategy
   547→    if has_only_additions:
   548→        return "same"
   549→    print(colorize("  --strategy is required.", "red"))
   550→    existing = meta.get("strategy_summary", "")
   551→    if existing:
   552→        print(colorize('  Use --strategy "same" to keep it, or provide a new summary.', "dim"))
   553→    return None
   554→
   555→
   556→def _confirm_strategy_valid(strategy: str) -> bool:
   557→    if strategy.strip().lower() == "same":
   558→        return True
   559→    if len(strategy.strip()) >= 200:
   560→        return True
   561→    print(colorize(f"  Strategy too short: {len(strategy.strip())} chars (minimum 200).", "red"))
   562→    return False
   563→
   564→
   565→def _confirmed_text_or_error(
   566→    *,
   567→    plan: dict,
   568→    state: dict,
   569→    confirmed: str | None,
   570→) -> str | None:
   571→    if confirmed and len(confirmed.strip()) >= _MIN_ATTESTATION_LEN:
   572→        return confirmed.strip()
   573→    print(colorize("  Current plan:", "bold"))
   574→    show_plan_summary(plan, state)
   575→    if confirmed:
   576→        print(
   577→            colorize(
   578→                f"\n  --confirmed text too short ({len(confirmed.strip())} chars, min {_MIN_ATTESTATION_LEN}).",
   579→                "red",
   580→            )
   581→        )
   582→    print(colorize('\n  Add --confirmed "I validate this plan..." to proceed.', "dim"))
   583→    return None
   584→
   585→
   586→def _note_cites_new_issues_or_error(note: str, si) -> bool:
   587→    new_ids = si.new_since_last
   588→    if not new_ids:
   589→        return True
   590→    valid_ids = set(si.open_issues.keys())
   591→    cited = extract_issue_citations(note, valid_ids)
   592→    new_cited = cited & new_ids
   593→    if new_cited:
   594→        return True
   595→    print(colorize("  Note must cite at least 1 new/changed issue.", "red"))
   596→    print(colorize(f"  {len(new_ids)} new issue(s) since last triage:", "dim"))
   597→    for fid in sorted(new_ids)[:5]:
   598→        print(colorize(f"    {fid}", "dim"))
   599→    if len(new_ids) > 5:
   600→        print(colorize(f"    ... and {len(new_ids) - 5} more", "dim"))
   601→    return False

    47→        if not refs and (dimensions or cluster_names):

   425→def _canonical_external_payload(
   426→    raw_payload: dict[str, Any],
   427→    *,
   428→    session: dict[str, Any],
   429→) -> dict[str, Any]:
   430→    """Return import payload with canonical provenance and required session token."""
   431→    session_meta = raw_payload.get("session")
   432→    if not isinstance(session_meta, dict):
   433→        raise CommandError(
   434→            "Error: external reviewer payload must include top-level `session` object."
   435→            ' Expected: {"session":{"id":"...","token":"..."},"assessments":{...},"issues":[...]}',
   436→        )
   437→
   438→    payload_id = str(session_meta.get("id", "")).strip()
   439→    payload_token = str(session_meta.get("token", "")).strip()
   440→    expected_id = str(session.get("session_id", "")).strip()
   441→    expected_token = str(session.get("token", "")).strip()
   442→    if payload_id != expected_id or payload_token != expected_token:
   443→        raise CommandError(
   444→            "Error: session id/token mismatch in external reviewer payload."
   445→            " Regenerate output using the session template/instructions.",
   446→        )
   447→
   448→    payload = {
   449→        key: value
   450→        for key, value in raw_payload.items()
   451→        if key not in {"session", "provenance"}
   452→    }
   453→    payload["provenance"] = {
   454→        "kind": "blind_review_batch_import",
   455→        "blind": True,
   456→        "runner": str(session.get("runner", "claude")),
   457→        "session_id": str(session.get("session_id", "")),
   458→        "created_at": _iso_seconds(_utc_now()),
   459→        "packet_path": str(session.get("blind_packet_path", "")),
   460→        "packet_sha256": str(session.get("packet_sha256", "")),
   461→    }
   462→    return payload
   463→
   464→
   465→def _ensure_session_open(session: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   466→    status = str(session.get("status", "open")).strip().lower()
   467→    if status == "open":
   468→        return
   469→    raise CommandError(
   470→        f"Error: session is not open (status={status or 'unknown'}). Start a new session with --external-start.",
   471→    )
   472→
   473→
   474→def _ensure_session_not_expired(session: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   475→    expires_at = _parse_iso(session.get("expires_at"))
   476→    if expires_at is None:
   477→        raise CommandError(
   478→            "Error: session metadata is missing/invalid expires_at.",
   479→        )
   480→    now = _utc_now()
   481→    if now <= expires_at:
   482→        return
   483→    raise CommandError(
   484→        f"Error: session expired at {session.get('expires_at')}. Start a new session with --external-start.",
   485→    )
   486→

   488→def do_external_submit(
   489→    *,
   490→    import_file: str,
   491→    session_id: str,
   492→    state: dict,
   493→    lang,
   494→    state_file,
   495→    config: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
   496→    allow_partial: bool = False,
   497→    scan_after_import: bool = False,
   498→    scan_path: str = ".",
   499→    dry_run: bool = False,
   500→) -> None:
   501→    """Submit external reviewer output via session, adding canonical provenance."""
   502→    config = config or {}
   503→    session_path, session = _session_payload(session_id)
   504→    _ensure_session_open(session)
   505→    _ensure_session_not_expired(session)
   506→
   507→    if str(session.get("runner", "")).strip().lower() not in _EXTERNAL_SUPPORTED_RUNNERS:
   508→        raise CommandError(
   509→            "Error: only Claude external sessions currently support durable score submit.",
   510→        )
   511→
   512→    issues_path = Path(import_file)
   513→    raw_payload = _load_json_object(issues_path, label="external issues")
   514→    canonical_payload = _canonical_external_payload(raw_payload, session=session)
   515→
   516→    stamp = run_stamp()
   517→    session_dir = session_path.parent
   518→    canonical_path = session_dir / f"canonical_import_{stamp}.json"
   519→    safe_write_text(canonical_path, json.dumps(canonical_payload, indent=2) + "\n")
   520→
   521→    if dry_run:
   522→        do_validate_import(
   523→            str(canonical_path),
   524→            lang,
   525→            allow_partial=allow_partial,
   526→            attested_external=True,
   527→            manual_attest=str(session.get("attest", EXTERNAL_ATTEST_TEXT)),
   528→        )
   529→        return
   530→
   531→    do_import(
   532→        str(canonical_path),
   533→        state,
   534→        lang,
   535→        state_file,
   536→        config=config,
   537→        allow_partial=allow_partial,
   538→        attested_external=True,
   539→        manual_attest=str(session.get("attest", EXTERNAL_ATTEST_TEXT)),
   540→    )
   541→
   542→    submitted_at = _iso_seconds(_utc_now())
   543→    session["status"] = "submitted"
   544→    session["submitted_at"] = submitted_at
   545→    session["submitted_input_file"] = str(issues_path)
   546→    session["submitted_canonical_file"] = str(canonical_path)
   547→    safe_write_text(session_path, json.dumps(session, indent=2) + "\n")
   548→
   549→    if scan_after_import:
   550→        code = run_followup_scan(
   551→            lang_name=lang.name,
   552→            scan_path=scan_path,
   553→            deps=FollowupScanDeps(
   554→                project_root=_runtime_project_root(),
   555→                timeout_seconds=FOLLOWUP_SCAN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
   556→                python_executable=sys.executable,
   557→                subprocess_run=subprocess.run,
   558→                timeout_error=subprocess.TimeoutExpired,
   559→                colorize_fn=colorize,
   560→            ),
   561→        )
   562→        if code != 0:
   563→            raise CommandError(f"External review exited with code {code}", exit_code=code)
   564→

    24→def codex_batch_command(*, prompt: str, repo_root: Path, output_file: Path) -> list[str]:
    25→    """Build one codex exec command line for a batch prompt."""
    26→    effort = os.environ.get("DESLOPPIFY_CODEX_REASONING_EFFORT", "low").strip().lower()
    27→    if effort not in {"low", "medium", "high", "xhigh"}:
    28→        effort = "low"
    29→    return [
    30→        "codex",
    31→        "exec",
    32→        "--ephemeral",
    33→        "-C",
    34→        str(repo_root),
    35→        "-s",
    36→        "workspace-write",
    37→        "-c",
    38→        'approval_policy="never"',
    39→        "-c",
    40→        f'model_reasoning_effort="{effort}"',
    41→        "-o",
    42→        str(output_file),
    43→        prompt,
    44→    ]
    45→
    46→
    47→def run_codex_batch(
    48→    *,
    49→    prompt: str,
    50→    repo_root: Path,
    51→    output_file: Path,
    52→    log_file: Path,
    53→    deps: CodexBatchRunnerDeps,
    54→    codex_batch_command_fn=None,
    55→) -> int:
    56→    """Execute one codex batch and return a stable CLI-style status code."""
    57→    if codex_batch_command_fn is None:
    58→        codex_batch_command_fn = codex_batch_command
    59→    cmd = codex_batch_command_fn(
    60→        prompt=prompt,
    61→        repo_root=repo_root,
    62→        output_file=output_file,
    63→    )
    64→    config = _resolve_retry_config(deps)
    65→    log_sections: list[str] = []
    66→
    67→    for attempt in range(1, config.max_attempts + 1):
    68→        header, result = _run_batch_attempt(
    69→            cmd=cmd,
    70→            deps=deps,
    71→            output_file=output_file,
    72→            log_file=log_file,
    73→            log_sections=log_sections,
    74→            attempt=attempt,
    75→            max_attempts=config.max_attempts,
    76→            use_popen=config.use_popen,
    77→            live_log_interval=config.live_log_interval,
    78→            stall_seconds=config.stall_seconds,
    79→        )
    80→        early_return = _handle_early_attempt_return(result)
    81→        if early_return is not None:
    82→            return early_return
    83→        timeout_or_stall = _handle_timeout_or_stall(
    84→            header=header,
    85→            result=result,
    86→            deps=deps,
    87→            output_file=output_file,
    88→            log_file=log_file,
    89→            log_sections=log_sections,
    90→            stall_seconds=config.stall_seconds,
    91→        )
    92→        if timeout_or_stall is not None:
    93→            return timeout_or_stall
    94→
    95→        log_sections.append(
    96→            f"{header}\n\nSTDOUT:\n{result.stdout_text}\n\nSTDERR:\n{result.stderr_text}\n"
    97→        )
    98→
    99→        success_code = _handle_successful_attempt(
   100→            result=result,
   101→            output_file=output_file,
   102→            log_file=log_file,
   103→            deps=deps,
   104→            log_sections=log_sections,
   105→        )
   106→        if success_code is not None:
   107→            return success_code
   108→        failure_code = _handle_failed_attempt(
   109→            result=result,
   110→            deps=deps,
   111→            attempt=attempt,
   112→            max_attempts=config.max_attempts,
   113→            retry_backoff_seconds=config.retry_backoff_seconds,
   114→            log_file=log_file,
   115→            log_sections=log_sections,
   116→        )
   117→        if failure_code is not None:
   118→            return failure_code
   119→
   120→    deps.safe_write_text_fn(log_file, "\n\n".join(log_sections))
   121→    return 1

   124→def run_followup_scan(
   125→    *,
   126→    lang_name: str,
   127→    scan_path: str,
   128→    deps: FollowupScanDeps,
   129→    force_queue_bypass: bool = False,
   130→) -> int:
   131→    """Run a follow-up scan and return a non-zero status when it fails."""
   132→    scan_cmd = [
   133→        deps.python_executable,
   134→        "-m",
   135→        "desloppify",
   136→        "--lang",
   137→        lang_name,
   138→        "scan",
   139→        "--path",
   140→        scan_path,
   141→    ]
   142→    if force_queue_bypass:
   143→        followup_attest = (
   144→            "I understand this is not the intended workflow and "
   145→            "I am intentionally skipping queue completion"
   146→        )
   147→        scan_cmd.extend(["--force-rescan", "--attest", followup_attest])
   148→        print(
   149→            deps.colorize_fn(
   150→                "  Follow-up scan queue bypass enabled (--force-followup-scan).",
   151→                "yellow",
   152→            )
   153→        )
   154→    print(deps.colorize_fn("\n  Running follow-up scan...", "bold"))
   155→    try:
   156→        result = deps.subprocess_run(
   157→            scan_cmd,
   158→            cwd=str(deps.project_root),
   159→            timeout=deps.timeout_seconds,
   160→        )
   161→    except deps.timeout_error:
   162→        print(
   163→            deps.colorize_fn(
   164→                f"  Follow-up scan timed out after {deps.timeout_seconds}s.",
   165→                "yellow",
   166→            ),
   167→            file=sys.stderr,
   168→        )
   169→        return 124
   170→    except OSError as exc:
   171→        print(
   172→            deps.colorize_fn(f"  Follow-up scan failed: {exc}", "red"),
   173→            file=sys.stderr,
   174→        )
   175→        return 1
   176→    return int(getattr(result, "returncode", 0) or 0)

    25→    "strict_target_score",
    26→    "target_score",
    27→    "strict_score",
    28→    "objective_score",
    29→    "overall_score",
    30→    "verified_strict_score",
    31→}
    32→
    33→
    34→def write_packet_snapshot(
    35→    packet: dict[str, Any],
    36→    *,
    37→    stamp: str,
    38→    review_packet_dir: Path,
    39→    blind_path: Path,
    40→    safe_write_text_fn,
    41→) -> tuple[Path, Path]:
    42→    """Persist immutable and blind packet snapshots for runner workflows."""
    43→    review_packet_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    44→    packet_path = review_packet_dir / f"holistic_packet_{stamp}.json"
    45→    safe_write_text_fn(packet_path, json.dumps(packet, indent=2) + "\n")
    46→    blind_packet = _build_blind_packet(packet)
    47→    safe_write_text_fn(blind_path, json.dumps(blind_packet, indent=2) + "\n")
    48→    return packet_path, blind_path
    49→
    50→
    51→def _build_blind_packet(packet: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    52→    """Return a blind-review packet with score anchoring metadata removed."""
    53→    blind = deepcopy(packet)
    54→    for key in _BLIND_PACKET_DROP_KEYS:
    55→        blind.pop(key, None)
    56→
    57→    config = blind.get("config")
    58→    if isinstance(config, dict):
    59→        sanitized = _sanitize_blind_config(config)
    60→        if sanitized:
    61→            blind["config"] = sanitized
    62→        else:
    63→            blind.pop("config", None)
    64→    return blind
    65→
    66→
    67→def build_blind_packet(packet: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    68→    """Public wrapper for blind packet sanitization."""
    69→    return _build_blind_packet(packet)
    70→
    71→
    72→def run_stamp() -> str:
    73→    """Stable UTC run stamp for artifact paths."""
    74→    return datetime.now(UTC).strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
    75→
    76→
    77→def _sanitize_blind_config(config: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    78→    """Drop score/target hints from config while preserving unrelated options."""
    79→    sanitized: dict[str, Any] = {}
    80→    for key, value in config.items():
    81→        lowered = key.strip().lower()
    82→        if not lowered:
    83→            continue
    84→        if lowered in _BLIND_CONFIG_SCORE_HINT_KEYS:
    85→            continue
    86→        if "target" in lowered:
    87→            continue
    88→        if lowered.endswith("_score"):
    89→            continue
    90→        sanitized[key] = value
    91→    return sanitized
    92→
    93→
    94→def sha256_file(path: Path) -> str | None:
    95→    """Compute sha256 hex digest for path contents (or None on read failure)."""
    96→    try:
    97→        data = path.read_bytes()
    98→    except OSError:
    99→        return None
   100→    return sha256(data).hexdigest()
   101→
   102→
   103→def build_batch_import_provenance(
   104→    *,
   105→    runner: str,
   106→    blind_packet_path: Path,
   107→    run_stamp: str,
   108→    batch_indexes: list[int],
   109→) -> dict[str, Any]:
   110→    """Build provenance payload used to trust assessment-bearing imports."""
   111→    packet_hash = sha256_file(blind_packet_path)
   112→    batch_indexes_1 = sorted({int(index) + 1 for index in batch_indexes})
   113→    return {
   114→        "kind": "blind_review_batch_import",
   115→        "blind": True,
   116→        "runner": runner,
   117→        "run_stamp": run_stamp,
   118→        "created_at": datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
   119→        "batch_count": len(batch_indexes_1),
   120→        "batch_indexes": batch_indexes_1,
   121→        "packet_path": str(blind_packet_path),
   122→        "packet_sha256": packet_hash,
   123→    }
   124→
   125→
   126→def selected_batch_indexes(
   127→    *,
   128→    raw_selection: str | None,
   129→    batch_count: int,
   130→    parse_fn,
   131→    colorize_fn,
   132→) -> list[int]:
   133→    """Validate selected batch indexes or raise CommandError."""
   134→    try:
   135→        selected = parse_fn(raw_selection, batch_count)
   136→    except ValueError as exc:
   137→        raise PacketValidationError(str(exc), exit_code=2) from exc
   138→    if selected:
   139→        return selected
   140→    raise PacketValidationError("no batches selected", exit_code=2)
   141→
   142→
   143→def prepare_run_artifacts(
   144→    *,
   145→    stamp: str,
   146→    selected_indexes: list[int],
   147→    batches: list[dict[str, Any]],
   148→    packet_path: Path,
   149→    run_root: Path,
   150→    repo_root: Path,
   151→    build_prompt_fn,
   152→    safe_write_text_fn,
   153→    colorize_fn,
   154→) -> tuple[Path, Path, dict[int, Path], dict[int, Path], dict[int, Path]]:
   155→    """Build prompt/output/log paths and persist prompts for selected batches."""
   156→    run_dir = run_root / stamp
   157→    prompts_dir = run_dir / "prompts"
   158→    results_dir = run_dir / "results"
   159→    logs_dir = run_dir / "logs"
   160→    prompts_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   161→    results_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   162→    logs_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   163→
   164→    selected_1_based = [idx + 1 for idx in selected_indexes]
   165→    print(colorize_fn(f"\n  Running holistic batches: {selected_1_based}", "bold"))
   166→    print(colorize_fn(f"  Run artifacts: {run_dir}", "dim"))
   167→
   168→    prompt_files: dict[int, Path] = {}
   169→    output_files: dict[int, Path] = {}
   170→    log_files: dict[int, Path] = {}
   171→    for idx in selected_indexes:
   172→        batch = batches[idx] if isinstance(batches[idx], dict) else {}
   173→        prompt_text = build_prompt_fn(
   174→            repo_root=repo_root,
   175→            packet_path=packet_path,
   176→            batch_index=idx,
   177→            batch=batch,
   178→        )
   179→        prompt_file = prompts_dir / f"batch-{idx + 1}.md"
   180→        output_file = results_dir / f"batch-{idx + 1}.raw.txt"
   181→        log_file = logs_dir / f"batch-{idx + 1}.log"
   182→        safe_write_text_fn(prompt_file, prompt_text)
   183→        prompt_files[idx] = prompt_file
   184→        output_files[idx] = output_file
   185→        log_files[idx] = log_file
   186→    return run_dir, logs_dir, prompt_files, output_files, log_files
   187→
   188→
   189→__all__ = [
   190→    "build_batch_import_provenance",
   191→    "build_blind_packet",
   192→    "prepare_run_artifacts",
   193→    "run_stamp",

   197→]

   183→def _resolve_retry_config(deps: CodexBatchRunnerDeps) -> _RetryConfig:
   184→    retries_raw = deps.max_retries if isinstance(deps.max_retries, int) else 0
   185→    max_retries = max(0, retries_raw)
   186→    max_attempts = max_retries + 1
   187→    backoff_raw = (
   188→        float(deps.retry_backoff_seconds)
   189→        if isinstance(deps.retry_backoff_seconds, int | float)
   190→        else 0.0
   191→    )
   192→    retry_backoff_seconds = max(0.0, backoff_raw)
   193→    live_log_interval = (
   194→        float(deps.live_log_interval_seconds)
   195→        if isinstance(deps.live_log_interval_seconds, int | float)
   196→        and float(deps.live_log_interval_seconds) > 0
   197→        else 5.0
   198→    )
   199→    stall_seconds = (
   200→        int(deps.stall_after_output_seconds)
   201→        if isinstance(deps.stall_after_output_seconds, int | float)
   202→        and int(deps.stall_after_output_seconds) > 0
   203→        else 0
   204→    )
   205→    use_popen = bool(deps.use_popen_runner) and callable(
   206→        getattr(deps, "subprocess_popen", None)
   207→    )
   208→    return _RetryConfig(
   209→        max_attempts=max_attempts,
   210→        retry_backoff_seconds=retry_backoff_seconds,
   211→        live_log_interval=live_log_interval,
   212→        stall_seconds=stall_seconds,
   213→        use_popen=use_popen,
   214→    )

   217→def _run_batch_attempt(
   218→    *,
   219→    cmd: list[str],
   220→    deps: CodexBatchRunnerDeps,
   221→    output_file: Path,
   222→    log_file: Path,
   223→    log_sections: list[str],
   224→    attempt: int,
   225→    max_attempts: int,
   226→    use_popen: bool,
   227→    live_log_interval: float,
   228→    stall_seconds: int,
   229→) -> tuple[str, _ExecutionResult]:
   230→    header = f"ATTEMPT {attempt}/{max_attempts}\n$ {' '.join(cmd)}"
   231→    started_monotonic = time.monotonic()
   232→    state = _RunnerState(last_stream_activity=started_monotonic)
   233→    ctx = _AttemptContext(
   234→        header=header,
   235→        started_at_iso=datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
   236→        started_monotonic=started_monotonic,
   237→        output_file=output_file,
   238→        log_file=log_file,
   239→        log_sections=log_sections,
   240→        safe_write_text_fn=deps.safe_write_text_fn,
   241→    )
   242→    _write_live_snapshot(state, ctx)
   243→    if use_popen:
   244→        result = _run_via_popen(
   245→            cmd,
   246→            deps,
   247→            state,
   248→            ctx,
   249→            live_log_interval,
   250→            stall_seconds,
   251→        )
   252→    else:
   253→        result = _run_via_subprocess(cmd, deps, state, ctx, live_log_interval)
   254→    return header, result
   255→
   256→
   257→def _handle_early_attempt_return(result: _ExecutionResult) -> int | None:
   258→    return result.early_return
   259→
   260→
   261→def _handle_timeout_or_stall(
   262→    *,
   263→    header: str,
   264→    result: _ExecutionResult,
   265→    deps: CodexBatchRunnerDeps,
   266→    output_file: Path,
   267→    log_file: Path,
   268→    log_sections: list[str],
   269→    stall_seconds: int,
   270→) -> int | None:
   271→    if not result.timed_out and not result.stalled:
   272→        return None
   273→    if result.timed_out:
   274→        log_sections.append(
   275→            f"{header}\n\nTIMEOUT after {deps.timeout_seconds}s\n\n"
   276→            f"STDOUT:\n{result.stdout_text}\n\nSTDERR:\n{result.stderr_text}\n"
   277→        )
   278→    else:
   279→        log_sections.append(
   280→            f"{header}\n\nSTALL RECOVERY after {stall_seconds}s "
   281→            "of stable output and no stream activity.\n\n"
   282→            f"STDOUT:\n{result.stdout_text}\n\nSTDERR:\n{result.stderr_text}\n"
   283→        )
   284→    if _output_file_has_json_payload(output_file):
   285→        recovery_message = (
   286→            "Recovered timed-out batch from JSON output file; "
   287→            "continuing as success."
   288→            if result.timed_out
   289→            else "Recovered stalled batch from JSON output file; "
   290→            "continuing as success."
   291→        )
   292→        log_sections.append(recovery_message)
   293→        deps.safe_write_text_fn(log_file, "\n\n".join(log_sections))
   294→        return 0
   295→    deps.safe_write_text_fn(log_file, "\n\n".join(log_sections))
   296→    return 124
   297→
   298→
   299→def _handle_successful_attempt(
   300→    *,
   301→    result: _ExecutionResult,
   302→    output_file: Path,
   303→    log_file: Path,
   304→    deps: CodexBatchRunnerDeps,
   305→    log_sections: list[str],
   306→) -> int | None:
   307→    if result.code != 0:
   308→        return None
   309→    if not _output_file_has_json_payload(output_file):
   310→        log_sections.append(
   311→            "Runner exited 0 but output file is missing or invalid; "
   312→            "treating as execution failure."
   313→        )
   314→        deps.safe_write_text_fn(log_file, "\n\n".join(log_sections))
   315→        return 1
   316→    deps.safe_write_text_fn(log_file, "\n\n".join(log_sections))
   317→    return 0
   318→
   319→
   320→def _handle_failed_attempt(
   321→    *,
   322→    result: _ExecutionResult,
   323→    deps: CodexBatchRunnerDeps,
   324→    attempt: int,
   325→    max_attempts: int,
   326→    retry_backoff_seconds: float,
   327→    log_file: Path,
   328→    log_sections: list[str],
   329→) -> int | None:
   330→    combined = f"{result.stdout_text}\n{result.stderr_text}".lower()
   331→    is_transient = any(needle in combined for needle in _TRANSIENT_RUNNER_PHRASES)
   332→    if not is_transient or attempt >= max_attempts:
   333→        deps.safe_write_text_fn(log_file, "\n\n".join(log_sections))
   334→        return result.code
   335→    delay_seconds = retry_backoff_seconds * (2 ** (attempt - 1))
   336→    log_sections.append(
   337→        "Transient runner failure detected; "
   338→        f"retrying in {delay_seconds:.1f}s (attempt {attempt + 1}/{max_attempts})."
   339→    )
   340→    try:
   341→        if delay_seconds > 0:
   342→            deps.sleep_fn(delay_seconds)
   343→    except (OSError, RuntimeError, ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
   344→        log_sections.append(
   345→            f"Retry delay hook failed: {exc} — aborting remaining retries."
   346→        )
   347→        deps.safe_write_text_fn(log_file, "\n\n".join(log_sections))
   348→        return 1
   349→    return None
   350→

   392→typical workflow:

   399→  desloppify plan resolve <id> --attest .. # mark as fixed

   402→  Patterns match issues by detector, file, ID prefix, glob, or name.

    33→_LEADING_NUM_RE = re.compile(r'^\d+\.\s*')
    34→_HEX8_RE = re.compile(r'^[0-9a-f]{8}$')
    35→
    36→
    37→def _suggest_close_matches(state: dict, plan: dict | None, patterns: list[str]) -> None:
    38→    """Print fuzzy match suggestions for patterns that resolved to zero issues."""
    39→    all_ids: list[str] = list(state.get("issues", {}).keys())
    40→    if plan is not None:
    41→        seen_ids: set[str] = set(all_ids)
    42→        for fid in plan.get("queue_order", []):
    43→            if fid not in seen_ids:
    44→                seen_ids.add(fid)
    45→                all_ids.append(fid)
    46→        for cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).values():
    47→            for fid in cluster.get("issue_ids", []):
    48→                if fid not in seen_ids:
    49→                    seen_ids.add(fid)
    50→                    all_ids.append(fid)
    51→
    52→    for pattern in patterns:
    53→        segments = pattern.split("::")
    54→        last_seg = segments[-1]
    55→        suggestions: list[str] = []
    56→
    57→        if _HEX8_RE.match(last_seg):
    58→            suggestions = [fid for fid in all_ids if fid.endswith(f"::{last_seg}") or fid == last_seg]
    59→            if suggestions:
    60→                print(colorize(f"  No match for: {pattern!r}", "yellow"))
    61→                print(colorize("  Did you mean:", "dim"))
    62→                for m in suggestions[:3]:
    63→                    print(colorize(f"    {m}", "dim"))
    64→                print(colorize(f"  Tip: match by hash suffix alone: {last_seg}", "dim"))
    65→            continue
    66→
    67→        # Try last segment and second-to-last as descriptive name slugs
    68→        slug = segments[-2] if len(segments) >= 2 else ""
    69→        for fid in all_ids:
    70→            if f"::{last_seg}::" in fid or fid.endswith(f"::{last_seg}"):
    71→                suggestions.append(fid)
    72→            elif slug and (f"::{slug}::" in fid or fid.endswith(f"::{slug}")):
    73→                suggestions.append(fid)
    74→        if suggestions:
    75→            print(colorize(f"  No match for: {pattern!r}", "yellow"))
    76→            print(colorize("  Did you mean:", "dim"))
    77→            for m in suggestions[:3]:
    78→                print(colorize(f"    {m}", "dim"))
    79→
    80→
    81→def _print_pattern_hints() -> None:
    82→    """Print valid pattern format hints after a no-match error.
    83→
    84→    Side-effect only: prints help text to stdout when pattern resolution
    85→    returns zero matches, guiding the user toward valid pattern syntax.
    86→    """
    87→    print(colorize("  Valid patterns:", "dim"))
    88→    print(colorize("    f41b3eb7              (8-char hash suffix from dashboard)", "dim"))
    89→    print(colorize("    review::path::name    (ID prefix)", "dim"))
    90→    print(colorize("    review                (all issues from detector)", "dim"))
    91→    print(colorize("    src/foo.py            (all issues in file)", "dim"))
    92→    print(colorize("    timing_attack         (issue name — last ::segment of ID)", "dim"))
    93→    print(colorize("    review::*naming*      (glob pattern)", "dim"))
    94→    print(colorize("    my-cluster            (cluster name — expands to members)", "dim"))
    95→

   100→    action: str | None = getattr(args, "action", None)

   130→def _cmd_cluster_add(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   131→    state = command_runtime(args).state
   132→    if not require_completed_scan(state):
   133→        return
   134→
   135→    cluster_name: str = getattr(args, "cluster_name", "")
   136→    patterns: list[str] = getattr(args, "patterns", [])
   137→    dry_run: bool = getattr(args, "dry_run", False)
   138→
   139→    plan = load_plan()
   140→    issue_ids = resolve_ids_from_patterns(state, patterns, plan=plan)
   141→    if not issue_ids:
   142→        print(colorize("  No matching issues found.", "yellow"))
   143→        _print_pattern_hints()
   144→        _suggest_close_matches(state, plan, patterns)
   145→        return
   146→
   147→    if dry_run:
   148→        print(colorize(f"  [dry-run] Would add {len(issue_ids)} item(s) to {cluster_name}:", "cyan"))
   149→        for fid in issue_ids:
   150→            print(colorize(f"    {fid}", "dim"))
   151→        return
   152→
   153→    try:
   154→        count = add_to_cluster(plan, cluster_name, issue_ids)
   155→    except ValueError as ex:
   156→        print(colorize(f"  {ex}", "red"))
   157→        return
   158→
   159→    # Check for overlap with other manual clusters
   160→    member_set = set(issue_ids)
   161→    for other_name, other_cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).items():
   162→        if other_name == cluster_name or other_cluster.get("auto"):
   163→            continue
   164→        other_ids = set(other_cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
   165→        if not other_ids:
   166→            continue
   167→        overlap = member_set & other_ids
   168→        if len(overlap) > len(other_ids) * 0.5:
   169→            print(colorize(
   170→                f"  Warning: {len(overlap)} issue(s) also in cluster '{other_name}' "
   171→                f"({len(overlap)}/{len(other_ids)} = {int(len(overlap)/len(other_ids)*100)}% overlap).",
   172→                "yellow",
   173→            ))
   174→
   175→    append_log_entry(
   176→        plan, "cluster_add", issue_ids=issue_ids, cluster_name=cluster_name, actor="user",
   177→    )
   178→    save_plan(plan)
   179→    print(colorize(f"  Added {count} item(s) to cluster {cluster_name}.", "green"))

   232→def _resolve_item_position(
   233→    position: str,
   234→    target: str | None,
   235→    item_ids: list[str],
   236→    ordered_slice: list[str],
   237→    cluster_member_set: set[str],
   238→    cluster_name: str,
   239→    state: dict,
   240→    plan: dict,
   241→) -> tuple[str, str | None, int | None] | None:
   242→    """Resolve where items should be positioned within a cluster.
   243→
   244→    Returns (resolved_position, resolved_target, offset) on success,
   245→    or None if an error was printed and the caller should abort.
   246→    """
   247→    item_set = set(item_ids)
   248→
   249→    if position == "top":
   250→        first_non_item = next((fid for fid in ordered_slice if fid not in item_set), None)
   251→        if first_non_item is None or set(ordered_slice[:len(item_ids)]) == item_set:
   252→            print(colorize("  Already at the top of the cluster.", "yellow"))
   253→            return None
   254→        return ("before", first_non_item, None)
   255→
   256→    if position == "bottom":
   257→        last_non_item = next((fid for fid in reversed(ordered_slice) if fid not in item_set), None)
   258→        if last_non_item is None or set(ordered_slice[-len(item_ids):]) == item_set:
   259→            print(colorize("  Already at the bottom of the cluster.", "yellow"))
   260→            return None
   261→        return ("after", last_non_item, None)
   262→
   263→    if position in ("before", "after"):
   264→        if target is None:
   265→            print(colorize(f"  '{position}' requires a target. Example: --item PAT {position} TARGET", "red"))
   266→            return None
   267→        target_ids = resolve_ids_from_patterns(state, [target], plan=plan)
   268→        if not target_ids:
   269→            print(colorize(f"  No match for target {target!r}.", "yellow"))
   270→            return None
   271→        resolved_target = target_ids[0]
   272→        if resolved_target not in cluster_member_set:
   273→            print(colorize(f"  Target {resolved_target!r} is not in cluster {cluster_name!r}.", "red"))
   274→            return None
   275→        return (position, resolved_target, None)
   276→
   277→    if position in ("up", "down"):
   278→        if target is None:
   279→            print(colorize(f"  '{position}' requires an offset. Example: --item PAT {position} 3", "red"))
   280→            return None
   281→        try:
   282→            offset = int(target)
   283→        except (ValueError, TypeError):
   284→            print(colorize(f"  Invalid offset: {target}", "red"))
   285→            return None
   286→        return (position, None, offset)
   287→
   288→    return (position, None, None)
   289→
   290→
   291→def _reorder_within_cluster(
   292→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   293→    plan: dict,
   294→    clusters: dict,
   295→    cluster_names: list[str],
   296→    position: str,
   297→    target: str | None,
   298→    item_pattern: str,
   299→) -> None:
   300→    """Reorder items within a single cluster."""
   301→    if len(cluster_names) != 1:
   302→        print(colorize("  --item requires exactly one cluster name.", "red"))
   303→        return
   304→    cluster_name = cluster_names[0]
   305→    cluster_member_set = set(clusters[cluster_name].get("issue_ids", []))
   306→
   307→    state = command_runtime(args).state
   308→    item_ids = resolve_ids_from_patterns(state, [item_pattern], plan=plan)
   309→    if not item_ids:
   310→        print(colorize("  No matching issues found for --item pattern.", "yellow"))
   311→        return
   312→    for fid in item_ids:
   313→        if fid not in cluster_member_set:
   314→            print(colorize(f"  {fid!r} is not a member of cluster {cluster_name!r}.", "red"))
   315→            return
   316→
   317→    queue_order: list[str] = plan.get("queue_order", [])
   318→    ordered_slice = [fid for fid in queue_order if fid in cluster_member_set]
   319→
   320→    result = _resolve_item_position(
   321→        position, target, item_ids, ordered_slice,
   322→        cluster_member_set, cluster_name, state, plan,
   323→    )
   324→    if result is None:
   325→        return
   326→    resolved_position, resolved_target, offset = result
   327→
   328→    count = move_items(plan, item_ids, resolved_position, target=resolved_target, offset=offset)
   329→    append_log_entry(
   330→        plan, "cluster_reorder", cluster_name=cluster_name, actor="user",
   331→        detail={"position": resolved_position, "count": count, "item": item_pattern},
   332→    )
   333→    save_plan(plan)
   334→    print(colorize(f"  Moved {count} item(s) to {resolved_position} within cluster {cluster_name}.", "green"))
   335→
   336→
   337→def _reorder_whole_clusters(
   338→    plan: dict,
   339→    clusters: dict,
   340→    cluster_names: list[str],
   341→    position: str,
   342→    target: str | None,
   343→) -> None:
   344→    """Reorder entire clusters as blocks relative to each other."""
   345→    target = resolve_target(plan, target, position)
   346→
   347→    offset = None
   348→    if position in ("up", "down") and target is not None:
   349→        try:
   350→            offset = int(target)
   351→        except (ValueError, TypeError):
   352→            print(colorize(f"  Invalid offset: {target}", "red"))
   353→            return
   354→        target = None
   355→
   356→    seen: set[str] = set()
   357→    all_member_ids: list[str] = []
   358→    for name in cluster_names:
   359→        for fid in clusters[name].get("issue_ids", []):
   360→            if fid not in seen:
   361→                seen.add(fid)
   362→                all_member_ids.append(fid)
   363→
   364→    if not all_member_ids:
   365→        print(colorize("  No members in the specified cluster(s).", "yellow"))
   366→        return
   367→
   368→    count = move_items(plan, all_member_ids, position, target=target, offset=offset)
   369→    append_log_entry(
   370→        plan, "cluster_reorder", cluster_name=",".join(cluster_names), actor="user",
   371→        detail={"position": position, "count": count},
   372→    )
   373→    save_plan(plan)
   374→    label = ", ".join(cluster_names)
   375→    print(colorize(f"  Moved cluster(s) {label} ({count} items) to {position}.", "green"))
   376→

   378→def _cmd_cluster_reorder(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   379→    raw_names: str = getattr(args, "cluster_names", "") or getattr(args, "cluster_name", "")
   380→    cluster_names: list[str] = [n.strip() for n in raw_names.split(",") if n.strip()]
   381→    position: str = getattr(args, "position", "top")
   382→    target: str | None = getattr(args, "target", None)
   383→    item_pattern: str | None = getattr(args, "item_pattern", None)
   384→
   385→    plan = load_plan()
   386→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   387→
   388→    # Validate all names exist
   389→    for name in cluster_names:
   390→        if name not in clusters:
   391→            print(colorize(f"  Cluster {name!r} does not exist.", "red"))
   392→            return
   393→
   394→    if item_pattern is not None:
   395→        _reorder_within_cluster(args, plan, clusters, cluster_names, position, target, item_pattern)
   396→    else:
   397→        _reorder_whole_clusters(plan, clusters, cluster_names, position, target)

   421→def _print_step(i: int, step: str | dict) -> None:
   422→    """Print a single step with title, detail, refs, and done status."""
   423→    if isinstance(step, str):
   424→        print(colorize(f"    {i}. {step}", "dim"))

   426→    done = step.get("done", False)
   427→    marker = "[x]" if done else "[ ]"
   428→    title = step.get("title", "")
   429→    print(f"    {i}. {marker} {title}")
   430→    if done:
   431→        print(colorize("         (completed)", "dim"))
   432→        return
   433→    detail = step.get("detail", "")
   434→    if detail:
   435→        for line in detail.splitlines():
   436→            print(colorize(f"         {line}", "dim"))
   437→    refs = step.get("issue_refs", [])
   438→    if refs:
   439→        print(colorize(f"         Refs: {', '.join(refs)}", "dim"))

   498→def _sorted_clusters_by_queue_pos(
   499→    clusters: dict, queue_order: list[str],
   500→) -> tuple[list[tuple[str, dict]], dict[str, int]]:
   501→    """Sort clusters by (priority, earliest queue position).
   502→
   503→    Clusters with explicit priority sort first (ascending), then unset-priority
   504→    clusters sort by queue position.
   505→
   506→    Returns (sorted_cluster_pairs, min_pos_cache) where min_pos_cache maps
   507→    cluster name to its earliest queue position (999_999 if no members queued).
   508→    """
   509→    pos_map = {fid: i for i, fid in enumerate(queue_order)}
   510→
   511→    def _min_pos(cluster_data: dict) -> int:
   512→        positions = [pos_map[fid] for fid in cluster_data.get("issue_ids", []) if fid in pos_map]
   513→        return min(positions) if positions else 999_999
   514→
   515→    min_pos_cache = {name: _min_pos(c) for name, c in clusters.items()}
   516→    sorted_clusters = sorted(
   517→        clusters.items(),
   518→        key=lambda kv: (kv[1].get("priority", 999), min_pos_cache[kv[0]]),
   519→    )
   520→    return sorted_clusters, min_pos_cache
   521→
   522→
   523→def _print_cluster_list_verbose(
   524→    sorted_clusters: list[tuple[str, dict]],
   525→    min_pos_cache: dict[str, int],
   526→    active: str | None,
   527→) -> None:
   528→    """Print the verbose table view of the cluster list."""
   529→    name_width = max(20, min(35, max(len(n) for n, _ in sorted_clusters)))
   530→    total = len(sorted_clusters)
   531→    has_dep = any(c.get("dependency_order") is not None for _, c in sorted_clusters)

   608→def _cmd_cluster_update(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   609→    """Update cluster description, steps, and/or priority."""
   610→    cluster_name: str = getattr(args, "cluster_name", "")
   611→    description: str | None = getattr(args, "description", None)
   612→    steps: list[str] | None = getattr(args, "steps", None)
   613→    steps_file: str | None = getattr(args, "steps_file", None)
   614→    add_step: str | None = getattr(args, "add_step", None)
   615→    detail: str | None = getattr(args, "detail", None)
   616→    update_step: int | None = getattr(args, "update_step", None)
   617→    remove_step: int | None = getattr(args, "remove_step", None)
   618→    done_step: int | None = getattr(args, "done_step", None)
   619→    undone_step: int | None = getattr(args, "undone_step", None)
   620→    priority: int | None = getattr(args, "priority", None)
   621→
   622→    has_update = any(x is not None for x in [
   623→        description, steps, steps_file, add_step, update_step,
   624→        remove_step, done_step, undone_step, priority,
   625→    ])
   626→    if not has_update:
   627→        print(colorize("  Nothing to update. Use --description, --steps, --steps-file, --add-step, --priority, etc.", "yellow"))
   628→        return
   629→
   630→    plan = load_plan()
   631→    cluster = plan.get("clusters", {}).get(cluster_name)
   632→    if cluster is None:
   633→        print(colorize(f"  Cluster {cluster_name!r} does not exist.", "red"))
   634→        return
   635→
   636→    if description is not None:
   637→        cluster["description"] = description
   638→
   639→    if priority is not None:
   640→        cluster["priority"] = priority
   641→        print(colorize(f"  Priority set to {priority}.", "dim"))
   642→
   643→    # Steps replacement: --steps-file takes precedence over --steps
   644→    if steps_file is not None:
   645→        path = Path(steps_file)
   646→        if not path.is_file():
   647→            print(colorize(f"  Steps file not found: {steps_file}", "red"))
   648→            return
   649→        parsed = parse_steps_file(path.read_text())
   650→        cluster["action_steps"] = parsed
   651→        print(colorize(f"  Loaded {len(parsed)} step(s) from {steps_file}.", "dim"))
   652→    elif steps is not None:
   653→        # Legacy flat strings → wrap as ActionStep dicts
   654→        cluster["action_steps"] = [normalize_step(s) for s in steps]
   655→        print(colorize(f"  Stored {len(steps)} action step(s).", "dim"))
   656→
   657→    # Incremental step operations
   658→    current_steps: list = cluster.get("action_steps") or []
   659→
   660→    if add_step is not None:
   661→        new_step: dict = {"title": add_step}
   662→        if detail is not None:
   663→            new_step["detail"] = detail
   664→        current_steps.append(new_step)
   665→        cluster["action_steps"] = current_steps
   666→        print(colorize(f"  Added step {len(current_steps)}: {add_step}", "dim"))
   667→
   668→    if update_step is not None:
   669→        idx = update_step - 1
   670→        if idx < 0 or idx >= len(current_steps):
   671→            print(colorize(f"  Step {update_step} out of range (1-{len(current_steps)}).", "red"))
   672→            return
   673→        old = current_steps[idx]
   674→        if isinstance(old, str):
   675→            old = {"title": old}
   676→        if add_step is None:
   677→            # When --update-step is used without --add-step, keep title, update detail only
   678→            if detail is not None:
   679→                old["detail"] = detail
   680→        else:
   681→            old["title"] = add_step
   682→            if detail is not None:
   683→                old["detail"] = detail
   684→        current_steps[idx] = old
   685→        cluster["action_steps"] = current_steps
   686→        print(colorize(f"  Updated step {update_step}.", "dim"))
   687→
   688→    if remove_step is not None:
   689→        idx = remove_step - 1
   690→        if idx < 0 or idx >= len(current_steps):
   691→            print(colorize(f"  Step {remove_step} out of range (1-{len(current_steps)}).", "red"))
   692→            return
   693→        removed = current_steps.pop(idx)
   694→        cluster["action_steps"] = current_steps
   695→        title = step_summary(removed)
   696→        print(colorize(f"  Removed step {remove_step}: {title}", "dim"))
   697→
   698→    if done_step is not None:
   699→        idx = done_step - 1
   700→        if idx < 0 or idx >= len(current_steps):
   701→            print(colorize(f"  Step {done_step} out of range (1-{len(current_steps)}).", "red"))
   702→            return
   703→        step = current_steps[idx]
   704→        if isinstance(step, str):
   705→            step = {"title": step}
   706→            current_steps[idx] = step
   707→        step["done"] = True
   708→        cluster["action_steps"] = current_steps
   709→        print(colorize(f"  Marked step {done_step} as done: {step.get('title', '')}", "dim"))
   710→
   711→    if undone_step is not None:
   712→        idx = undone_step - 1
   713→        if idx < 0 or idx >= len(current_steps):
   714→            print(colorize(f"  Step {undone_step} out of range (1-{len(current_steps)}).", "red"))
   715→            return
   716→        step = current_steps[idx]
   717→        if isinstance(step, str):
   718→            step = {"title": step}
   719→            current_steps[idx] = step
   720→        step["done"] = False
   721→        cluster["action_steps"] = current_steps
   722→        print(colorize(f"  Marked step {undone_step} as not done: {step.get('title', '')}", "dim"))
   723→
   724→    # Show resulting steps after any mutation
   725→    final_steps = cluster.get("action_steps") or []
   726→    if final_steps and any(x is not None for x in [steps, steps_file, add_step, update_step, remove_step, done_step, undone_step]):
   727→        print()
   728→        print(colorize(f"  Current steps ({len(final_steps)}):", "dim"))
   729→        for i, s in enumerate(final_steps, 1):
   730→            _print_step(i, s)
   731→
   732→    cluster["user_modified"] = True
   733→    cluster["updated_at"] = utc_now()
   734→    append_log_entry(
   735→        plan, "cluster_update", cluster_name=cluster_name, actor="user",
   736→        detail={"description": description},
   737→    )
   738→    save_plan(plan)
   739→    print(colorize(f"  Updated cluster: {cluster_name}", "green"))

   742→def _cmd_cluster_export(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   743→    """Export cluster steps to stdout in text or YAML format."""
   744→    cluster_name: str = getattr(args, "cluster_name", "")
   745→    export_format: str = getattr(args, "export_format", "text")
   746→

   751→        return
   752→
   753→    steps = cluster.get("action_steps") or []
   754→    if not steps:
   755→        print(colorize("  No steps to export.", "yellow"))
   756→        return

   758→    if export_format == "yaml":
   759→        import yaml  # noqa: PLC0415
   760→        data = {
   761→            "clusters": [{
   762→                "name": cluster_name,

   767→                ],
   768→            }]

   775→def _cmd_cluster_import(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   776→    """Bulk create/update clusters from a YAML file."""
   777→    file_path: str = getattr(args, "file", "")
   778→    dry_run: bool = getattr(args, "dry_run", False)
   779→
   780→    path = Path(file_path)
   781→    if not path.is_file():
   782→        print(colorize(f"  File not found: {file_path}", "red"))
   783→        return
   784→
   785→    import yaml  # noqa: PLC0415
   786→    data = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text())
   787→    if not isinstance(data, dict) or "clusters" not in data:
   788→        print(colorize("  Invalid YAML: expected top-level 'clusters' key.", "red"))
   789→        return
   790→
   791→    entries = data["clusters"]
   792→    if not isinstance(entries, list):
   793→        print(colorize("  Invalid YAML: 'clusters' must be a list.", "red"))
   794→        return
   795→
   796→    plan = load_plan()
   797→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   798→    created = 0
   799→    updated = 0
   800→
   801→    for entry in entries:
   802→        if not isinstance(entry, dict) or "name" not in entry:
   803→            print(colorize(f"  Skipping entry without 'name': {entry!r}", "yellow"))
   804→            continue
   805→        name = entry["name"]
   806→        is_new = name not in clusters
   807→
   808→        if dry_run:
   809→            action = "CREATE" if is_new else "UPDATE"
   810→            step_count = len(entry.get("steps", []))
   811→            print(colorize(f"  [{action}] {name}: {step_count} step(s)", "cyan"))
   812→            continue
   813→
   814→        if is_new:
   815→            try:
   816→                cluster = create_cluster(plan, name, entry.get("description"))
   817→            except ValueError as ex:
   818→                print(colorize(f"  {ex}", "red"))
   819→                continue
   820→            created += 1
   821→        else:
   822→            cluster = clusters[name]
   823→            updated += 1
   824→
   825→        if "description" in entry:
   826→            cluster["description"] = entry["description"]
   827→        if "priority" in entry:
   828→            cluster["priority"] = entry["priority"]
   829→        if "steps" in entry:
   830→            imported_steps = []
   831→            for s in entry["steps"]:
   832→                if isinstance(s, str):
   833→                    imported_steps.append({"title": s})
   834→                elif isinstance(s, dict):
   835→                    step: dict = {"title": s.get("title", "")}
   836→                    if "detail" in s:
   837→                        step["detail"] = s["detail"]
   838→                    if "refs" in s:
   839→                        step["issue_refs"] = s["refs"]
   840→                    elif "issue_refs" in s:
   841→                        step["issue_refs"] = s["issue_refs"]
   842→                    imported_steps.append(step)
   843→            cluster["action_steps"] = imported_steps
   844→        cluster["user_modified"] = True
   845→        cluster["updated_at"] = utc_now()
   846→
   847→    if dry_run:
   848→        print(colorize("  (dry run — no changes saved)", "dim"))
   849→        return
   850→
   851→    save_plan(plan)
   852→    print(colorize(f"  Import complete: {created} created, {updated} updated.", "green"))
   853→

   855→def _cmd_cluster_merge(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   856→    """Merge source cluster into target cluster."""
   857→    source: str = getattr(args, "source", "")
   858→    target: str = getattr(args, "target", "")
   859→
   860→    plan = load_plan()
   861→    try:
   862→        added, source_ids = merge_clusters(plan, source, target)

   866→
   867→    append_log_entry(

   869→        cluster_name=target, actor="user",
   870→        detail={"source": source, "added": added},

   872→    save_plan(plan)
   873→    print(colorize(
   874→        f"  Merged cluster {source!r} into {target!r}: "
   875→        f"{added} issue(s) added, {len(source_ids)} total moved. Source deleted.",
   876→        "green",
   877→    ))

   880→def cmd_cluster_dispatch(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   881→    """Route cluster subcommands."""
   882→    cluster_action = getattr(args, "cluster_action", None)
   883→    dispatch = {
   884→        "create": _cmd_cluster_create,
   885→        "add": _cmd_cluster_add,
   886→        "remove": _cmd_cluster_remove,
   887→        "delete": _cmd_cluster_delete,
   888→        "reorder": _cmd_cluster_reorder,
   889→        "show": _cmd_cluster_show,
   890→        "list": _cmd_cluster_list,
   891→        "update": _cmd_cluster_update,
   892→        "merge": _cmd_cluster_merge,
   893→        "export": _cmd_cluster_export,
   894→        "import": _cmd_cluster_import,
   895→    }
   896→    handler = dispatch.get(cluster_action)
   897→    if handler is None:
   898→        _cmd_cluster_list(args)
   899→        return
   900→    handler(args)
   901→
   902→
   903→__all__ = ["cmd_cluster_dispatch"]

1→"""Prompt construction and data models for epic triage."""

    21→    open_issues: dict[str, dict]       # id -> issue (review + concerns)
    22→    mechanical_issues: dict[str, dict]  # id -> issue (non-review, for context)

    28→    triage_version: int                  # next version number

    40→class ContradictionNote:
    41→    """Record of a resolved contradiction."""

    48→class TriageResult:

    50→
    51→    strategy_summary: str
    52→    epics: list[dict]
    53→    dismissed_issues: list[DismissedIssue] = field(default_factory=list)
    54→    contradiction_notes: list[ContradictionNote] = field(default_factory=list)

    57→def collect_triage_input(plan: PlanModel, state: StateModel) -> TriageInput:
    58→    """Gather all data needed for the triage LLM prompt."""
    59→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
    60→    issues = state.get("issues", {})
    61→    meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
    62→    epics = triage_clusters(plan)
    63→
    64→    open_review: dict[str, dict] = {}
    65→    open_mechanical: dict[str, dict] = {}
    66→    for fid, f in issues.items():
    67→        if f.get("status") != "open":
    68→            continue
    69→        if f.get("detector") in ("review", "concerns"):
    70→            open_review[fid] = f
    71→        else:
    72→            open_mechanical[fid] = f
    73→
    74→    triaged_ids = set(meta.get("triaged_ids", []))
    75→    current_review_ids = set(open_review.keys())
    76→    new_since = current_review_ids - triaged_ids
    77→    resolved_since = triaged_ids - current_review_ids
    78→    previously_dismissed = list(meta.get("dismissed_ids", []))
    79→    version = int(meta.get("version", 0)) + 1
    80→
    81→    # Resolved issue objects (for REFLECT stage)
    82→    resolved_issue_objs = {
    83→        fid: issues[fid] for fid in resolved_since if fid in issues
    84→    }
    85→
    86→    # Completed clusters since last triage completion
    87→    last_completed = meta.get("last_completed_at", "")
    88→    all_completed: list[dict] = plan.get("completed_clusters", [])
    89→    if last_completed:
    90→        recent_completed = [
    91→            c for c in all_completed
    92→            if c.get("completed_at", "") > last_completed
    93→        ]
    94→    else:
    95→        recent_completed = list(all_completed)
    96→
    97→    return TriageInput(
    98→        open_issues=open_review,
    99→        mechanical_issues=open_mechanical,
   100→        existing_epics=dict(epics),

   104→        previously_dismissed=previously_dismissed,
   105→        triage_version=version,

   110→_TRIAGE_SYSTEM_PROMPT = """\
   111→You are maintaining the meta-plan for this codebase. Your goal is to produce
   112→a coherent, prioritized strategy to address ALL open review issues.
   113→
   114→Your plan should:
   115→- Cluster issues by ROOT CAUSE, not by dimension or detector
   116→- Give each cluster (epic) a clear thesis: one imperative sentence
   117→- Order epics by dependency: what must be done first for later work to make sense
   118→- Dismiss issues that don't make sense, are contradictory, or are false positives
   119→- Mark which epics are agent-safe (can be executed mechanically) vs need human judgment
   120→- Avoid creating work that contradicts other work in the plan
   121→- Be ambitious but realistic — aim to resolve all issues coherently
   122→
   123→Available directions for epics: delete, merge, flatten, enforce, simplify, decompose, extract, inline.
   124→
   125→Available plan tools (the agent executing your plan has access to these):
   126→- `desloppify plan queue` — view all items in priority order
   127→- `desloppify plan focus epic/<name>` — focus the queue on one epic
   128→- `desloppify plan skip <id> --permanent --note "why" --attest "..."` — permanently dismiss
   129→- `desloppify plan skip <id> --note "revisit later"` — temporarily defer
   130→- `desloppify plan resolve <id> --note "what I did" --attest "..."` — mark resolved
   131→- `desloppify plan reorder <id> top|bottom|before|after <target>` — reorder
   132→- `desloppify plan cluster show <name>` — inspect a cluster
   133→- `desloppify scan` — re-scan after making changes to verify progress
   134→- `desloppify show review --status open` — see all open review issues
   135→
   136→Your output defines the ENTIRE work plan. Issues not assigned to any epic
   137→will remain in the queue as individual items. Dismissed issues will be
   138→removed from the queue with your stated reason.
   139→
   140→Respond with a single JSON object matching this schema:
   141→{
   142→  "strategy_summary": "2-4 sentence narrative: what the meta-plan says, top priorities, current state",
   143→  "epics": [
   144→    {
   145→      "name": "slug-name",
   146→      "thesis": "imperative one-liner",
   147→      "direction": "delete|merge|flatten|enforce|simplify|decompose|extract|inline",
   148→      "root_cause": "why this cluster exists",
   149→      "issue_ids": ["id1", "id2"],
   150→      "dismissed": ["id3"],
   151→      "agent_safe": true,
   152→      "dependency_order": 1,
   153→      "action_steps": ["step 1", "step 2"],
   154→      "status": "pending"
   155→    }
   156→  ],
   157→  "dismissed_issues": [
   158→    {"issue_id": "id", "reason": "why this issue doesn't make sense"}
   159→  ],
   160→  "contradiction_notes": [
   161→    {"kept": "issue_id", "dismissed": "issue_id", "reason": "why"}
   162→  ],
   163→  "priority_rationale": "why the dependency_order is what it is"
   164→}
   165→"""
   166→
   167→def build_triage_prompt(si: TriageInput) -> str:
   168→    """Build the user-facing prompt content with all issue data."""
   169→    parts: list[str] = []
   170→
   171→    # Section: existing epics
   172→    if si.existing_epics:
   173→        parts.append("## Existing Epics (update these, don't recreate)")
   174→        for name, epic in sorted(si.existing_epics.items()):
   175→            status = epic.get("status", "pending")
   176→            thesis = epic.get("thesis", "")
   177→            direction = epic.get("direction", "")
   178→            fids = epic.get("issue_ids", [])
   179→            parts.append(
   180→                f"- {name} [{status}] ({direction}): {thesis}"
   181→                f"\n  Issues: {', '.join(fids[:10])}"
   182→                f"{'...' if len(fids) > 10 else ''}"
   183→            )
   184→        parts.append("")
   185→
   186→    # Section: what changed
   187→    if si.new_since_last:
   188→        parts.append(f"## New issues since last triage ({len(si.new_since_last)})")
   189→        for fid in sorted(si.new_since_last):
   190→            f = si.open_issues.get(fid, {})
   191→            parts.append(f"- {fid}: {f.get('summary', '(no summary)')}")
   192→        parts.append("")
   193→
   194→    if si.resolved_since_last:
   195→        parts.append(f"## Resolved since last triage ({len(si.resolved_since_last)})")
   196→        for fid in sorted(si.resolved_since_last):
   197→            parts.append(f"- {fid}")
   198→        parts.append("")
   199→
   200→    # Section: all open review issues
   201→    parts.append(f"## All open review issues ({len(si.open_issues)})")
   202→    for fid, f in sorted(si.open_issues.items()):
   203→        detail = f.get("detail", {}) if isinstance(f.get("detail"), dict) else {}
   204→        suggestion = detail.get("suggestion", "")
   205→        dimension = detail.get("dimension", "")
   206→        confidence = f.get("confidence", "medium")
   207→        file_path = f.get("file", "")
   208→        summary = f.get("summary", "")
   209→        parts.append(f"- [{confidence}] {fid}")
   210→        parts.append(f"  File: {file_path}")
   211→        if dimension:
   212→            parts.append(f"  Dimension: {dimension}")
   213→        parts.append(f"  Summary: {summary}")
   214→        if suggestion:
   215→            parts.append(f"  Suggestion: {suggestion}")
   216→    parts.append("")
   217→
   218→    # Section: dimension scores for context
   219→    if si.dimension_scores:
   220→        parts.append("## Dimension scores (context)")
   221→        for name, data in sorted(si.dimension_scores.items()):
   222→            if isinstance(data, dict):
   223→                score = data.get("score", "?")
   224→                strict = data.get("strict", score)
   225→                issues = data.get("failing", 0)
   226→                parts.append(f"- {name}: {score}% (strict: {strict}%, {issues} issues)")
   227→        parts.append("")
   228→
   229→    # Section: previously dismissed
   230→    if si.previously_dismissed:
   231→        parts.append(f"## Previously dismissed ({len(si.previously_dismissed)})")
   232→        parts.append("Maintain unless contradicted by new evidence.")
   233→        for fid in si.previously_dismissed:
   234→            parts.append(f"- {fid}")
   235→        parts.append("")
   236→
   237→    return "\n".join(parts)
   238→
   239→__all__ = [
   240→    "_TRIAGE_SYSTEM_PROMPT",
   241→    "ContradictionNote",
   242→    "DismissedIssue",
   243→    "TriageInput",
   244→    "TriageResult",
   245→    "build_triage_prompt",
   246→    "collect_triage_input",
   247→]
   248→

   278→def _cmd_stage_organize(
   279→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   280→    *,
   281→    services: TriageServices | None = None,
   282→) -> None:
   283→    """Record the ORGANIZE stage: validates cluster enrichment.
   284→
   285→    Instead of gating on a text report, validates that the plan data
   286→    itself has been enriched: each manual cluster needs description +
   287→    action_steps. This forces the agent to actually think about each
   288→    cluster's execution plan.
   289→    """
   290→    report: str | None = getattr(args, "report", None)
   291→    attestation: str | None = getattr(args, "attestation", None)
   292→
   293→    resolved_services = services or default_triage_services()
   294→    plan = resolved_services.load_plan()
   295→
   296→    if not has_triage_in_queue(plan):
   297→        print(colorize("  No planning stages in the queue — nothing to organize.", "yellow"))
   298→        return
   299→
   300→    meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
   301→    stages = meta.get("triage_stages", {})
   302→
   303→    # Jump-back: reuse existing report if no --report provided
   304→    existing_stage = stages.get("organize")
   305→    is_reuse = False
   306→    if not report and existing_stage and existing_stage.get("report"):
   307→        report = existing_stage["report"]
   308→        is_reuse = True
   309→
   310→    if not _require_reflect_stage_for_organize(stages):
   311→        return
   312→
   313→    # Fold-confirm: auto-confirm reflect if attestation provided
   314→    if not _auto_confirm_reflect_for_organize(
   315→        args=args,
   316→        plan=plan,
   317→        stages=stages,
   318→        attestation=attestation,
   319→    ):
   320→        return
   321→
   322→    # Validate: at least 1 manual cluster with issues
   323→    manual_clusters = _manual_clusters_or_error(plan)
   324→    if manual_clusters is None:
   325→        return
   326→
   327→    # Validate: all manual clusters are enriched
   328→    if not _clusters_enriched_or_error(plan):
   329→        return
   330→
   331→    # Validate: all review issues are in a manual cluster (or wontfixed)
   332→    state = resolved_services.command_runtime(args).state
   333→    if not _unclustered_review_issues_or_error(plan, state):
   334→        return
   335→
   336→    # Warn if few/no cluster operations since reflect
   337→    reflect_ts = stages.get("reflect", {}).get("timestamp", "")
   338→    if reflect_ts and not is_reuse:
   339→        activity = count_log_activity_since(plan, reflect_ts)
   340→        cluster_ops = sum(
   341→            activity.get(k, 0)
   342→            for k in ("cluster_create", "cluster_add", "cluster_update", "cluster_remove")
   343→        )
   344→        if cluster_ops == 0:
   345→            print(colorize("  Warning: no cluster operations logged since reflect.", "yellow"))
   346→            print(colorize("  Did you create clusters, add issues, and enrich them?", "yellow"))
   347→            print(colorize("  The organize stage should reflect real work — not just recording a report.", "dim"))
   348→            print()
   349→        elif cluster_ops < 3:
   350→            print(colorize(f"  Note: only {cluster_ops} cluster operation(s) logged since reflect.", "yellow"))
   351→            print(colorize("  Make sure all clusters are properly set up before proceeding.", "dim"))
   352→            print()
   353→
   354→    report = _organize_report_or_error(report)
   355→    if report is None:
   356→        return
   357→
   358→    stages = meta.setdefault("triage_stages", {})
   359→    cleared = _record_organize_stage(
   360→        stages,
   361→        report=report,
   362→        issue_count=len(manual_clusters),
   363→        existing_stage=existing_stage,
   364→        is_reuse=is_reuse,
   365→    )
   366→
   367→    resolved_services.save_plan(plan)
   368→
   369→    resolved_services.append_log_entry(
   370→        plan,
   371→        "triage_organize",
   372→        actor="user",
   373→        detail={"cluster_count": len(manual_clusters), "reuse": is_reuse},

   387→def _cmd_stage_enrich(
   388→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   389→    *,
   390→    services: TriageServices | None = None,
   391→) -> None:
   392→    """Record the ENRICH stage: validate steps have detail/refs for executor readiness.
   393→
   394→    This stage sits between organize and commit. It checks whether action steps
   395→    are detailed enough for an executor with zero context. Steps should have
   396→    ``detail`` (sub-points) and/or ``issue_refs`` (for auto-completion).
   397→
   398→    The agent can still go back and organize (add/remove clusters, reorder)
   399→    at this point — the stage just validates step quality.
   400→    """
   401→    report: str | None = getattr(args, "report", None)
   402→    attestation: str | None = getattr(args, "attestation", None)
   403→
   404→    resolved_services = services or default_triage_services()
   405→    plan = resolved_services.load_plan()
   406→
   407→    if not has_triage_in_queue(plan):
   408→        print(colorize("  No planning stages in the queue — nothing to enrich.", "yellow"))
   409→        return
   410→
   411→    meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
   412→    stages = meta.get("triage_stages", {})
   413→
   414→    # Jump-back: reuse existing report if no --report provided
   415→    existing_stage = stages.get("enrich")
   416→    report, is_reuse = _resolve_reusable_report(report, existing_stage)
   417→
   418→    if not _require_organize_stage_for_enrich(stages):
   419→        return
   420→
   421→    # Auto-confirm organize if attestation provided
   422→    if not stages.get("organize", {}).get("confirmed_at"):
   423→        if attestation:
   424→            from ._stage_validation import _auto_confirm_organize_for_complete
   425→            if not _auto_confirm_organize_for_complete(
   426→                plan=plan, stages=stages, attestation=attestation,
   427→            ):
   428→                return
   429→        else:
   430→            print(colorize("  Cannot enrich: organize stage not confirmed.", "red"))
   431→            print(colorize("  Run: desloppify plan triage --confirm organize", "dim"))
   432→            print(colorize("  Or pass --attestation to auto-confirm organize inline.", "dim"))
   433→            return
   434→
