1→/**
     2→ * useVariantPromotion - Handles promoting variants to standalone generations
     3→ *
     4→ * Manages variant promotion (creating standalone generation from a variant)
     5→ * and adding variants as new generations to shots with timeline positioning.
     6→ */
     7→
     8→import { useState, useCallback } from 'react';
     9→import { toast } from '@/shared/components/ui/runtime/sonner';
    10→import { normalizeAndPresentError } from '@/shared/lib/errorHandling/runtimeError';
    11→import { getSupabaseClient as supabase } from '@/integrations/supabase/client';
    12→import { usePromoteVariantToGeneration } from '@/shared/hooks/variants/usePromoteVariantToGeneration';
    13→import { useAddImageToShot } from '@/shared/hooks/shots';
    14→
    15→interface UseVariantPromotionProps {
    16→  selectedProjectId: string | null;
    17→}
    18→
    19→interface UseVariantPromotionReturn {
    20→  promoteSuccess: boolean;
    21→  isPromoting: boolean;
    22→  handlePromoteToGeneration: (variantId: string) => Promise<void>;
    23→  handleAddVariantAsNewGenerationToShot: (
    24→    shotId: string,
    25→    variantId: string,
    26→    currentTimelineFrame?: number
    27→  ) => Promise<boolean>;
    28→}
    29→
    30→export function useVariantPromotion({
    31→  selectedProjectId,
    32→}: UseVariantPromotionProps): UseVariantPromotionReturn {
    33→  const promoteVariantMutation = usePromoteVariantToGeneration();
    34→  const addImageToShotMutation = useAddImageToShot();
    35→  const [promoteSuccess, setPromoteSuccess] = useState(false);
    36→
    37→  // Handler for "Make new image" button in VariantSelector
    38→  const handlePromoteToGeneration = useCallback(async (variantId: string) => {
    39→    if (!selectedProjectId) {
    40→      toast.error('No project selected');
    41→      return;
    42→    }
    43→
    44→    setPromoteSuccess(false);
    45→
    46→    try {
    47→      await promoteVariantMutation.mutateAsync({
    48→        variantId,
    49→        projectId: selectedProjectId,
    50→      });
    51→
    52→      setPromoteSuccess(true);
    53→      setTimeout(() => setPromoteSuccess(false), 2000);
    54→    } catch (error) {
    55→      normalizeAndPresentError(error, { context: 'useVariantPromotion', showToast: false });
    56→    }
    57→  }, [promoteVariantMutation, selectedProjectId]);
    58→
    59→  // Handler for "Add as new image to shot" button in ShotSelectorControls
    60→  // Positions new image between current and next item in the TARGET shot
    61→  const handleAddVariantAsNewGenerationToShot = useCallback(async (
    62→    shotId: string,
    63→    variantId: string,
    64→    currentTimelineFrame?: number
    65→  ): Promise<boolean> => {
    66→    if (!selectedProjectId) {
    67→      toast.error('No project selected');
    68→      return false;
    69→    }
    70→
    71→    try {
    72→      // 1. Create the generation from the variant
    73→      const newGen = await promoteVariantMutation.mutateAsync({
    74→        variantId,
    75→        projectId: selectedProjectId,
    76→      });
    77→
    78→      // 2. Calculate target timeline frame by querying the TARGET shot's items
    79→      let targetTimelineFrame: number | undefined;
    80→      if (currentTimelineFrame !== undefined) {
    81→        // Query all items in the target shot to find next item and calculate average spacing
    82→        const { data: allShotItems } = await supabase().from('shot_generations')
    83→          .select('timeline_frame')
    84→          .eq('shot_id', shotId)
    85→          .not('timeline_frame', 'is', null)
    86→          .order('timeline_frame', { ascending: true });
    87→
    88→        const frames = (allShotItems || [])
    89→          .map(item => item.timeline_frame as number)
    90→          .filter(f => f !== null && f !== undefined);
    91→
    92→        // Find the next item after current position
    93→        const nextTimelineFrame = frames.find(f => f > currentTimelineFrame);
    94→
    95→        if (nextTimelineFrame !== undefined && nextTimelineFrame > currentTimelineFrame) {
    96→          // Place in the middle between current and next
    97→          targetTimelineFrame = Math.floor((currentTimelineFrame + nextTimelineFrame) / 2);
    98→          // If middle would be same as current (consecutive frames), use current + 1
    99→          if (targetTimelineFrame === currentTimelineFrame) {
   100→            targetTimelineFrame = currentTimelineFrame + 1;
   101→          }
   102→        } else {
   103→          // No next item in shot - calculate average spacing and use that
   104→          if (frames.length >= 2) {
   105→            // Calculate average gap between consecutive frames
   106→            let totalGap = 0;
   107→            for (let i = 1; i < frames.length; i++) {
   108→              totalGap += frames[i] - frames[i - 1];
   109→            }
   110→            const averageGap = Math.round(totalGap / (frames.length - 1));
   111→            targetTimelineFrame = currentTimelineFrame + Math.max(1, averageGap);
   112→          } else {
   113→            // Only one item in shot, use current + 1
   114→            targetTimelineFrame = currentTimelineFrame + 1;
   115→          }
   116→        }
   117→      }
   118→
   119→      // 3. Add to shot
   120→      await addImageToShotMutation.mutateAsync({
   121→        shot_id: shotId,
   122→        generation_id: newGen.id,
   123→        project_id: selectedProjectId,
   124→        imageUrl: newGen.location,
   125→        thumbUrl: newGen.thumbnail_url || undefined,
   126→        timelineFrame: targetTimelineFrame,
   127→      });
   128→      return true;
   129→    } catch (error) {
   130→      normalizeAndPresentError(error, { context: 'useVariantPromotion', showToast: false });
   131→      return false;
   132→    }
   133→  }, [promoteVariantMutation, addImageToShotMutation, selectedProjectId]);
   134→
   135→  return {
   136→    promoteSuccess,
   137→    isPromoting: promoteVariantMutation.isPending,
   138→    handlePromoteToGeneration,
   139→    handleAddVariantAsNewGenerationToShot,
   140→  };
   141→}
   142→

   317→    const currentSettings: SteerableMotionSettings = {
   318→      ...DEFAULT_STEERABLE_MOTION_SETTINGS,
   319→      ...(shotSettingsRef.current.settings?.steerableMotionSettings ?? {}),
   320→    };
   321→    shotSettingsRef.current.updateFields({
   322→      steerableMotionSettings: {
   323→        ...currentSettings,
   324→        ...settings
   325→      }
   326→    });
   327→  }, [shotSettingsRef]);
   328→
   329→  // =============================================================================
   330→  // PHASE CONFIG
   331→  // =============================================================================
   332→  const handlePhaseConfigChange = useCallback((config: PhaseConfig) => {
   333→    // Auto-set model_switch_phase to 1 when num_phases is 2
   334→    const adjustedConfig = config.num_phases === 2 
   335→      ? { ...config, model_switch_phase: 1 }
   336→      : config;
   337→    
   338→    // Clear preset reference when user manually edits config - the config no longer matches the preset
   339→    shotSettingsRef.current.updateFields({
   340→      phaseConfig: adjustedConfig,
   341→      selectedPhasePresetId: null
   342→    });
   343→  }, [shotSettingsRef]);
   344→
   345→  const handlePhasePresetSelect = useCallback((presetId: string, config: PhaseConfig, presetMetadata?: PresetMetadata) => {
   346→    
   347→    // DEEP CLONE: Create completely new config to prevent shared references
   348→    // This ensures modifying LoRA strengths in one phase doesn't affect other phases
   349→    const deepClonedConfig: PhaseConfig = {
   350→      ...config,
   351→      steps_per_phase: [...config.steps_per_phase],
   352→      phases: config.phases.map(phase => ({
   353→        ...phase,
   354→        loras: phase.loras.map(lora => ({ ...lora })) // Deep clone each LoRA
   355→      }))
   356→    };
   357→    
   358→    // Update preset ID, phase config, and generation type mode (if preset specifies one)
   359→    const updates: Partial<VideoTravelSettings> = {
   360→      selectedPhasePresetId: presetId,
   361→      phaseConfig: deepClonedConfig
   362→    };
   363→    
   364→    // Also apply the preset's generation type mode if it has one
   365→    const presetGenerationTypeMode = presetMetadata?.generationTypeMode;
   366→    if (presetGenerationTypeMode === 'i2v' || presetGenerationTypeMode === 'vace') {
   367→      updates.generationTypeMode = presetGenerationTypeMode;
   368→    }
   369→    
   370→    shotSettingsRef.current.updateFields(updates);
   371→  }, [shotSettingsRef]);
   372→
   373→  const handlePhasePresetRemove = useCallback(() => {
   374→    
   375→    // Clear preset ID but keep the current config
   376→    shotSettingsRef.current.updateField('selectedPhasePresetId', null);
   377→  }, [shotSettingsRef]);
   378→
   379→  // Handler for restoring defaults in Advanced mode - respects current I2V/VACE mode
   380→  const handleRestoreDefaults = useCallback(() => {
   381→    const currentSettings = shotSettingsRef.current.settings;
   382→    const isVaceMode = currentSettings?.generationTypeMode === 'vace';
   383→    const defaultPresetId = isVaceMode ? BUILTIN_DEFAULT_VACE_ID : BUILTIN_DEFAULT_I2V_ID;
   384→    
   385→    // Update preset ID to match the restored config
   386→    shotSettingsRef.current.updateField('selectedPhasePresetId', defaultPresetId);
   387→    
   388→    // Force rebuild regardless of current mode (user explicitly clicked "Restore Defaults")
   389→    rebuildPhaseConfig({ force: true });
   390→  }, [shotSettingsRef, rebuildPhaseConfig]);
   391→
   392→  // =============================================================================
   393→  // GENERATION MODE (batch vs timeline)
   394→  // =============================================================================
   395→  const handleGenerationModeChange = useCallback((mode: 'batch' | 'timeline' | 'by-pair') => {
   396→    
   397→    // Optimistically update the cache for THIS shot immediately
   398→    if (selectedShotRef.current?.id) {
   399→      updateShotModeRef.current(selectedShotRef.current.id, mode);
   400→    }
   401→
   402→    // Update the actual settings (will save to DB asynchronously)
   403→    shotSettingsRef.current.updateField('generationMode', mode);
   404→  }, [shotSettingsRef]);
   405→

   409→  const handleSelectedLorasChange = useCallback((lorasToSet: ActiveLora[]) => {

# Triage Tooling Fixes

Fixes to the desloppify triage flow identified by 5-agent audit. Ranked by impact.

## Master Checklist

- [ ] **1. Path validation in ENRICH gate** (high impact, ~1 day)
- [ ] **2. Effort tag requirement in ENRICH** (medium impact, ~0.5 day)
- [ ] **3. Cross-cluster file overlap warning in ORGANIZE** (medium impact, ~1 day)
- [ ] **4. Step title length cap** (low impact, ~0.5 day)
- [ ] **5. Cluster dependency field support** (medium impact, ~0.5 day)

---

## 1. Path validation in ENRICH gate

**The single most impactful change.** Would have caught 3 of 7 documented failure types.

### Problem
`_shallow_steps()` in `_stage_validation.py:232-247` checks that steps have a `detail` field but never validates that file paths in the detail actually exist on disk. Steps referencing `src/nonexistent/path.ts` pass identically to correct paths.

### Fix

**File:** `desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/_stage_validation.py`

Add a new function `_steps_with_bad_paths()` that:

   227→/**
   228→ * Apply pending clip actions to an existing clips array.
   229→ * Resolves each deferred action by filling the first available empty slot,
   230→ * or appending when no empty slots remain.
   231→ */
   232→export function applyPendingClipActions(
   233→  prevClips: VideoClip[],
   234→  actions: PendingClipAction[],
   235→): VideoClip[] {
   236→  let clips = [...prevClips];
   237→  // Track which indices have been filled by previous actions in this batch
   238→  const filledIndices = new Set<number>();
   239→
   240→  for (const action of actions) {
   241→    const emptyIndex = clips.findIndex(
   242→      (clip, idx) => !clip.url && !filledIndices.has(idx),
   243→    );
   244→
   245→    if (emptyIndex !== -1) {
   246→      clips = clips.map((clip, idx) =>
   247→        idx === emptyIndex
   248→          ? {
   249→              ...clip,
   250→              url: action.clip.url,
   251→              posterUrl: action.clip.posterUrl,
   252→              durationSeconds: action.clip.durationSeconds,
   253→              loaded: false,
   254→              playing: false,
   255→              generationId: action.clip.generationId,
   256→            }
   257→          : clip,
   258→      );
   259→      filledIndices.add(emptyIndex);
   260→    } else {
   261→      clips = [...clips, action.clip];
   262→    }
   263→  }
   264→
   265→  return clips;
   266→}

   232→      let augmentedTaskData: Record<string, unknown> | null = taskResultData;
   233→      let cachedShotData: Record<string, unknown> | null = null;
   234→
   235→      if (shotId) {
   236→
   237→        try {
   238→          // Fetch shot with settings
   239→          const { data: shotData, error: shotError } = await supabase().from('shots')
   240→            .select('id, name, settings')
   241→            .eq('id', shotId)
   242→            .single();
   243→
   244→          // Fetch shot generations (input images) - only images, not videos
   245→          const { data: shotGenerations, error: genError } = await supabase().from('shot_generations')
   246→            .select(`
   247→              timeline_frame,
   248→              generation:generations!shot_generations_generation_id_generations_id_fk(
   249→                id,
   250→                location,
   251→                thumbnail_url,
   252→                type
   253→              )
   254→            `)
   255→            .eq('shot_id', shotId)
   256→            .order('timeline_frame', { ascending: true });
   257→
   258→          if (!shotError && !genError && shotData && shotGenerations) {
   259→            // Get generation mode from shot settings
   260→            const travelSettings = (shotData.settings as Record<string, unknown> | undefined)?.travel_between_images as Record<string, unknown> || {};
   261→            const generationMode = travelSettings.generationMode || 'batch';
   262→
   263→            // Extract images with their timeline positions
   264→            const images = shotGenerations
   265→              .filter((sg) => sg.generation?.type === 'image' && sg.generation?.location)
   266→              .map((sg) => ({
   267→                url: sg.generation.location,
   268→                thumbnail_url: sg.generation.thumbnail_url,
   269→                timeline_frame: sg.timeline_frame,
   270→              }));
   271→
   272→            // Store shot data in a clean, standardized format
   273→            // This is the SOURCE OF TRUTH for the share page
   274→            cachedShotData = {
   275→              shot_id: shotId,
   276→              shot_name: shotData.name,
   277→              generation_mode: generationMode,
   278→              images: images,
   279→              settings: {
   280→                prompt: travelSettings.batchVideoPrompt || '',
   281→                negative_prompt: travelSettings.negativePrompt || '',
   282→                frames: travelSettings.batchVideoFrames || 38,
   283→                steps: travelSettings.batchVideoSteps || 6,
   284→                motion: travelSettings.amountOfMotion || 50,
   285→                enhance_prompt: travelSettings.enhancePrompt || false,
   286→                phase_config: travelSettings.phaseConfig || null,
   287→                context_frames: travelSettings.contextFrames || 0,
   288→              },
   289→            };
   290→
   291→          }
   292→        } catch { /* intentionally ignored */ }
   293→      }
   294→
   295→      // Augment task data with cached_shot_data field
   296→      if (cachedShotData) {
   297→        augmentedTaskData = {
   298→          ...taskResultData,
   299→          cached_shot_data: cachedShotData,
   300→        };
   301→      }
   302→
   303→      // Generate unique slug with retry logic
   304→      let attempts = 0;
   305→      const maxAttempts = 5;
   306→      let newSlug: string | null = null;
   307→
   308→      // Fetch creator profile once (outside the retry loop)
   309→      const { data: creatorRow } = await supabase().from('users')
   310→        .select('username, name, avatar_url')
   311→        .eq('id', session.session.user.id)
   312→        .maybeSingle();
   313→
   314→      while (attempts < maxAttempts && !newSlug) {
   315→        const candidateSlug = generateShareSlug(10);
   316→        const creator = (creatorRow as Record<string, unknown> | null) ?? null;
   317→        const normalizedTaskId = typeof taskId === 'string' && taskId.length > 0 ? taskId : null;
   318→        const sharedGenerationInsert = {
   319→          share_slug: candidateSlug,
   320→          ...(normalizedTaskId ? { task_id: normalizedTaskId } : {}),
   321→          generation_id: generationId,
   322→          creator_id: session.session.user.id,
   323→          creator_username: asNullableString(creator?.username),
   324→          creator_name: asNullableString(creator?.name),
   325→          creator_avatar_url: asNullableString(creator?.avatar_url),
   326→          cached_generation_data: generationResult.data,
   327→          cached_task_data: sanitizeTaskDataForSharing(augmentedTaskData),
   328→          shot_id: shotId || null,
   329→        };
   330→
   331→        const { data: newShare, error: insertError } = await supabase().from('shared_generations')
   332→          .insert(sharedGenerationInsert)
   333→          .select('share_slug')
   334→          .single();
   335→
   336→        if (!insertError && newShare) {
   337→          newSlug = newShare.share_slug;
   338→          break;
   339→        }
   340→
   341→        // If error is unique constraint violation, retry with new slug
   342→        if (isUniqueViolationError(insertError)) {
   343→          attempts++;
   344→          continue;
   345→        }
   346→
   347→        // Other error
   348→        if (insertError) {
   349→          normalizeAndPresentError(insertError, { context: 'useShareGeneration', showToast: false });
   350→          toast({
   351→            title: "Share failed",
   352→            description: insertError.message || "Please try again",
   353→            variant: "destructive"
   354→          });
   355→          setIsCreatingShare(false);
   356→          return;
   357→        }
   358→      }
   359→
   360→      if (!newSlug) {
   361→        toast({
   362→          title: "Share failed",
   363→          description: "Failed to generate unique link. Please try again.",
   364→          variant: "destructive"
   365→        });
   366→        setIsCreatingShare(false);
   367→        return;
   368→      }
   369→
   370→      setShareSlug(newSlug);
   371→
   372→      // Notify caller of newly created share
   373→      if (generationId) {
   374→        onShareCreated?.(generationId, newSlug);
   375→      }
   376→
   377→      // Copy to clipboard
   378→      const shareUrl = `${window.location.origin}/share/${newSlug}`;
   379→      try {
   380→        await navigator.clipboard.writeText(shareUrl);
   381→        toast({
   382→          title: "Share created!",
   383→          description: "Share link copied to clipboard"
   384→        });
   385→        setShareCopied(true);
   386→        setTimeout(() => setShareCopied(false), 2000);
   387→      } catch {
   388→        toast({
   389→          title: "Share created",
   390→          description: "Click the copy button to copy the link",
   391→        });
   392→      }
   393→    } catch (error) {
   394→      normalizeAndPresentError(error, {
   395→        context: 'useShareGeneration',
   396→        toastTitle: 'Something went wrong',
   397→        logData: { message: 'Please try again' }
   398→      });
   399→    } finally {
   400→      setIsCreatingShare(false);
   401→    }
   402→  }, [shareSlug, generationId, taskId, shotId, toast, onShareCreated]);
   403→
   404→  return {
   405→    handleShare,
   406→    isCreatingShare,
   407→    shareCopied,
   408→    shareSlug
   409→  };
   410→}
   411→

   277→function useDeleteFromTable(table: 'generations' | 'generation_variants', entityLabel: string) {
   278→  return useMutation({
   279→    mutationFn: async (input: ScopedGenerationInput | ScopedVariantInput) => {
   280→      const projectId = ensureProjectScope(
   281→        input.projectId,
   282→        `useGenerationMutations.useDeleteFromTable.${table}.projectScope`,
   283→      );
   284→
   285→      if (table === 'generations') {
   286→        await verifyGenerationScope(
   287→          input.id,
   288→          projectId,
   289→          `useGenerationMutations.useDeleteFromTable.${table}.scopeValidation`,
   290→        );
   291→
   292→        const { data, error } = await deleteGenerationByScope({
   293→          id: input.id,
   294→          projectId,
   295→        });
   296→
   297→        if (error) {
   298→          normalizeAndPresentAndRethrow(error, {
   299→            context: `useGenerationMutations.useDeleteFromTable.${table}`,
   300→            showToast: false,
   301→            logData: { id: input.id, projectId, entityLabel },
   302→          });
   303→        }
   304→
   305→        if (!data || data.length === 0) {
   306→          normalizeAndPresentAndRethrow(new Error('No rows deleted while enforcing generation scope'), {
   307→            context: `useGenerationMutations.useDeleteFromTable.${table}.noRows`,
   308→            showToast: false,
   309→            logData: { id: input.id, projectId, entityLabel },
   310→          });
   311→        }
   312→
   313→        return;
   314→      }
   315→
   316→      const variantScope = await verifyVariantScope(
   317→        input.id,
   318→        projectId,
   319→        `useGenerationMutations.useDeleteFromTable.${table}.scopeValidation`,
   320→      );
   321→      const { data, error } = await deleteGenerationVariantByScope({
   322→        id: input.id,
   323→        generationId: variantScope.generationId,
   324→      });
   325→
   326→      if (error) {
   327→        normalizeAndPresentAndRethrow(error, {
   328→          context: `useGenerationMutations.useDeleteFromTable.${table}`,
   329→          showToast: false,
   330→          logData: { id: input.id, projectId, entityLabel, generationId: variantScope.generationId },
   331→        });
   332→      }
   333→
   334→      if (!data || data.length === 0) {
   335→        normalizeAndPresentAndRethrow(new Error('No rows deleted while enforcing variant scope'), {
   336→          context: `useGenerationMutations.useDeleteFromTable.${table}.noRows`,
   337→          showToast: false,
   338→          logData: { id: input.id, projectId, entityLabel, generationId: variantScope.generationId },
   339→        });
   340→      }
   341→    },
   342→    onError: (error: Error) => {
   343→      normalizeAndPresentError(error, {
   344→        context: `useDelete${entityLabel.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + entityLabel.slice(1)}`,
   345→        toastTitle: `Failed to delete ${entityLabel}`,
   346→      });
   347→    },
   348→  });
   349→}

   398→export function useInlineEditState(
   399→  media: GenerationRow,
   400→  onNavigateToGeneration?: (generationId: string) => Promise<void>,
   401→): InlineEditStateResult {
   402→  const env = useInlineEditEnvironment(media);
   403→  const persistence = useInlineEditPersistence(env.actualGenerationId, env.selectedProjectId);
   404→  const activeVariant = persistence.variants.activeVariant;
   405→  const effectiveImageUrl = activeVariant?.location || env.effectiveImageUrl;
   406→  useEffect(() => {
   407→    env.setUpscaleActiveVariant(activeVariant?.location, activeVariant?.id);
   408→  }, [env, activeVariant?.location, activeVariant?.id]);
   409→  const { data: availableLoras } = usePublicLoras();
   410→  const { inpainting, magic } = useInlineEditInpaintingAndMagic(media, env, persistence);
   411→  const reposition = useInlineEditReposition(media, env, inpainting, persistence);
   412→  const img2img = useInlineEditImg2Img(media, env, persistence, availableLoras);
   413→  useInlineEditSettingsSync(env.actualGenerationId, persistence.editSettings, inpainting);
   414→  const { sourceGenerationData } = useSourceGeneration({
   415→    media,
   416→    onOpenExternalGeneration: onNavigateToGeneration
   417→      ? async (id) => onNavigateToGeneration(id)
   418→      : undefined,
   419→  });
   420→  const starToggle = useStarToggle({ media });
   421→  const handleDownload = async () => {
   422→    await downloadMedia(effectiveImageUrl, media.id, env.isVideo, media.contentType);
   423→  };
   424→  const {
   425→    inpaintingState,
   426→    transformState,
   427→    generationState,
   428→    imageEditValue,
   429→  } = buildInlineEditStateModels({
   430→    env,

   432→    inpainting,
   433→    magic,
   434→    reposition,
   435→    img2img,
   436→    starToggle,
   437→    handleDownload,
   438→  });
   439→  return {
   440→    media,

   449→  const navigation = useLightboxNavigationModel(input.core, input.navigation);

   502→export function useSharedLightboxState(input: UseSharedLightboxStateInput): UseSharedLightboxStateReturn {

   517→    effectiveMedia: presentationState.effectiveMedia,

     9→interface AutoTopupPreferences {

    18→
    19→// Fetch user's auto-top-up preferences
    20→async function fetchAutoTopupPreferences(): Promise<AutoTopupPreferences> {
    21→  const { data: { user }, error: authError } = await getSupabase().auth.getUser();
    22→  
    23→  if (authError || !user) {
    24→    throw new Error('Authentication required');
    25→  }
    26→
    27→  // Try without the problematic field first, since we know it's causing 400 errors
    28→  
    29→  // Fetch auto-topup preferences.
    30→  // IMPORTANT: Stripe IDs are NOT selected client-side (column privileges revoked).
    31→  const { data, error } = await getSupabase()
    32→    .from('users')
    33→    .select(`
    34→      auto_topup_enabled,
    35→      auto_topup_amount,
    36→      auto_topup_threshold,
    37→      auto_topup_last_triggered,
    38→      auto_topup_setup_completed
    39→    `)
    40→    .eq('id', user.id)
    41→    .single();
    42→
    43→  if (error) {
    44→    throw new Error(`Failed to fetch auto-top-up preferences: ${error.message}`);
    45→  }
    46→
    47→  const hasPaymentMethod = !!data?.auto_topup_setup_completed;
    48→
    49→  return {
    50→    enabled: data?.auto_topup_enabled || false,
    51→    // Setup completed if payment method is configured
    52→    setupCompleted: hasPaymentMethod,
    53→    amount: data?.auto_topup_amount ? data.auto_topup_amount / 100 : 50, // Convert cents to dollars
    54→    threshold: data?.auto_topup_threshold ? data.auto_topup_threshold / 100 : 10, // Convert cents to dollars
    55→    hasPaymentMethod,
    56→    lastTriggered: data?.auto_topup_last_triggered ?? undefined,
    57→    // Note: Stripe IDs are intentionally NOT exposed to frontend
    58→  };
    59→}
    60→
    61→// Update auto-top-up preferences
    62→interface UpdateAutoTopupParams {
    63→  enabled: boolean;
    64→  amount?: number; // in dollars
    65→  threshold?: number; // in dollars
    66→}
    67→
    68→async function updateAutoTopupPreferences(params: UpdateAutoTopupParams): Promise<void> {
    69→  
    70→  const { data: { session }, error: authError } = await getSupabase().auth.getSession();
    71→  
    72→  if (authError || !session) {
    73→    throw new Error('Authentication required');
    74→  }
    75→
    76→  const requestBody = {

    78→    autoTopupAmount: params.amount,
    79→    autoTopupThreshold: params.threshold,

    81→  
    82→  // Call the setup-auto-topup edge function
    83→  const data = await invokeWithTimeout('setup-auto-topup', {
    84→    body: requestBody,
    85→    headers: {

     9→/** Sort a positions map by frame number (ascending), returning [id, frame] entries. */
    10→export const sortPositionEntries = (positions: Map<string, number>): [string, number][] =>
    11→  [...positions.entries()].sort((a, b) => a[1] - b[1]);
    12→
    13→// Minimum gap between frames (4N+1 format, starting at 5)
    14→const MIN_GAP = 5;
    15→
    16→/**
    17→ * Quantize all positions to ensure gaps between adjacent items are in 4N+1 format.
    18→ * First item remains at position 0, subsequent items are adjusted to have quantized gaps.
    19→ * The trailing endpoint is extracted before quantizing and re-added after (its gap has
    20→ * different constraints — quantization happens in the drag handler).
    21→ */
    22→export const quantizePositions = (positions: Map<string, number>): Map<string, number> => {
    23→  // Extract trailing endpoint before quantizing
    24→  const trailingValue = positions.get(TRAILING_ENDPOINT_KEY);
    25→  const imagePositions = new Map(positions);
    26→  imagePositions.delete(TRAILING_ENDPOINT_KEY);
    27→
    28→  const entries = sortPositionEntries(imagePositions);
    29→
    30→  if (entries.length === 0) {
    31→    // If only trailing existed, return it as-is
    32→    const result = new Map<string, number>();
    33→    if (trailingValue !== undefined) result.set(TRAILING_ENDPOINT_KEY, trailingValue);
    34→    return result;
    35→  }
    36→
    37→  const result = new Map<string, number>();
    38→
    39→  // First item always at 0
    40→  result.set(entries[0][0], 0);
    41→
    42→  // Subsequent items: quantize the gap from previous
    43→  for (let i = 1; i < entries.length; i++) {
    44→    const [id, pos] = entries[i];
    45→    const prevPos = result.get(entries[i - 1][0]) ?? 0;
    46→    const originalGap = pos - entries[i - 1][1];
    47→    const quantizedGap = quantizeGap(Math.max(originalGap, MIN_GAP), MIN_GAP);
    48→    result.set(id, prevPos + quantizedGap);

    52→  if (trailingValue !== undefined) {

    56→  return result;

    63→const shrinkOversizedGaps = (

   132→
   133→  // Limit movement to 50 frames per drag for natural feel
   134→  const maxSingleMove = 50;
   135→  const limitedMovement = Math.max(-maxSingleMove, Math.min(maxSingleMove, movementAmount));
   136→  const limitedTargetFrame = originalPos + limitedMovement;
   137→
   138→  const result = new Map(positions);
   139→  result.set(draggedId, limitedTargetFrame);
   140→
   141→  // Apply gap constraints (this also handles frame 0 enforcement)
   142→  return shrinkOversizedGaps(result, excludeId, skipQuantization);
   143→};
   144→
   145→// Convert pixel position to frame number
   146→export const pixelToFrame = (pixelX: number, containerWidth: number, fullMin: number, fullRange: number): number => {
   147→  const fraction = pixelX / containerWidth;
   148→  return Math.round(fullMin + fraction * fullRange);
   149→};
   150→
   151→// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   152→// Multi-select bundling: bundle selected items 5 frames apart
   153→// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   154→const BUNDLE_GAP = 5;
   155→
   156→export const applyFluidTimelineMulti = (
   157→  positions: Map<string, number>,
   158→  selectedIds: string[],
   159→  targetFrame: number,
   160→  skipQuantization: boolean = false,
   161→): Map<string, number> => {
   162→  if (selectedIds.length === 0) return positions;
   163→  if (selectedIds.length === 1) {
   164→    return applyFluidTimeline(positions, selectedIds[0], targetFrame, undefined, 0, Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, skipQuantization);
   165→  }
   166→
   167→  const result = new Map(positions);
   168→
   169→  // Sort selected items by current position to preserve relative order
   170→  const selectedWithPositions = selectedIds
   171→    .map(id => ({ id, frame: positions.get(id) ?? 0 }))
   172→    .sort((a, b) => a.frame - b.frame);
   173→
   174→  // Place selected items 5 frames apart
   175→  selectedWithPositions.forEach((item, index) => {
   176→    result.set(item.id, targetFrame + (index * BUNDLE_GAP));
   177→  });
   178→
   179→  // Push out non-selected items that are within the bundle range
   180→  const bundleEnd = targetFrame + ((selectedIds.length - 1) * BUNDLE_GAP);
   181→  const nonSelectedItems = [...positions.entries()]
   182→    .filter(([id]) => !selectedIds.includes(id));
   183→
   184→  nonSelectedItems.forEach(([id, pos]) => {
   185→    if (pos >= targetFrame && pos <= bundleEnd) {
   186→      result.set(id, bundleEnd + BUNDLE_GAP);
   187→    }
   188→  });
   189→
   190→  // Apply gap constraints (handles frame 0 enforcement)
   191→  return shrinkOversizedGaps(result, undefined, skipQuantization);
   192→};
   193→

     2→

    14→
    15→## 1. Path validation in ENRICH gate
    16→
    17→**The single most impactful change.** Would have caught 3 of 7 documented failure types.
    18→
    19→### Problem
    20→`_shallow_steps()` in `_stage_validation.py:232-247` checks that steps have a `detail` field but never validates that file paths in the detail actually exist on disk. Steps referencing `src/nonexistent/path.ts` pass identically to correct paths.
    21→
    22→### Fix
    23→
    24→**File:** `desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/_stage_validation.py`
    25→
    26→Add a new function `_steps_with_bad_paths()` that:
    27→1. Iterates all manual cluster steps (same loop shape as `_shallow_steps`)
    28→2. Extracts file paths from `detail` text using regex: `re.findall(r'(?:src|supabase)/[\w./-]+\.\w+', detail)`
    29→3. For each extracted path, checks `Path(repo_root / path).exists()`
    30→4. Also tries common extension swaps: `.ts` ↔ `.tsx`, `.js` ↔ `.jsx`
    31→5. Returns `list[tuple[str, int, list[str]]]` — `(cluster_name, step_index, bad_paths)`
    32→
    33→Call it from two places:
    34→- **`_cmd_stage_enrich()`** at line ~436 (after `_shallow_steps` check): if bad paths found, print warning with details but don't block (first pass is advisory)
    35→- **`_confirm_enrich()`** at line ~376 (after `_shallow_steps` re-check): if bad paths found, **block confirmation** with actionable error listing each bad path and which step it's in
    36→
    37→```python
    38→import re
    39→from pathlib import Path
    40→
    41→_PATH_RE = re.compile(r'(?:src|supabase)/[\w./-]+\.\w+')
    42→_EXT_SWAPS = {'.ts': '.tsx', '.tsx': '.ts', '.js': '.jsx', '.jsx': '.js'}
    43→
    44→def _steps_with_bad_paths(plan: dict, repo_root: Path) -> list[tuple[str, int, list[str]]]:
    45→    """Return steps referencing file paths that don't exist on disk."""
    46→    results = []
    47→    for name, cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).items():
    48→        if cluster.get("auto") or not cluster.get("issue_ids"):
    49→            continue
    50→        for i, step in enumerate(cluster.get("action_steps") or []):
    51→            if not isinstance(step, dict):
    52→                continue
    53→            detail = step.get("detail", "")
    54→            if not detail:
    55→                continue
    56→            bad = []
    57→            for path_str in _PATH_RE.findall(detail):
    58→                p = repo_root / path_str
    59→                if p.exists():
    60→                    continue
    61→                # Try extension swap
    62→                alt_ext = _EXT_SWAPS.get(p.suffix)
    63→                if alt_ext and p.with_suffix(alt_ext).exists():
    64→                    continue
    65→                bad.append(path_str)
    66→            if bad:
    67→                results.append((name, i + 1, bad))
    68→    return results
    69→```
    70→
    71→**Repo root resolution:** Use the existing `command_runtime(args).root` or find `.desloppify/` parent.

    75→- Step with bad path → flagged
    76→- Step with `.ts` that exists as `.tsx` → not flagged (extension swap)
    77→- Step with no paths in detail → not flagged
    78→- Auto clusters skipped

### ERROR_CONSISTENCY

**[79baeebf] useAutoTopupState mutates local state optimistically but never reverts on server failure**

**Verdict: GENUINE**

Evidence: In `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/domains/billing/components/CreditsManagement/hooks/useAutoTopupState.ts`:
- `handleAutoTopupToggle` (line 82): calls `setLocalAutoTopupEnabled(enabled)` immediately, then calls `updateAutoTopup(saveData)`. 
- `handleAutoTopupThresholdChange` (line 93): calls `setLocalAutoTopupThreshold(threshold)` immediately, then debounces the save.
- `handlePurchaseAmountChange` (line 109): calls `setPurchaseAmount(amount)` and `setLocalAutoTopupThreshold(newThreshold)` immediately, then saves.

The underlying `useAutoTopup` hook (in `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/hooks/billing/useAutoTopup.ts`) has `onError` that logs but does NOT revert local state. The query invalidation in `onSuccess` would eventually correct state, but on failure, local state stays optimistically updated with no revert and no user notification (`showToast: false`).

Notes: This is a real bug. The user could toggle auto-topup, see it as "enabled" in the UI, but the server never persisted the change. Fix: either revert local state in `onError` callback, or switch to React Query's built-in optimistic update pattern with rollback.

**[d1bf3224] useJoinClips.handleAddToJoin catches errors with showToast: false, giving no user feedback on failure**

**Verdict: GENUINE but LOW SEVERITY**

Evidence: `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/domains/media-lightbox/hooks/useJoinClips.ts` line 90: `normalizeAndPresentError(error, { context: 'useJoinClips', showToast: false })`. The error is caught, logged, but the user sees nothing.

However, important context: `handleAddToJoin` (lines 43-93) is entirely a **localStorage operation** -- it reads/writes localStorage and doesn't make any network calls. The only realistic failure mode is a corrupt localStorage JSON parse. The `finally` block (line 92) does reset `isAddingToJoin` to false, so the UI doesn't get stuck.

Notes: While technically genuine (errors are swallowed silently), this is a localStorage write operation where failure is extremely rare and non-critical. Adding a toast would be reasonable but this is low severity. Borderline over-engineering to prioritize.

**[aaf84e91] useVariantPromotion.handlePromoteToGeneration catches mutation error silently on user-initiated action**

**Verdict: GENUINE**

Evidence: `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/domains/media-lightbox/hooks/useVariantPromotion.ts` lines 54-55: `normalizeAndPresentError(error, { context: 'useVariantPromotion', showToast: false })`. This is a user-initiated action ("Make new image" button, line 37 comment) that calls `promoteVariantMutation.mutateAsync` -- a network mutation. On failure, the user gets no feedback. The `handleAddVariantAsNewGenerationToShot` (line 129) similarly silences errors with `showToast: false`.

Unlike the join clips case, this involves actual server mutations (creating a generation, adding to a shot). Silent failure here means the user clicks a button, nothing happens, and they have no idea why.

Notes: This should be fixed. At minimum, `showToast: true` for user-initiated mutations. The `handleAddVariantAsNewGenerationToShot` at least returns `false` on error so the caller could theoretically handle it, but `handlePromoteToGeneration` has no such signal.

**[d9da7cc5] Two error strategies (OperationResult and throw+normalizeAndPresentError) coexist without selection guidance**

**Verdict: GENUINE**

Evidence: 
- `OperationResult` pattern used in: auth flows (`runAuthSupabaseOperation.ts`), session probing (`supabaseSession.ts`), media playback (`safePlay.ts`), tool settings (`toolSettingsService.ts`), edge functions (`edgeOperation.ts`, `edgeRequest.ts`), billing (`billing.ts`), rate limiting (`rateLimit.ts`), clip metadata.
- `throw + normalizeAndPresentError` pattern used in: 101 files across the codebase (176 occurrences of `showToast: false` alone).

There are two independent `OperationResult` types -- one in `src/shared/lib/operationResult.ts` and another in `supabase/functions/_shared/edgeOperation.ts`. The frontend one has `policy` fields (`fail_closed`, `fail_open`, `degrade`, `best_effort`); the edge one may differ.

No documentation or selection guidance exists for when to use which pattern.

Notes: This is a real architectural inconsistency. The `OperationResult` pattern is more structured and supports explicit failure policies, but it's used in maybe 10-15 files while throw+catch is used in 100+. The two approaches aren't inherently incompatible (OperationResult for operations that can degrade; throw for fatal errors), but without guidance, the choice is ad-hoc. The fix is documentation/guidance rather than code change -- adding a section to the error handling doc explaining when to use which pattern.

## Structured Analysis

### design_coherence (8 issues)

**[898b3c7d] GenerationTokenPanel takes 18 individual props where a config object pattern would be clearer**

**Verdict: Genuine, but borderline over-engineering to fix.**

Evidence: The interface `GenerationTokenPanelProps` (lines 32-49 of `GenerationTokenPanel.tsx`) declares exactly 18 props. The claim is accurate. However, these props naturally fall into coherent groups: 4 value/setter pairs for config options (computerType, gpuType, memoryProfile, windowsShell), a boolean toggle (showDebugLogs), tab state, and one action callback. Grouping into a config object would help readability but the component is a leaf component -- it doesn't pass these props further. The real issue is the parent coupling, not the prop count itself. A config object would reduce the prop list to ~4-5 grouped objects. Mild improvement, not urgent.

**[b634fc71] useGenerationsPaneController returns 60+ values mixing pane lifecycle, filters, data, and navigation**

**Verdict: Genuine.**

Evidence: The return object (lines 217-282 of `useGenerationsPaneController.ts`) contains exactly **65 fields**. This is a classic "god hook" -- it returns pane state (isLocked, paneProps, transformClass, showBackdrop), filter state (mediaTypeFilter, selectedShotFilter, starredOnly, searchTerm), gallery data (paginatedData, totalCount, page), UI state (shotFilterOpen, mediaTypeFilterOpen, isSearchOpen), refs, and navigation. The claim of "60+ values" is verified. This is a legitimate design concern -- the hook is the entire controller for the pane, and splitting into sub-hooks that the pane composes would improve maintainability.

**[af79d5c0] parseSegmentOverrides manually checks 15+ fields with identical parse-assign-if-present pattern**

**Verdict: Genuine, but fix would be over-engineering.**

Evidence: `parseSegmentOverrides` (lines 115-202 of `generationMetadata.ts`) manually parses **15 fields** (prompt, negativePrompt, textBeforePrompts, textAfterPrompts, motionMode, amountOfMotion, phaseConfig, selectedPhasePresetId, loras, numFrames, randomSeed, seed, structureMotionStrength, structureTreatment, structureUni3cEndPercent). The pattern is indeed repetitive: parse value, check if defined, assign if present. However, this is a **runtime type-checking boundary** for untrusted JSON data. Each field has a distinct validation strategy (asString, asNumber, asBoolean, asMotionMode, isPhaseConfig, array filtering). A table-driven approach would either lose type safety or require complex generics. The explicitness here is deliberate and correct for a safety boundary. Fixing this would likely introduce abstraction that obscures the validation logic.

### abstraction_fitness (3 issues)

**[e4f0d065] useShotEditorLayoutPayloadModel is 340 lines of 1:1 field forwarding**

**Verdict: Genuine, but the "fix" is nuanced -- the abstraction serves a purpose.**

Evidence: The file is exactly 340 lines. The function (lines 142-340) takes a structured `UseShotEditorLayoutPayloadModelParams` input (already organized into `core`, `images`, `controllers`, `settings`, `dimensions`, `sections` groups) and produces 6 output models (`contextInput`, `headerModel`, `finalVideoModel`, `timelineModel`, `generationModel`, `modalsModel`) each wrapped in `useMemo`. The forwarding is indeed mostly 1:1 with some renaming (e.g., `handleReorderImagesInShot` -> `handleImageReorder`, `handleAcceleratedChange` -> `onAcceleratedChange`). However, this is a **view model adapter** -- it reshapes data from domain/controller shape into layout component shape. The type safety and explicit mapping is intentional. The 340 lines are mostly type definitions (lines 1-140) and the memo'd reshaping. It is verbose but serves as the contract boundary between the editor state and the layout. Not 1:1 forwarding -- it aggregates from multiple sources into different shapes.

**[43d5957e] useVideoEditPanelModel forwards 25+ fields through useMemo with trivial renaming**

**Verdict: Genuine but mild.**

Evidence: The file is 84 lines. The function (lines 16-84) creates a `useMemo` that reorganizes `editModel.videoMode.*` fields into a structured object with `trim`, `replace`, `enhance` groups plus `regenerateFormProps` and `taskId`. It forwards about **27 fields** total. There is some renaming (e.g., `setStartTrim` -> `onStartTrimChange`, `saveTrimmedVideo` -> `onSaveTrim`). Like the previous issue, this is a view model adapter that reshapes from hook internals to component-facing API. The renaming follows a convention (set* -> on*Change). The memo dependency array is exhaustive (25 entries). This is a code smell but the reshaping is deliberate -- it decouples the edit model internals from the panel component's prop interface.

**[43845973] useUpdatingTimestamp is a zero-behavior alias for useRelativeTimestamp**

Evidence: In `useUpdatingTimestamp.ts` (line 42-44):
```typescript
export function useUpdatingTimestamp(options: UseUpdatingTimestampOptions = {}): string | null {
  return useRelativeTimestamp(options);

This is literally a one-line wrapper that adds zero behavior. It has 4 call sites (`UpdatingTimeCell.tsx`, `BatchSelector.tsx`, `VideoUploadList.tsx`, plus tests). The `useRelativeTimestamp` function is defined in the same file (line 27) and is the real implementation. `useUpdatingTimestamp` exists purely as a legacy name. ### mid_level_elegance (3 issues)

**[384b83f8] useLoraPersistence takes 14 destructured args from useLoraManager**

**Verdict: Genuine.**

Evidence: The call site in `useLoraManager.tsx` (lines 186-201) passes exactly **14 arguments**: `projectId`, `shotId`, `persistenceScope`, `persistenceKey`, `disableAutoLoad`, `enableProjectPersistence`, `selectedLoras`, `selectedLorasRef`, `availableLoras`, `handleAddLora`, `handleRemoveLora`, `handleLoraStrengthChange`, `markAsUserSet`, `setHasEverSetLoras`. The interface `UseLoraPersistenceArgs` (lines 13-28 of `loraPersistence.tsx`) confirms all 14. This is a lot of coupling. The persistence hook needs to call back into the manager (add/remove/strength callbacks) to apply loaded loras, which creates a circular dependency smell. However, the alternative (having the manager poll persistence results) would be more complex. The 14 args could be reduced by passing the lora manager as an object, but that would just push the coupling one level up.

**[90d25443] useAdjustedTaskDetails mixes 3-level param resolution with loading-state orchestration**

**Verdict: Genuine but justified.**

Evidence: The function (lines 69-200 of `useAdjustedTaskDetails.ts`) does three things: (1) extracts `variantSourceTaskId` from variant params, (2) conditionally fetches the source task via `useQuery`, and (3) computes `adjustedTaskDetailsData` in a `useMemo` with complex priority logic (lines 113-194): check if variant is task-created, determine best param source (matching taskDetailsData > fetched source task > variant params), handle loading states with `waitingForInitialVariant` and `shouldShowLoading`. The loading-state orchestration (lines 178-194) is particularly tricky with its multi-condition checks. The claim of "3-level param resolution" maps to the three param sources (taskDetailsData.task.params, variantSourceTask.params, variantParams). This is complex but the complexity is inherent in the domain -- variants can come from different sources and the UI needs to show the right params. Splitting would likely just move the complexity without reducing it.

**[e564fa7b] SharedLightboxShotProps is a 16-field optional callback bag**

**Verdict: Genuine.**

Evidence: `SharedLightboxShotProps` (lines 34-50 of `types.ts`) has exactly **16 fields**, and **all but none are optional** (every field has `?`). The fields mix: IDs (`shotId`, `selectedShotId`), data (`allShots`), callbacks (`onShotChange`, `onAddToShot`, `onAddToShotWithoutPosition`, `onNavigateToShot`, `onShowTick`, `onShowSecondaryTick`, `onOptimisticPositioned`, `onOptimisticUnpositioned`), and state (`optimisticPositionedIds`, `optimisticUnpositionedIds`, `positionedInSelectedShot`, `associatedWithoutPositionInSelectedShot`). Having 16 optional fields means the type provides almost no compile-time guarantees about which combinations are valid. This is a genuine "optional callback bag" anti-pattern. However, the lightbox is used in many contexts (gallery, shot editor, standalone) where different subsets of shot functionality are available, so the optionality reflects real usage variance.

## Cross-Issue Contradictions

No direct contradictions found between issues. However, there is a thematic tension:

## naming_quality

**[84c27582] useMediaGalleryViewInteractions uses 'any' for 7+ params** -- **Genuine.** The `UseMediaGalleryViewInteractionsParams` interface at `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/components/MediaGallery/hooks/useMediaGalleryViewInteractions.ts` uses `any` in these typed params: `allShots: any[]`, `simplifiedShotOptions: any[]`, `navigateToShot: (...args: any[]) => void`, `actionsHook: any`, `filtersHook: any`, `stateHook: any`, `onCreateShot?: ((...args: any[]) => Promise<any>)`, `onAddToLastShot?: ((...args: any[]) => Promise<boolean>)`, `onAddToLastShotWithoutPosition?: ((...args: any[]) => Promise<boolean>)`, plus `onToggleStar`, `onApplySettings`, `onImageClick` all using `...args: any[]`. ### [1b6a55d0] useDeleteFromTable uses runtime table-name string branching inside a single mutation function
**Verdict: GENUINE, but borderline over-engineering to fix**

### [4cf87e91] useVideoEditPanelModel useMemo has 23 deep-path dependency entries

### incomplete_migration

**[2d2d9b9b] "Three deprecated invalidation aliases are defined and barrel-exported but have zero callers"**

**Verdict: Partially genuine, partially false positive.**

The three files in question are `useSettingsInvalidation.ts`, `useShotInvalidation.ts`, and `useTaskInvalidation.ts` in `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/hooks/invalidation/`. These are real files, they contain only type definitions (interfaces), and they have zero exports -- so they cannot be "barrel-exported." The barrel file (`index.ts`) does NOT export anything from them. They are dead code, but the issue description is inaccurate: they are not "aliases" and they are not "barrel-exported." They are orphaned type-only stubs with accompanying test files that don't actually test the stubs (the tests exercise `queryKeys` and `queryClient.invalidateQueries` directly). The test files are the real dead weight. **Genuine issue, but the description is misleading.**

**[3aa1991b] "Timeline time-utils.ts is a pure re-export shim with 9 callers that could import the canonical module directly"**

**[25c7e199] "Legacy primaryStructureVideo* fields and canonical structureVideos[] array coexist across 15+ files"**

**Verdict: Genuine, but nuanced.** Both `primaryStructureVideo` (derived type) and `structureVideos` (canonical array) are used extensively: `structureVideos` appears in 40 files (137 occurrences), and `primaryStructureVideo` is referenced in numerous UI components. However, `primaryStructureVideo` is intentionally derived from `structureVideos[0]` via `resolvePrimaryStructureVideo()` in `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/lib/tasks/travelBetweenImages/primaryStructureVideo.ts`. This is a deliberate convenience adapter, not legacy cruft -- the UI components need individual fields (path, metadata, treatment, motionStrength, etc.) rather than the array. The `@deprecated` markers are only on `legacyStructureVideo.ts` fields (structure_video_strength, etc.), not on `primaryStructureVideo`. The coexistence is by design, though there could be an argument for consolidation. **Genuine observation, but overstated severity -- this is architectural by design, not an incomplete migration.**

---

**[bbbd5ec8] "Six legacy migration hooks run on every ImageGenerationForm mount with no sunset plan"**

**Verdict: Genuine, but the "no sunset plan" claim is false.** The six migration hooks are real, called from `useLegacyMigrations()` at `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/components/ImageGenerationForm/hooks/useLegacyMigrations.ts`, which is invoked via `useProjectImageSettings` on form mount. However, there IS a sunset plan: the file has a comment `SUNSET: 2026-09-01` (line 17), and `legacyProjectImageSettings.ts` declares `removeBy: '2026-05-31'` with an enforcement function (`enforceLegacyProjectImageSettingsSunset`). The hooks DO run on every mount, which is accurate, but the "no sunset plan" claim is directly contradicted by the source code. **Genuine performance concern, false claim about missing sunset plan.**

---

### initialization_coupling

**[c6995c9b] "useToolSettings.ts registers global event listeners as module-level side effect on import"**

**Verdict: False positive.** Reading `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/hooks/settings/useToolSettings.ts`: the only module-level side effect is line 166: `setSettingsWriteFunction(rawUpdateToolSettings)`, which registers a write function with the settings write queue. This is NOT a global event listener -- it's a dependency injection pattern that sets a callback. There are no `addEventListener`, `window.on*`, or similar calls at module scope. The issue mischaracterizes a DI registration as "global event listeners."

---

**[f2ce7483] "projectSelectionStore.ts reads localStorage at module scope during evaluation"**

**Verdict: Genuine.** At `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/contexts/projectSelectionStore.ts`, line 27-29: `let snapshot: ProjectSelectionSnapshot = { selectedProjectId: readPersistedProjectSelection() }` runs at module evaluation time, and `readPersistedProjectSelection()` reads `window.localStorage.getItem(...)`. There is a guard (`typeof window === 'undefined'` check with try/catch), making it SSR-safe, but it does read localStorage at import time. **Genuine, though guarded.**

---

**[49914c90] "debugConfig.ts attaches debugConfig to window object at module scope"**

**Verdict: Genuine, but guarded.** At `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/lib/debug/debugConfig.ts`, lines 154-156: `if (import.meta.env.DEV && typeof window !== 'undefined') { window.debugConfig = debugConfig; }`. This IS a module-scope side effect that mutates the global `window` object, but it's guarded behind `import.meta.env.DEV` (dev-only) and `typeof window !== 'undefined'` (SSR-safe). The side effect is intentional for developer ergonomics. **Genuine, low severity -- dev-only and guarded.**

---

### dependency_health

**[575c4b57] "react-markdown + remark-gfm eagerly imported for single-use blog page, bundled in main chunk"**

**Verdict: Genuine.** In `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/app/routes.tsx`, line 20: `import BlogPostPage from '@/pages/Blog/BlogPostPage';` is a static/eager import. BlogPostPage is the only consumer of `react-markdown` and `remark-gfm` (confirmed: only 2 files reference `react-markdown`). Since BlogPostPage is NOT lazy-loaded, these two dependencies are included in the main bundle. Other secondary tool pages are lazy-loaded (lines 17-18), so blog pages are inconsistent with the pattern. **Genuine -- easy win to lazy-load BlogPostPage and BlogListPage.**

---

**[19a0de52] "@dnd-kit/core version specifier (^6.1.0) is below peer dependency minimum required by @dnd-kit/sortable (^6.3.0)"**

**Verdict: Genuine but low-risk at present.** `package.json` declares `@dnd-kit/core: "^6.1.0"` while `@dnd-kit/sortable@10.0.0` requires `@dnd-kit/core: "^6.3.0"` as a peer dependency. Currently `npm ls` shows `@dnd-kit/core@6.3.1` is installed (satisfying both), so there's no runtime issue today. However, the specifier `^6.1.0` would technically allow installing `6.1.x` or `6.2.x`, which would violate the peer dep. **Genuine version specifier mismatch -- should bump to `^6.3.0` for correctness.**

---

### logic_clarity

**[4d4fc630] "Math.min(params.fullMax, params.fullMax) is always params.fullMax -- redundant expression, likely copy-paste bug"**

**Verdict: Genuine.** At `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/tools/travel-between-images/components/Timeline/hooks/useTabletEndpointSelection.ts`, line 95: `let rightLimit = Math.min(params.fullMax, params.fullMax);`. This is redundant -- `Math.min(x, x)` always returns `x`. Comparing with the left side (line 94): `let leftLimit = Math.max(0, params.fullMin)` shows the expected pattern -- the right limit should likely be `Math.min(someUpperBound, params.fullMax)`. Looking at line 137: `newEnd = Math.min(params.fullMax, Math.max(...))` shows `fullMax` used correctly as an upper bound. The most likely intended code was `Math.min(params.fullRange, params.fullMax)` or similar -- this is indeed a copy-paste bug. **Genuine bug.**

   206→      });

   227→/**
   228→ * Apply pending clip actions to an existing clips array.
   229→ * Resolves each deferred action by filling the first available empty slot,
   230→ * or appending when no empty slots remain.
   231→ */
   232→export function applyPendingClipActions(
   233→  prevClips: VideoClip[],
   234→  actions: PendingClipAction[],
   235→): VideoClip[] {
   236→  let clips = [...prevClips];
   237→  // Track which indices have been filled by previous actions in this batch
   238→  const filledIndices = new Set<number>();
   239→
   240→  for (const action of actions) {
   241→    const emptyIndex = clips.findIndex(
   242→      (clip, idx) => !clip.url && !filledIndices.has(idx),
   243→    );
   244→
   245→    if (emptyIndex !== -1) {
   246→      clips = clips.map((clip, idx) =>
   247→        idx === emptyIndex
   248→          ? {
   249→              ...clip,
   250→              url: action.clip.url,
   251→              posterUrl: action.clip.posterUrl,
   252→              durationSeconds: action.clip.durationSeconds,
   253→              loaded: false,
   254→              playing: false,
   255→              generationId: action.clip.generationId,
   256→            }
   257→          : clip,
   258→      );
   259→      filledIndices.add(emptyIndex);
   260→    } else {
   261→      clips = [...clips, action.clip];
   262→    }
   263→  }
   264→
   265→  return clips;
   266→}

     def _organize_instructions() -> str:
         return """\
     ## ORGANIZE Stage Instructions
     
     Your task: create clusters that represent **practical work sessions** — changes that
     belong in the same PR because they touch the same files, the same area, or have the
     same blast radius.
     
     **DO NOT group by dimension or abstract theme.** "god-hooks" or "convention-cleanup" are
     categories, not plans. A good cluster = "I open these 3 files and make these changes."
     A bad cluster = "11 issues that are all about hooks being too big" (but touch 11 different files).
     
     **USE A SUBAGENT for this stage.** Launch a single subagent that:
     1. Collects all remaining issue file paths (each issue names its file)
     2. Finds which issues share files or directories (file proximity analysis)
     3. Groups by what makes sense to change together in one PR
     4. Names clusters after the area/files, not the problem type
     
     Example of GOOD clustering (by area):
     - `media-lightbox-hooks` — 4 issues all in src/domains/media-lightbox/hooks/
     - `timeline-cleanup` — 3 issues touching Timeline components + utils
     - `task-typing` — 5 issues all touching src/types/database.ts + src/shared/lib/taskParamsUtils.ts
     
     Example of BAD clustering (by theme):
     - `god-hooks-decomposition` — 11 issues in 11 unrelated files
     - `convention-cleanup` — 14 issues across the entire codebase
     - `bugs-and-quick-wins` — grab bag sorted by severity
     ...
     **Self-check before recording:**
     - If a cluster has issues from 5+ different directories with no file overlap, it's probably a
       theme-group, not a practical cluster. Split it by area.
     - If your step count ≈ issue count, you probably mapped 1:1 instead of planning. Consolidate
       steps that touch the same file.
     - If a cluster name describes a problem type ("abstraction-bloat", "error-handling") instead of
       a location or specific change, reconsider the grouping.
     ...
     """
     ```

     ```python
     def _clusters_with_directory_scatter(
         plan: dict, *, threshold: int = 5,
     ) -> list[tuple[str, int, list[str]]]:
         """Return clusters whose issues span too many unrelated directories.
         A cluster with issues in 5+ distinct top-level directories is likely
         grouped by theme/dimension rather than by file proximity.
         Returns (cluster_name, dir_count, sample_dirs)."""
         results: list[tuple[str, int, list[str]]] = []
         for name, cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).items():
             if cluster.get("auto") or not cluster.get("issue_ids"):
                 continue
             dirs: set[str] = set()
             for step in cluster.get("action_steps") or []:
                 if isinstance(step, dict) and step.get("detail"):
                     for path_str in _PATH_RE.findall(step["detail"]):
                         parts = path_str.split("/")
                         if len(parts) >= 3:
                             dirs.add("/".join(parts[:3]))
                         elif len(parts) >= 2:
                             dirs.add("/".join(parts[:2]))
             if len(dirs) >= threshold:
                 results.append((name, len(dirs), sorted(dirs)[:6]))
         return results

     def _clusters_with_high_step_ratio(
         plan: dict, *, max_ratio: float = 1.0,
     ) -> list[tuple[str, int, int, float]]:
         """Return clusters where step count >= issue count (1:1 mapping).
         Returns (cluster_name, steps, issues, ratio)."""
         results: list[tuple[str, int, int, float]] = []
         for name, cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).items():
             if cluster.get("auto") or not cluster.get("issue_ids"):
                 continue
             steps = len(cluster.get("action_steps") or [])
             issues = len(cluster.get("issue_ids") or [])
             if issues >= 3 and steps > 0:
                 ratio = steps / issues
                 if ratio > max_ratio:
                     results.append((name, steps, issues, ratio))
         return results
     ```

1→/**
     2→ * Shared Generation Data Transformers
     3→ * 
     4→ * SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for transforming generation data from database to UI format.
     5→ * 
     6→ * This eliminates the need to manually update transformation logic in multiple places
     7→ * when adding new fields. Instead, update once here and all consumers automatically
     8→ * get the new field.
     9→ * 
    10→ * Architecture Benefits:
    11→ * - DRY: No duplicated transformation logic across hooks/components
    12→ * - Type Safety: Centralized TypeScript types ensure consistency
    13→ * - Maintainability: Add new fields in one place instead of 5+
    14→ * - Testability: Can unit test transformations in isolation
    15→ * 
    16→ * NOTE: upscaled_url has been removed - upscaled versions are now stored as
    17→ * generation_variants with variant_type='upscaled' and become the primary variant,
    18→ * so `location` already contains the best available URL.
    19→ */
    20→
    21→import type { GeneratedImageWithMetadata } from '@/shared/components/MediaGallery/types';
    22→import type { GenerationRow } from '@/domains/generation/types';
    23→import type { GenerationMetadata } from '@/domains/generation/types';
    24→import { getSupabaseClient as supabase } from '@/integrations/supabase/client';
    25→import { stripQueryParameters } from '@/shared/lib/media/mediaUrl';
    26→import { TOOL_IDS, isToolId } from '@/shared/lib/toolIds';
    27→import { ServerError } from '@/shared/lib/errorHandling/errors';
    28→import { normalizeAndPresentError } from '@/shared/lib/errorHandling/runtimeError';
    29→import { expandShotData } from '@/shared/lib/shotData';
    30→import { parseGenerationTaskId } from '@/shared/lib/generationTaskIdParser';
    31→import { filterUuidStrings } from '@/shared/lib/uuid';
    32→import { asRecord, asString, firstString } from '@/shared/lib/jsonNarrowing';
    33→
    34→/**
    35→ * Result type for calculateDerivedCounts
    36→ */
    37→export interface DerivedCountsResult {
    38→  /** Count of variants/derivatives per generation */
    39→  derivedCounts: Record<string, number>;
    40→  /** Whether each generation has any unviewed variants (viewed_at IS NULL) */
    41→  hasUnviewedVariants: Record<string, boolean>;
    42→  /** Count of unviewed variants per generation */
    43→  unviewedVariantCounts: Record<string, number>;
    44→  /** True when counts were intentionally returned empty due to a read-path failure. */
    45→  degraded?: boolean;
    46→  /** Machine-readable reason for degraded fallback behavior. */
    47→  errorCode?: 'query_failed';
    48→}
    49→
    50→function createEmptyDerivedCountsResult(): DerivedCountsResult {
    51→  return {
    52→    derivedCounts: {},
    53→    hasUnviewedVariants: {},
    54→    unviewedVariantCounts: {},
    55→  };
    56→}
    57→
    58→/**
    59→ * Calculate derivedCount for generations (how many variants/derivatives exist)
    60→ * Also tracks whether any variants are unviewed (for NEW badge display)
    61→ *
    62→ * Queries both:
    63→ * - generations table (based_on relationships)
    64→ * - generation_variants table (edit variants)
    65→ *
    66→ * @param generationIds - Array of generation IDs to count variants for
    67→ * @returns Object with derivedCounts and hasUnviewedVariants maps
    68→ */
    69→async function calculateDerivedCounts(
    70→  generationIds: string[]
    71→): Promise<DerivedCountsResult> {
    72→  const persistedGenerationIds = filterUuidStrings(generationIds);
    73→  if (persistedGenerationIds.length === 0) {
    74→    return createEmptyDerivedCountsResult();
    75→  }
    76→
    77→  const { derivedCounts, hasUnviewedVariants, unviewedVariantCounts } = createEmptyDerivedCountsResult();
    78→
    79→  // Only count from generation_variants table (actual variants)
    80→  // Note: We intentionally don't count based_on generations here - those are
    81→  // separate images in the gallery, not variants of this image
    82→  const { data: variantCountsData, error: variantCountsError } = await supabase().from('generation_variants')
    83→    .select('generation_id, viewed_at')
    84→    .in('generation_id', persistedGenerationIds);
    85→
    86→  if (variantCountsError) {
    87→    throw new ServerError('Failed to load variant badge counts', {
    88→      context: { generationIdsCount: generationIds.length },
    89→      cause: variantCountsError,
    90→    });
    91→  }
    92→
    93→  if (variantCountsData) {
    94→    for (const item of variantCountsData as Array<{ generation_id: string; viewed_at: string | null }>) {
    95→      const genId = item.generation_id;
    96→      derivedCounts[genId] = (derivedCounts[genId] || 0) + 1;
    97→      if (item.viewed_at === null) {
    98→        hasUnviewedVariants[genId] = true;
    99→        unviewedVariantCounts[genId] = (unviewedVariantCounts[genId] || 0) + 1;
   100→      }
   101→    }
   102→  }
   103→
   104→  return { derivedCounts, hasUnviewedVariants, unviewedVariantCounts };
   105→}
   106→
   107→/**
   108→ * Fail-open variant of calculateDerivedCounts for non-critical UI surfaces.
   109→ * Keeps badge rendering resilient when counts query intermittently fails.
   110→ */
   111→export async function calculateDerivedCountsSafe(
   112→  generationIds: string[]
   113→): Promise<DerivedCountsResult> {
   114→  try {
   115→    return await calculateDerivedCounts(generationIds);
   116→  } catch (error) {
   117→    normalizeAndPresentError(error, { context: 'generationTransformers.calculateDerivedCountsSafe', showToast: false });
   118→    return {
   119→      ...createEmptyDerivedCountsResult(),
   120→      degraded: true,
   121→      errorCode: 'query_failed',
   122→    };
   123→  }
   124→}

   201→/**
   202→ * Extract prompt from various nested param structures
   203→ */
   204→function extractPrompt(params: Record<string, unknown> | null | undefined): string {
   205→  if (!params) return 'No prompt';
   206→
   207→  const originalParams = asRecord(params.originalParams);
   208→  const orchestratorDetails = asRecord(originalParams?.orchestrator_details);
   209→  const metadataBlock = asRecord(params.metadata);
   210→
   211→  return firstString(
   212→    orchestratorDetails?.prompt,
   213→    params.prompt,
   214→    metadataBlock?.prompt,
   215→  ) ?? 'No prompt';
   216→}
   217→
   218→/**
   219→ * Extract thumbnail URL with fallback logic
   220→ * Handles special case for travel-between-images videos where thumbnail might be in params
   221→ */
   222→function extractThumbnailUrl(item: RawGeneration, mainUrl: string): string {
   223→  // Start with database thumbnail_url field
   224→  let thumbnailUrl = item.thumbnail_url;
   225→  const toolType = item.params?.tool_type;
   226→  
   227→  // If no thumbnail in database, check params for travel-between-images videos
   228→  if (!thumbnailUrl && isToolId(toolType) && toolType === TOOL_IDS.TRAVEL_BETWEEN_IMAGES) {
   229→    const originalParams = asRecord(item.params?.originalParams);
   230→    const orchestratorDetails = asRecord(originalParams?.orchestrator_details);
   231→    const fullPayload = asRecord(item.params?.full_orchestrator_payload);
   232→    const originalFullPayload = asRecord(originalParams?.full_orchestrator_payload);
   233→
   234→    thumbnailUrl = firstString(
   235→      item.params?.thumbnailUrl,
   236→      orchestratorDetails?.thumbnail_url,
   237→      fullPayload?.thumbnail_url,
   238→      originalFullPayload?.thumbnail_url,
   239→    ) ?? undefined;
   240→  }
   241→  
   242→  // Final fallback to main URL
   243→  return thumbnailUrl || mainUrl;
   244→}
   245→
   246→/**
   247→ * Normalize timeline_frame to position (divide by 50)
   248→ */
   249→function normalizePosition(timelineFrame: number | null | undefined): number | null {
   250→  if (timelineFrame === null || timelineFrame === undefined) return null;
   251→  return Math.floor(timelineFrame / 50);
   252→}
   253→
   254→/**
   255→ * Transform a raw generation record from database to UI format
   256→ * 
   257→ * This is the MAIN transformation function used by most hooks/components
   258→ * 
   259→ * @param item - Raw generation from database query
   260→ * @param options - Optional customization (shot context, metadata, etc.)
   261→ * @returns Transformed generation ready for UI display
   262→ */
   263→export function transformGeneration(
   264→  item: RawGeneration,
   265→  options: TransformOptions = {}
   266→): GeneratedImageWithMetadata {
   267→  const mainUrl = item.location;
   268→  const thumbnailUrl = extractThumbnailUrl(item, mainUrl);
   269→  const taskIdParse = parseGenerationTaskId(item.tasks);
   270→  const taskId = taskIdParse.taskId;
   271→  const prompt = extractPrompt(item.params);
   272→  
   273→  // Extract content_type from params for proper download file extensions
   274→  // Stored as 'image' or 'video', convert to MIME type
   275→  const storedContentType = item.params?.content_type;
   276→  const isVideo = item.type?.includes('video') || storedContentType === 'video' || false;
   277→  let contentType: string | undefined;
   278→  if (storedContentType === 'video') {
   279→    // Default to mp4 for videos, can be overridden by URL extension
   280→    contentType = 'video/mp4';
   281→  } else if (storedContentType === 'image') {
   282→    // Default to png for images, can be overridden by URL extension  
   283→    contentType = 'image/png';
   284→  }
   285→  
   286→  // Compute stable URL identities for caching/comparison
   287→  // Supabase URLs have rotating tokens but the file path is stable
   288→  const urlIdentity = stripQueryParameters(mainUrl);
   289→  const thumbUrlIdentity = stripQueryParameters(thumbnailUrl);
   290→
   291→  // Base transformation - fields common to all generations
   292→  const baseItem: GeneratedImageWithMetadata = {
   293→    id: item.id,
   294→    url: mainUrl,
   295→    thumbUrl: thumbnailUrl,
   296→    urlIdentity,
   297→    thumbUrlIdentity,
   298→    prompt,
   299→    metadata: {
   300→      ...(item.params || {}),
   301→      taskId, // Include task ID in metadata for MediaGalleryItem
   302→      taskIdStatus: taskIdParse.status, // Surface parse health to avoid silent shape drift
   303→      based_on: item.based_on, // Include based_on for lineage tracking
   304→      ...(options.metadata || {}), // Merge any additional metadata
   305→    },
   306→    createdAt: item.created_at,
   307→    updatedAt: item.updated_at,
   308→    isVideo,
   309→    contentType, // For proper download file extensions
   310→    starred: item.starred || false,
   311→    based_on: item.based_on, // Top level for easy access
   312→    position: null, // Will be set if shot context provided
   313→    timeline_frame: null, // Will be set if shot context provided
   314→    name: item.name ?? asString(item.params?.name) ?? undefined,
   315→    derivedCount: item.derivedCount || 0, // Number of generations/variants based on this one
   316→    hasUnviewedVariants: item.hasUnviewedVariants || false, // For NEW badge display
   317→    unviewedVariantCount: item.unviewedVariantCount || 0, // Count for tooltip
   318→    // Parent/child relationship fields
   319→    is_child: item.is_child ?? undefined,
   320→    parent_generation_id: item.parent_generation_id ?? undefined,
   321→    child_order: item.child_order ?? undefined,
   322→  };
   323→
   324→  // Normalize JSONB shot_data into a flat association list.
   325→  const shotGenerations = expandShotData(asRecord(item.shot_data));
   326→  
   327→  // If shot context is provided via options, use it
   328→  if (options.shotImageEntryId || options.timeline_frame !== undefined) {
   329→    return {
   330→      ...baseItem,
   331→      shotImageEntryId: options.shotImageEntryId,
   332→      timeline_frame: options.timeline_frame ?? null,
   333→      position: normalizePosition(options.timeline_frame),
   334→    };
   335→  }
   336→
   337→  // Otherwise, process shot associations from query data
   338→  if (shotGenerations.length > 0) {
   339→    // Single shot optimization
   340→    if (shotGenerations.length === 1) {
   341→      const singleShot = shotGenerations[0];
   342→      return {
   343→        ...baseItem,
   344→        shot_id: singleShot.shot_id,
   345→        position: normalizePosition(singleShot.timeline_frame),
   346→        timeline_frame: singleShot.timeline_frame,
   347→      };
   348→    }
   349→    
   350→    // Multiple shots: include all associations
   351→    const allAssociations = shotGenerations.map(shotGen => ({
   352→      shot_id: shotGen.shot_id,
   353→      timeline_frame: shotGen.timeline_frame,
   354→      position: normalizePosition(shotGen.timeline_frame),
   355→    }));
   356→    
   357→    // When filtering by specific shot, use that shot as primary
   358→    let primaryShot = shotGenerations[0];
   359→    if (options.shotId) {
   360→      const matchingShot = shotGenerations.find(shotGen => shotGen.shot_id === options.shotId);
   361→      if (matchingShot) {
   362→        primaryShot = matchingShot;
   363→      }
   364→    }
   365→
   366→    return {
   367→      ...baseItem,
   368→      shot_id: primaryShot.shot_id,
   369→      position: normalizePosition(primaryShot.timeline_frame),
   370→      timeline_frame: primaryShot.timeline_frame,
   371→      all_shot_associations: allAssociations,
   372→    };
   373→  }
   374→  
   375→  return baseItem;
   376→}

   378→/**
   379→ * Transform for Timeline component's specific needs
   380→ * Maps to GenerationRow format expected by Timeline
   381→ */
   382→export function transformForTimeline(
   383→  shotGen: RawShotGeneration
   384→): GenerationRow & { timeline_frame?: number } {
   385→  const gen = shotGen.generation || shotGen.generations;
   386→  const genData = Array.isArray(gen) ? gen[0] : gen;
   387→  
   388→  if (!genData) {
   389→    return {
   390→      // PRIMARY IDs: id = shot_generations.id (unique per entry), generation_id = actual generation
   391→      id: shotGen.id,
   392→      generation_id: shotGen.generation_id,
   393→      // Deprecated (backwards compat)
   394→      shotImageEntryId: shotGen.id,
   395→      timeline_frame: shotGen.timeline_frame ?? undefined,
   396→    };
   397→  }
   398→  
   399→  return {
   400→    // PRIMARY IDs: id = shot_generations.id (unique per entry), generation_id = actual generation
   401→    id: shotGen.id,
   402→    generation_id: shotGen.generation_id,
   403→    // Deprecated (backwards compat)
   404→    shotImageEntryId: shotGen.id,
   405→    imageUrl: genData.location,
   406→    thumbUrl: genData.location,
   407→    location: genData.location,
   408→    type: genData.type ?? undefined,
   409→    createdAt: genData.created_at,
   410→    timeline_frame: shotGen.timeline_frame ?? undefined,
   411→    metadata: (asRecord(shotGen.metadata) as GenerationMetadata | null) ?? undefined,
   412→    starred: genData.starred ?? false,
   413→    based_on: genData.based_on ?? undefined,
   414→    derivedCount: genData.derivedCount ?? 0,
   415→  };
   416→}
