   418→/**
   419→ * Detect if a URL points to a video based on file extension.
   420→ * Used for variants which lack a `type` column.
   421→ */
   422→function isVideoUrl(url: string | null | undefined): boolean {
   423→  if (!url) return false;
   424→  const videoExtensions = ['.mp4', '.webm', '.mov', '.avi', '.mkv'];
   425→  return videoExtensions.some(ext => url.toLowerCase().includes(ext));
   426→}
   427→
   428→/**
   429→ * Transform a raw variant record from generation_variants table to UI format.
   430→ *
   431→ * Mirrors `transformGeneration` but for variants, which have a different
   432→ * schema (no `type` column, different metadata shape).
   433→ *
   434→ * @param variant - Raw variant from database query
   435→ * @param options - Optional overrides (e.g. toolType fallback)
   436→ * @returns Transformed variant ready for UI display
   437→ */
   438→export function transformVariant(
   439→  variant: RawVariant,
   440→  options?: { toolType?: string }
   441→): GeneratedImageWithMetadata {
   442→  const isVideo = isVideoUrl(variant.location);
   443→  const variantParams = asRecord(variant.params) ?? {};
   444→  const storedContentType = asString(variantParams.content_type) ?? undefined;
   445→
   446→  let contentType: string | undefined;
   447→  if (storedContentType === 'video' || isVideo) {
   448→    contentType = 'video/mp4';
   449→  } else {
   450→    contentType = 'image/png';
   451→  }
   452→
   453→  return {
   454→    id: variant.id,
   455→    url: variant.location,
   456→    thumbUrl: variant.thumbnail_url || variant.location,
   457→    isVideo,
   458→    contentType,
   459→    createdAt: variant.created_at,

    19→export function parseTaskParams(params: string | Record<string, unknown> | null | undefined): Record<string, unknown> {

   116→export function derivePrompt(parsedParams: Record<string, unknown>): string | null {
   117→  const params = parsedParams;
   118→  if (isTravelTaskParams(params)) {

   122→  const orchestratorDetails = asRecord(params.orchestrator_details);

   138→      segmentIndex === null ? undefined : enhancedFromOrchestratorPayload?.[segmentIndex],

   140→    if (enhancedPrompt) return enhancedPrompt;

   148→        orchestratorDetails?.base_prompt,
   149→      ) ?? null
   150→    );
   151→  }
   152→
   153→  // For full timeline/orchestrated tasks
   154→  // The global base_prompt is what the user typed in the prompt field.
   155→  // Per-pair overrides (base_prompts_expanded) are segment-specific and shouldn't
   156→  // be shown as the task-level prompt — they're misleading when the user explicitly
   157→  // cleared the global prompt.
   158→  const enhancedFromOrchestratorDetails = asStringArray(orchestratorDetails?.enhanced_prompts_expanded);
   159→  const enhancedFromOrchestratorPayload = asStringArray(orchestratorPayload?.enhanced_prompts_expanded);
   160→  return (
   161→    pickFirstString(
   162→      orchestratorDetails?.base_prompt,
   163→      orchestratorPayload?.base_prompt,
   164→      params.base_prompt,
   165→      params.prompt,

   167→      // which are per-pair overrides, not task-level prompts.
   168→      enhancedFromOrchestratorDetails?.[0],

   207→interface LoraInfo {

   209→  strength: number;
   210→  displayName: string;

   212→
   213→/**
   214→ * Extract LoRAs from task params (checks multiple locations)
   215→ */
   216→export function extractLoras(parsedParams: Record<string, unknown>): LoraInfo[] {
   217→  const params = parsedParams;
   218→  const orchestratorDetails = asRecord(params.orchestrator_details);
   219→  const orchestratorPayload = asRecord(params.full_orchestrator_payload);
   220→
   221→  // Check for array format (image edit tasks use this)
   222→  const lorasArray = params.loras || orchestratorDetails?.loras || orchestratorPayload?.loras;
   223→  if (Array.isArray(lorasArray) && lorasArray.length > 0) {
   224→    return lorasArray
   225→      .map((lora): LoraInfo | null => {
   226→        const loraRecord = asRecord(lora);
   227→        if (!loraRecord) return null;
   228→        const url = asString(loraRecord.url) ?? '';
   229→        const parsedStrength = toFiniteNumber(loraRecord.strength) ?? toFiniteNumber(loraRecord.multiplier) ?? 1;
   230→        return {
   231→          url,
   232→          strength: parsedStrength,
   233→          displayName: extractLoraDisplayName(url),
   234→        };
   235→      })
   236→      .filter((lora): lora is LoraInfo => lora !== null);
   237→  }
   238→
   239→  // Check for object format (video tasks use additional_loras)
   240→  const additionalLoras = params.additional_loras || orchestratorDetails?.additional_loras || orchestratorPayload?.additional_loras;
   241→  if (additionalLoras && typeof additionalLoras === 'object' && Object.keys(additionalLoras as Record<string, unknown>).length > 0) {
   242→    return Object.entries(additionalLoras as Record<string, unknown>).map(([url, strength]) => ({
   243→      url,
   244→      strength: toFiniteNumber(strength) ?? 1,
   245→      displayName: extractLoraDisplayName(url),
   246→    }));
   247→  }
   248→
   249→  return [];
   250→}
   251→
   252→function extractLoraDisplayName(url: string): string {
   253→  const fileName = url.split('/').pop() || 'Unknown';
   254→  return fileName.replace(/\.(safetensors|ckpt|pt)$/i, '').replace(/_/g, ' ');
   255→}

   257→const TRAVEL_SEGMENT_IMAGE_SOURCE_ORDER: TravelPayloadSource[] = [
   258→  'individualSegmentParams',
   259→  'taskViewContract',
   260→  'familyContract',
   261→  'rawParams',
   262→];
   263→
   264→const TRAVEL_TIMELINE_IMAGE_SOURCE_ORDER: TravelPayloadSource[] = [

   268→  'fullOrchestratorPayload',

   272→const TRAVEL_PROMPT_SOURCE_ORDER: TravelPayloadSource[] = [

   276→  'orchestratorDetails',
   277→  'fullOrchestratorPayload',
   278→  'rawParams',

   281→function dedupeTruthyStrings(values: Array<string | undefined>): string[] {
   282→  return Array.from(new Set(values.filter((value): value is string => typeof value === 'string' && value.length > 0)));
   283→}
   284→
   285→function isTravelTaskParams(params: Record<string, unknown>): boolean {
   286→  const familyContract = asRecord(params.task_family_contract);
   287→  return (
   288→    params.task_family === 'travel_between_images'
   289→    || familyContract?.task_family === 'travel_between_images'
   290→    || params.orchestrator_details !== undefined
   291→    || params.full_orchestrator_payload !== undefined
   292→    || params.individual_segment_params !== undefined
   293→    || Array.isArray(params.image_urls)
   294→    || Array.isArray(params.input_image_paths_resolved)
   295→  );
   296→}
   297→
   298→function deriveTravelInputImages(params: Record<string, unknown>): string[] {
   299→  const snapshot = buildTaskPayloadSnapshot(params);
   300→  const reader = createTravelPayloadReader(snapshot);
   301→  const isSegmentTask = params.segment_index !== undefined;
   302→
   303→  if (isSegmentTask) {
   304→    const segmentInputImages = reader.pickStringArray('input_image_paths_resolved', TRAVEL_SEGMENT_IMAGE_SOURCE_ORDER);
   305→    if (segmentInputImages && segmentInputImages.length > 0) {
   306→      return dedupeTruthyStrings(segmentInputImages);
   307→    }
   308→
   309→    const startImage = reader.pickString('start_image_url', TRAVEL_SEGMENT_IMAGE_SOURCE_ORDER);
   310→    const endImage = reader.pickString('end_image_url', TRAVEL_SEGMENT_IMAGE_SOURCE_ORDER);
   311→    return dedupeTruthyStrings([startImage, endImage]);
   312→  }
   313→
   314→  const timelineSources = [
   315→    reader.pickStringArray('input_images', TRAVEL_TIMELINE_IMAGE_SOURCE_ORDER),
   316→    reader.pickStringArray('input_image_paths_resolved', TRAVEL_TIMELINE_IMAGE_SOURCE_ORDER),
   317→    reader.pickStringArray('image_urls', TRAVEL_TIMELINE_IMAGE_SOURCE_ORDER),
   318→  ];
   319→  for (const candidate of timelineSources) {
   320→    if (candidate && candidate.length > 0) {
   321→      return dedupeTruthyStrings(candidate);
   322→    }
   323→  }
   324→
   325→  return [];
   326→}

   328→function deriveTravelPrompt(params: Record<string, unknown>): string | null {
   329→  const snapshot = buildTaskPayloadSnapshot(params);
   330→  const reader = createTravelPayloadReader(snapshot);
   331→  const segmentIndex = toIntegerOrNull(params.segment_index);
   332→  const isSegmentTask = params.segment_index !== undefined;
   333→
   334→  if (isSegmentTask) {
   335→    const enhancedPromptsExpanded = reader.pickStringArray('enhanced_prompts_expanded', [
   336→      'orchestratorDetails',
   337→      'fullOrchestratorPayload',
   338→      'rawParams',
   339→    ]);
   340→    const enhancedPrompt = pickFirstString(
   341→      reader.pickString('enhanced_prompt', TRAVEL_PROMPT_SOURCE_ORDER),
   342→      segmentIndex === null ? undefined : enhancedPromptsExpanded?.[segmentIndex],
   343→    );
   344→    if (enhancedPrompt) {
   345→      return enhancedPrompt;
   346→    }
   347→
   348→    return (
   349→      pickFirstString(
   350→        reader.pickString('prompt', TRAVEL_PROMPT_SOURCE_ORDER),
   351→        reader.pickString('base_prompt', TRAVEL_PROMPT_SOURCE_ORDER),
   352→      ) ?? null
   353→    );
   354→  }
   355→
   356→  return (
   357→    pickFirstString(
   358→      reader.pickString('prompt', TRAVEL_PROMPT_SOURCE_ORDER),
   359→      reader.pickString('base_prompt', TRAVEL_PROMPT_SOURCE_ORDER),
   360→      reader.pickString('enhanced_prompt', TRAVEL_PROMPT_SOURCE_ORDER),
   361→    ) ?? null
   362→  );
   363→}

   365→function toIntegerOrNull(value: unknown): number | null {
   366→  const numeric = toFiniteNumber(value);
   367→  if (numeric === null || !Number.isInteger(numeric)) return null;
   368→  return numeric;
   369→}

   374→}

    21→function useManagedTimeouts() {

1→/**
     2→ * useAdjustedTaskDetails - Fetches variant source task and computes adjusted task details
     3→ *
     4→ * For variants created by tasks, shows the variant's source task params
     5→ * instead of the original generation's task. Preserves onApplySettingsFromTask.

     7→
     8→import { useMemo } from 'react';

    17→import type { TaskDetailsData } from '../types';
    18→import type { Task } from '@/types/tasks';
    19→
    20→// Helper to derive input images from task params
    21→function deriveInputImages(params: Record<string, unknown>): string[] {
    22→  const images: string[] = [];
    23→
    24→  // Check various param locations for input images
    25→  const orchestratorDetails = params.orchestrator_details as Record<string, unknown> | undefined;
    26→
    27→  // Direct input_images array
    28→  if (Array.isArray(params.input_images)) {
    29→    images.push(...params.input_images.filter((img): img is string => typeof img === 'string'));
    30→  }
    31→
    32→  // Orchestrator details input_images
    33→  if (orchestratorDetails && Array.isArray(orchestratorDetails.input_images)) {
    34→    images.push(...orchestratorDetails.input_images.filter((img): img is string => typeof img === 'string'));
    35→  }
    36→
    37→  // Start/end image URLs
    38→  if (typeof params.start_image_url === 'string') images.push(params.start_image_url);
    39→  if (typeof params.end_image_url === 'string') images.push(params.end_image_url);
    40→
    41→  // Orchestrator start/end
    42→  if (orchestratorDetails) {
    43→    if (typeof orchestratorDetails.start_image_url === 'string') images.push(orchestratorDetails.start_image_url);
    44→    if (typeof orchestratorDetails.end_image_url === 'string') images.push(orchestratorDetails.end_image_url);
    45→  }
    46→
    47→  return [...new Set(images)]; // Dedupe
    48→}
    49→
    50→interface UseAdjustedTaskDetailsProps {
    51→  projectId?: string | null;
    52→  activeVariant: {
    53→    id: string;
    54→    params?: Record<string, unknown> | null;
    55→    variant_type?: string | null;
    56→    created_at?: string;
    57→    is_primary?: boolean | null;
    58→  } | null;
    59→  taskDetailsData: TaskDetailsData | undefined;
    60→  isLoadingVariants: boolean;
    61→  initialVariantId: string | undefined;
    62→}
    63→
    64→interface UseAdjustedTaskDetailsReturn {
    65→  adjustedTaskDetailsData: TaskDetailsData | undefined;
    66→  isLoadingVariantTask: boolean;
    67→}
    68→
    69→export function useAdjustedTaskDetails({
    70→  projectId,
    71→  activeVariant,
    72→  taskDetailsData,
    73→  isLoadingVariants,
    74→  initialVariantId,
    75→}: UseAdjustedTaskDetailsProps): UseAdjustedTaskDetailsReturn {
    76→  // Extract source_task_id and check if variant already has orchestrator_details
    77→  const { variantSourceTaskId, variantHasOrchestratorDetails } = useMemo(() => {
    78→    const variantParams = activeVariant?.params as Record<string, unknown> | undefined;
    79→    return {
    80→      variantSourceTaskId: getSourceTaskIdLegacyCompatible(variantParams),
    81→      variantHasOrchestratorDetails: hasOrchestratorDetails(variantParams),
    82→    };
    83→  }, [activeVariant?.params]);
    84→
    85→  // Fetch the variant's source task when it differs from taskDetailsData
    86→  // Skip fetch if variant already has orchestrator_details (e.g., clip_join variants)
    87→  // NOTE: Uses ['tasks', 'single', taskId] query key to share cache with usePrefetchTaskData
    88→  const { data: variantSourceTask, isLoading: isLoadingVariantTask } = useQuery({
    89→    [REDACTED](variantSourceTaskId ?? '', projectId ?? null),
    90→    queryFn: async () => {
    91→      if (!variantSourceTaskId || !projectId) return null;
    92→      const { data, error } = await supabase().from('tasks')
    93→        .select('*')
    94→        .eq('id', variantSourceTaskId)
    95→        .eq('project_id', projectId)
    96→        .single();
    97→      if (error) {
    98→        console.error('[VariantTaskDetails] Error fetching source task:', error);
    99→        return null;
   100→      }
   101→      return data;
   102→    },
   103→    // Don't fetch if: no task ID, already have matching taskDetailsData, or variant has orchestrator_details
   104→    enabled: !!variantSourceTaskId
   105→      && !!projectId
   106→      && variantSourceTaskId !== taskDetailsData?.taskId
   107→      && !variantHasOrchestratorDetails,
   108→    staleTime: Infinity, // Task data is immutable - cache forever (matches prefetch)
   109→  });
   110→
   111→  // For variants, show the variant's source task params instead of the original task
   112→  // But ALWAYS preserve onApplySettingsFromTask so the Apply button shows
   113→  const adjustedTaskDetailsData = useMemo(() => {
   114→    // Check if we're viewing a variant that was created by a task (has source_task_id in params)
   115→    const variantParams = activeVariant?.params as Record<string, unknown> | undefined;
   116→    const isTaskCreatedVariant = activeVariant && variantParams && (
   117→      variantParams.source_task_id ||
   118→      variantParams.created_from ||
   119→      (activeVariant.variant_type && activeVariant.variant_type !== VARIANT_TYPE.ORIGINAL)
   120→    );
   121→
   122→    if (isTaskCreatedVariant && variantParams) {
   123→      // Check if taskDetailsData already has the correct task (e.g., when opened from TasksPane)
   124→      const sourceTaskId = typeof variantParams.source_task_id === 'string' ? variantParams.source_task_id : undefined;
   125→      const hasMatchingTaskData = taskDetailsData?.taskId === sourceTaskId && taskDetailsData?.task?.params;
   126→
   127→      // Determine the best source of task params:
   128→      // 1. If taskDetailsData matches, use its params (already have full data)
   129→      // 2. If we fetched the source task, use its params
   130→      // 3. Fall back to variant params (may be incomplete)
   131→      // IMPORTANT: Use variant_type for display (e.g., 'clip_join'), NOT tool_type
   132→      // tool_type is the tool that launched the task (e.g., 'travel-between-images'),
   133→      // which is different from what kind of variant this is
   134→      let effectiveParams = variantParams;
   135→      const effectiveTaskType = activeVariant.variant_type || 'variant';
   136→
   137→      if (hasMatchingTaskData) {
   138→        effectiveParams = (taskDetailsData.task?.params ?? variantParams) as Record<string, unknown>;
   139→      } else if (!variantParams.orchestrator_details && variantSourceTask?.params) {
   140→        // Only use fetched task params if variant doesn't already have orchestrator_details
   141→        // clip_join variants store orchestrator_details directly, so we don't want to overwrite
   142→        try {
   143→          effectiveParams = typeof variantSourceTask.params === 'string'
   144→            ? JSON.parse(variantSourceTask.params)
   145→            : variantSourceTask.params;
   146→        } catch {
   147→          // Keep variantParams as fallback on parse failure
   148→        }
   149→      }
   150→      // Otherwise keep variantParams which may already have orchestrator_details (e.g., clip_join)
   151→
   152→      // Extract input images using shared utility
   153→      // This handles segment tasks (only segment images) vs full timeline tasks
   154→      const variantInputImages = deriveInputImages(effectiveParams);
   155→
   156→      return {
   157→        task: {
   158→          id: activeVariant.id,
   159→          taskType: effectiveTaskType,
   160→          params: effectiveParams,
   161→          status: 'Complete' as Task['status'],
   162→          createdAt: activeVariant.created_at || new Date().toISOString(),
   163→          projectId: '',
   164→        } as Task,
   165→        isLoading: isLoadingVariantTask,
   166→        error: null,
   167→        inputImages: variantInputImages,
   168→        taskId: sourceTaskId ?? activeVariant.id,
   169→        // ALWAYS preserve onApplySettingsFromTask so Apply button shows for all variants
   170→        onApplySettingsFromTask: taskDetailsData?.onApplySettingsFromTask,
   171→      };
   172→    }
   173→
   174→    // If variants are still loading AND we don't have task data yet, show loading
   175→    // But if we already have task data cached, show it immediately rather than blocking on variants
   176→    // This provides better UX when task data is prefetched/cached
   177→    // ALSO check if we're waiting for initialVariantId to be applied (clicked a specific variant)
   178→    const waitingForInitialVariant = initialVariantId &&
   179→      (!activeVariant || activeVariant.id !== initialVariantId);
   180→
   181→    // Only override to loading if:
   182→    // 1. Waiting for a specific variant (user clicked a variant)
   183→    // 2. Variants loading AND no active variant AND task details still loading
   184→    //    (If task details finished - either has task or knows there's none - don't block on variants)
   185→    const shouldShowLoading = waitingForInitialVariant ||
   186→      (isLoadingVariants && !activeVariant && taskDetailsData?.isLoading);
   187→
   188→    if (shouldShowLoading) {
   189→      return taskDetailsData ? { ...taskDetailsData, isLoading: true } : taskDetailsData;
   190→    }
   191→
   192→    // For all other cases, use the generation's task details as-is
   193→    return taskDetailsData;
   194→  }, [taskDetailsData, activeVariant, variantSourceTask, isLoadingVariantTask, isLoadingVariants, initialVariantId]);
   195→
   196→  return {
   197→    adjustedTaskDetailsData,
   198→    isLoadingVariantTask,
   199→  };
   200→}
   201→

    18→const PENDING_CLIPS_TTL_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000;
    19→
    20→interface PendingJoinClipParseResult {
    21→  entries: PendingJoinClipEntry[];
    22→  invalidCount: number;
    23→}
    24→
    25→function parsePendingJoinClips(raw: string): PendingJoinClipParseResult | null {
    26→  let parsed: unknown;
    27→  try {
    28→    parsed = JSON.parse(raw);
    29→  } catch {
    30→    return null;
    31→  }
    32→
    33→  if (!Array.isArray(parsed)) {
    34→    return null;
    35→  }
    36→
    37→  const entries: PendingJoinClipEntry[] = [];
    38→  let invalidCount = 0;
    39→  for (const value of parsed) {
    40→    if (!value || typeof value !== 'object' || Array.isArray(value)) {
    41→      invalidCount += 1;
    42→      continue;
    43→    }
    44→
    45→    const candidate = value as Record<string, unknown>;
    46→    if (
    47→      typeof candidate.videoUrl !== 'string'
    48→      || typeof candidate.generationId !== 'string'
    49→      || typeof candidate.timestamp !== 'number'
    50→      || !Number.isFinite(candidate.timestamp)
    51→    ) {
    52→      invalidCount += 1;
    53→      continue;
    54→    }
    55→
    56→    entries.push({
    57→      videoUrl: candidate.videoUrl,
    58→      generationId: candidate.generationId,
    59→      timestamp: candidate.timestamp,
    60→      ...(typeof candidate.thumbnailUrl === 'string' && candidate.thumbnailUrl.length > 0
    61→        ? { thumbnailUrl: candidate.thumbnailUrl }
    62→        : {}),
    63→      ...(typeof candidate.projectId === 'string' && candidate.projectId.length > 0
    64→        ? { projectId: candidate.projectId }
    65→        : {}),
    66→      ...(typeof candidate.userId === 'string' && candidate.userId.length > 0
    67→        ? { userId: candidate.userId }
    68→        : {}),
    69→    });
    70→  }
    71→
    72→  return { entries, invalidCount };
    73→}
    74→
    75→/** Create a throwaway <video> to read duration from a URL. */
    76→function getVideoDurationFromUrl(videoUrl: string): Promise<number> {
    77→  return new Promise<number>(resolve => {
    78→    const videoElement = document.createElement('video');
    79→    videoElement.preload = 'metadata';
    80→    videoElement.onloadedmetadata = () => resolve(videoElement.duration);
    81→    videoElement.onerror = () => resolve(0);
    82→    videoElement.src = videoUrl;
    83→  });
    84→}
    85→
    86→/**
    87→ * Reads and consumes pending join clips from localStorage.
    88→ * Returns deferred actions that are applied to clip state later.
    89→ * Placement is intentionally not resolved here because only the consumer has
    90→ * the previous clip array needed to choose fill-vs-append.
    91→ */
    92→export type PendingClipAction = {
    93→  type: 'deferred_insert';
    94→  clip: VideoClip;

    96→
    97→interface ConsumePendingJoinClipsOptions {
    98→  projectId?: string | null;
    99→  readVideoDuration?: (videoUrl: string) => Promise<number>;
   100→}
   101→
   102→async function toPendingClipActions(
   103→  entries: PendingJoinClipEntry[],
   104→  readVideoDuration: (videoUrl: string) => Promise<number>,
   105→): Promise<PendingClipAction[]> {
   106→  const actions: PendingClipAction[] = [];
   107→
   108→  for (const { videoUrl, thumbnailUrl, generationId } of entries) {
   109→    if (!videoUrl) continue;
   110→
   111→    const durationSeconds = await readVideoDuration(videoUrl);
   112→
   113→    const clip: VideoClip = {
   114→      id: generateUUID(),
   115→      url: videoUrl,
   116→      posterUrl: thumbnailUrl,
   117→      durationSeconds,
   118→      loaded: false,
   119→      playing: false,
   120→      generationId,
   121→    };
   122→
   123→    actions.push({ type: 'deferred_insert', clip });
   124→  }
   125→
   126→  return actions;
   127→}
   128→
   129→export async function consumePendingJoinClips(
   130→  options: ConsumePendingJoinClipsOptions = {},
   131→): Promise<OperationResult<PendingClipAction[]>> {
   132→  const projectId = options.projectId ?? null;

   140→      const now = Date.now();
   141→      const scopedRecentClips = inMemoryPending.filter(
   142→        (clip) =>
   143→          now - clip.timestamp < PENDING_CLIPS_TTL_MS
   144→          && isPendingJoinClipInScope(clip, { projectId, userId }),
   145→      );
   146→      if (scopedRecentClips.length === 0) {
   147→        localStorage.removeItem(getPendingJoinClipsStorageKey(projectId, userId));
   148→        return operationSuccess([]);
   149→      }
   150→
   151→      const actions = await toPendingClipActions(scopedRecentClips, readVideoDuration);
   152→      localStorage.removeItem(getPendingJoinClipsStorageKey(projectId, userId));
   153→      return operationSuccess(actions);
   154→    }
   155→
   156→    const pendingKeys = getPendingJoinClipsCandidateKeys({ projectId, userId });
   157→    const pendingSource = pendingKeys
   158→      .map((key) => ({ key, raw: localStorage.getItem(key) }))
   159→      .find((item) => typeof item.raw === 'string' && item.raw.length > 0);
   160→
   161→    if (!pendingSource || !pendingSource.raw) {
   162→      return operationSuccess([]);
   163→    }
   164→
   165→    const parsedPendingClips = parsePendingJoinClips(pendingSource.raw);
   166→    if (!parsedPendingClips) {
   167→      normalizeAndPresentError(new Error('Invalid pending join clips payload'), {
   168→        context: 'JoinClipsPage.pendingClipsInvalid',
   169→        showToast: false,
   170→        logData: { [REDACTED] },
   171→      });
   172→      localStorage.removeItem(pendingSource.key);
   173→      return operationFailure(new Error('Invalid pending join clips payload'), {
   174→        policy: 'degrade',
   175→        errorCode: 'pending_join_clips_invalid_payload',
   176→        message: 'Invalid pending join clips payload',
   177→        recoverable: true,

   180→    }
   181→
   182→    if (parsedPendingClips.invalidCount > 0) {

   184→        context: 'JoinClipsPage.pendingClipsPartialRecovery',
   185→        showToast: false,

   194→    const now = Date.now();

   211→    localStorage.removeItem(pendingSource.key);

   213→      ...(parsedPendingClips.invalidCount > 0 ? { policy: 'degrade' } : {}),
   214→    });
   215→  } catch (error) {
   216→    normalizeAndPresentError(error, { context: 'JoinClipsPage', showToast: false });
   217→    return operationFailure(error, {
   218→      policy: 'degrade',
   219→      errorCode: 'pending_join_clips_read_failed',
   220→      message: 'Failed to consume pending join clips',
   221→      recoverable: true,
   222→      cause: error,
   223→    });
   224→  }
   225→}
   226→
   227→/**
   228→ * Apply pending clip actions to an existing clips array.
   229→ * Resolves each deferred action by filling the first available empty slot,
   230→ * or appending when no empty slots remain.
   231→ */
   232→export function applyPendingClipActions(
   233→  prevClips: VideoClip[],
   234→  actions: PendingClipAction[],
   235→): VideoClip[] {
   236→  let clips = [...prevClips];
   237→  // Track which indices have been filled by previous actions in this batch
   238→  const filledIndices = new Set<number>();
   239→
   240→  for (const action of actions) {
   241→    const emptyIndex = clips.findIndex(
   242→      (clip, idx) => !clip.url && !filledIndices.has(idx),
   243→    );
   244→
   245→    if (emptyIndex !== -1) {
   246→      clips = clips.map((clip, idx) =>
   247→        idx === emptyIndex
   248→          ? {
   249→              ...clip,
   250→              url: action.clip.url,
   251→              posterUrl: action.clip.posterUrl,
   252→              durationSeconds: action.clip.durationSeconds,
   253→              loaded: false,
   254→              playing: false,
   255→              generationId: action.clip.generationId,
   256→            }
   257→          : clip,
   258→      );
   259→      filledIndices.add(emptyIndex);
   260→    } else {
   261→      clips = [...clips, action.clip];
   262→    }
   263→  }
   264→
   265→  return clips;
   266→}
   267→

    29→function sanitizeTaskDataForSharing(taskData: Record<string, unknown> | null): Record<string, unknown> | null {

    31→  
    32→  const sanitized = { ...taskData };
    33→
    34→  const redactDeep = (value: unknown, depth: number = 0): unknown => {
    35→    if (depth > 6) return null;
    36→    if (value == null) return value;
    37→    if (Array.isArray(value)) return value.map((v) => redactDeep(v, depth + 1));
    38→    if (typeof value !== 'object') return value;
    39→
    40→    const out: Record<string, unknown> = {};
    41→    for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(value)) {
    42→      // Strip any obviously sensitive keys
    43→      if (/(api[_-]?key|token|secret|password|service_role|authorization|stripe)/i.test(k)) {
    44→        continue;
    45→      }
    46→      out[k] = redactDeep(v, depth + 1);
    47→    }
    48→    return out;
    49→  };
    50→  
    51→  // Remove or sanitize sensitive fields from params
    52→  if (sanitized.params) {
    53→    sanitized.params = redactDeep(sanitized.params);

   255→    const { data: newShare, error: insertError } = await supabase().from('shared_generations')
   256→      .insert(sharedGenerationInsert)
   257→      .select('share_slug')
   258→      .single();
   259→
   260→    if (!insertError && newShare) {
   261→      return newShare.share_slug;
   262→    }
   263→
   264→    if (isUniqueViolationError(insertError)) {
   265→      attempts++;
   266→      continue;
   267→    }
   268→
   269→    if (insertError) {
   270→      throw insertError;
   271→    }
   272→  }
   273→
   274→  return null;
   275→}
   276→
   277→interface CopyShareLinkAndNotifyArgs {
   278→  slug: string;
   279→  successTitle: string;
   280→  successDescription: string;
   281→  fallbackTitle: string;
   282→  fallbackDescription: string;
   283→  setShareCopied: React.Dispatch<React.SetStateAction<boolean>>;
   284→}
   285→
   286→async function copyShareLinkAndNotify({
   287→  slug,
   288→  successTitle,
   289→  successDescription,
   290→  fallbackTitle,
   291→  fallbackDescription,
   292→  setShareCopied,
   293→}: CopyShareLinkAndNotifyArgs): Promise<void> {
   294→  const copied = await copyToClipboardWithFallback(buildShareUrl(slug));
   295→  if (copied) {
   296→    markShareCopied(setShareCopied);
   297→    toast({ title: successTitle, description: successDescription });
   298→    return;
   299→  }
   300→
   301→  toast({ title: fallbackTitle, description: fallbackDescription });
   302→}
   303→
   304→/**
   305→ * Hook to handle sharing of generations via unique slug
   306→ *
   307→ * @param generationId - The generation to share
   308→ * @param taskId - The task associated with the generation
   309→ * @param shotId - Optional shot ID for final videos (to fetch input images and settings)
   310→ */
   311→export function useShareGeneration(
   312→  generationId: string | undefined,
   313→  taskId: string | null | undefined,
   314→  shotId?: string | null,
   315→  options?: UseShareGenerationOptions
   316→): UseShareGenerationResult {
   317→  const { initialShareSlug, onShareCreated } = options ?? {};
   318→  const [shareSlug, setShareSlug] = useState<string | null>(initialShareSlug ?? null);
   319→  const [isCreatingShare, setIsCreatingShare] = useState(false);
   320→  const [shareCopied, setShareCopied] = useState(false);
   321→  // Reset share state when shot/generation changes
   322→  useEffect(() => {
   323→    setShareSlug(initialShareSlug ?? null);
   324→    setShareCopied(false);
   325→  }, [generationId, shotId, initialShareSlug]);
   326→
   327→  // Generate a short, URL-friendly random string
   328→  const generateShareSlug = (length: number = 10): string => {
   329→    const chars = [REDACTED];
   330→    let result = '';
   331→    const randomValues = new Uint8Array(length);
   332→    crypto.getRandomValues(randomValues);
   333→    
   334→    for (let i = 0; i < length; i++) {
   335→      result += chars[randomValues[i] % chars.length];
   336→    }
   337→    
   338→    return result;
   339→  };
   340→
   341→  const handleShare = useCallback(async (e: React.MouseEvent | React.TouchEvent) => {
   342→    e.stopPropagation();
   343→    e.preventDefault();
   344→
   345→    if (!generationId) {
   346→      toast({
   347→        title: 'Cannot create share',
   348→        description: 'Generation information not available',
   349→        variant: 'destructive',
   350→      });
   351→      return;
   352→    }
   353→
   354→    if (shareSlug) {
   355→      await copyShareLinkAndNotify({
   356→        slug: shareSlug,
   357→        successTitle: 'Link copied!',
   358→        successDescription: 'Share link copied to clipboard',
   359→        fallbackTitle: 'Share ready',
   360→        fallbackDescription: 'Click the copy button to copy the link',
   361→        setShareCopied,
   362→      });
   363→      return;
   364→    }
   365→
   366→    setIsCreatingShare(true);
   367→    try {
   368→      const { data: sessionData } = await supabase().auth.getSession();
   369→      const [REDACTED]?.access_token;
   370→      const userId = sessionData.session?.user.id;
   371→
   372→      if (!accessToken || !userId) {
   373→        toast({
   374→          title: 'Authentication required',
   375→          description: 'Please sign in to create share links',
   376→          variant: 'destructive',
   377→        });
   378→        return;
   379→      }
   380→
   381→      const existingSlug = await fetchExistingShareSlug(generationId, userId);
   382→      if (existingSlug) {
   383→        setShareSlug(existingSlug);
   384→        await copyShareLinkAndNotify({
   385→          slug: existingSlug,
   386→          successTitle: 'Link copied!',
   387→          successDescription: 'Existing share link copied to clipboard',
   388→          fallbackTitle: 'Share found',
   389→          fallbackDescription: 'Click the copy button to copy the link',
   390→          setShareCopied,
   391→        });
   392→        return;
   393→      }
   394→
   395→      const { generationData, augmentedTaskData } = await fetchShareCachedData(
   396→        generationId,
   397→        taskId,
   398→        shotId,
   399→      );
   400→
   401→      const newSlug = await insertShareWithRetry({
   402→        generationId,
   403→        taskId,
   404→        shotId,
   405→        userId,
   406→        generationData,
   407→        augmentedTaskData,
   408→        generateShareSlug,
   409→      });
   410→
   411→      if (!newSlug) {
   412→        toast({
   413→          title: 'Share failed',
   414→          description: 'Failed to generate unique link. Please try again.',
   415→          variant: 'destructive',
   416→        });
   417→        return;
   418→      }
   419→
   420→      setShareSlug(newSlug);
   421→      onShareCreated?.(generationId, newSlug);
   422→
   423→      await copyShareLinkAndNotify({
   424→        slug: newSlug,
   425→        successTitle: 'Share created!',
   426→        successDescription: 'Share link copied to clipboard',
   427→        fallbackTitle: 'Share created',
   428→        fallbackDescription: 'Click the copy button to copy the link',
   429→        setShareCopied,
   430→      });
   431→    } catch (error) {
   432→      normalizeAndPresentError(error, {
   433→        context: 'useShareGeneration',
   434→        toastTitle: 'Share failed',
   435→        logData: { message: 'Please try again' },
   436→      });
   437→    } finally {
   438→      setIsCreatingShare(false);
   439→    }
   440→  }, [generationId, onShareCreated, shareSlug, shotId, taskId]);
   441→
   442→  return {
   443→    handleShare,
   444→    isCreatingShare,
   445→    shareCopied,
   446→    shareSlug
   447→  };
   448→}
   449→

     6→export function resolveSettingsScopeTable(scope: SettingsScopeIdentifier): SettingsScopeTableName {
     7→  switch (scope) {

# Triage Tooling Fixes

Fixes to the desloppify triage flow identified by 5-agent audit. Ranked by impact.

## Master Checklist

- [ ] **1. Path validation in ENRICH gate** (high impact, ~1 day)
- [ ] **2. Effort tag requirement in ENRICH** (medium impact, ~0.5 day)
- [ ] **3. Cross-cluster file overlap warning in ORGANIZE** (medium impact, ~1 day)
- [ ] **4. Step title length cap** (low impact, ~0.5 day)
- [ ] **5. Cluster dependency field support** (medium impact, ~0.5 day)

---

## 1. Path validation in ENRICH gate

**The single most impactful change.** Would have caught 3 of 7 documented failure types.

### Problem
`_shallow_steps()` in `_stage_validation.py:232-247` checks that steps have a `detail` field but never validates that file paths in the detail actually exist on disk. Steps referencing `src/nonexistent/path.ts` pass identically to correct paths.

### Fix

**File:** `desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/_stage_validation.py`

Add a new function `_steps_with_bad_paths()` that:
1. Iterates all manual cluster steps (same loop shape as `_shallow_steps`)
2. Extracts file paths from `detail` text using regex: `re.findall(r'(?:src|supabase)/[\w./-]+\.\w+', detail)`
3. For each extracted path, checks `Path(repo_root / path).exists()`
4. Also tries common extension swaps: `.ts` ↔ `.tsx`, `.js` ↔ `.jsx`
5. Returns `list[tuple[str, int, list[str]]]` — `(cluster_name, step_index, bad_paths)`

Call it from two places:
- **`_cmd_stage_enrich()`** at line ~436 (after `_shallow_steps` check): if bad paths found, print warning with details but don't block (first pass is advisory)
- **`_confirm_enrich()`** at line ~376 (after `_shallow_steps` re-check): if bad paths found, **block confirmation** with actionable error listing each bad path and which step it's in

```python
import re
from pathlib import Path

_PATH_RE = re.compile(r'(?:src|supabase)/[\w./-]+\.\w+')
_EXT_SWAPS = {'.ts': '.tsx', '.tsx': '.ts', '.js': '.jsx', '.jsx': '.js'}

def _steps_with_bad_paths(plan: dict, repo_root: Path) -> list[tuple[str, int, list[str]]]:
    """Return steps referencing file paths that don't exist on disk."""
    results = []
    for name, cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).items():
        if cluster.get("auto") or not cluster.get("issue_ids"):
            continue
        for i, step in enumerate(cluster.get("action_steps") or []):
            if not isinstance(step, dict):
                continue
            detail = step.get("detail", "")
            if not detail:
                continue
            bad = []
            for path_str in _PATH_RE.findall(detail):
                p = repo_root / path_str
                if p.exists():
                    continue
                # Try extension swap
                alt_ext = _EXT_SWAPS.get(p.suffix)
                if alt_ext and p.with_suffix(alt_ext).exists():
                    continue
                bad.append(path_str)
            if bad:
                results.append((name, i + 1, bad))
    return results
```

**Repo root resolution:** Use the existing `command_runtime(args).root` or find `.desloppify/` parent.

### Tests
- Step with valid path → not flagged
- Step with bad path → flagged
- Step with `.ts` that exists as `.tsx` → not flagged (extension swap)
- Step with no paths in detail → not flagged
- Auto clusters skipped

---

## 2. Effort tag requirement in ENRICH

### Problem
Steps mix one-line fixes with multi-day refactors. No effort indication anywhere. A PM or executor can't estimate scope.

### Fix

**File:** `desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/_stage_validation.py`

Add `_steps_without_effort()`:
```python
_VALID_EFFORTS = {"trivial", "small", "medium", "large"}

def _steps_without_effort(plan: dict) -> list[tuple[str, int, int]]:
    """Return (cluster_name, missing_count, total) for steps without effort tags."""
    results = []
    for name, cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).items():
        if cluster.get("auto") or not cluster.get("issue_ids"):
            continue
        steps = cluster.get("action_steps") or []
        if not steps:
            continue
        missing = sum(
            1 for s in steps
            if isinstance(s, dict) and s.get("effort") not in _VALID_EFFORTS
        )
        if missing:
            results.append((name, missing, len(steps)))
    return results
```

Call from `_cmd_stage_enrich()` — **warning only** (not a blocker, since effort is a new field and we don't want to break existing workflows):
```python
untagged = _steps_without_effort(plan)
if untagged:
    total_missing = sum(n for _, n, _ in untagged)
    print(colorize(f"  Note: {total_missing} step(s) have no effort tag.", "yellow"))
    print(colorize("  Consider: desloppify plan cluster update <name> --update-step N --effort small", "dim"))
```

**File:** `desloppify/app/commands/plan/cluster_handlers.py`

Add `--effort` argument support to `_cmd_cluster_update()`:
- New arg: `effort: str | None = getattr(args, "effort", None)`
- In the `update_step` block (~line 678), add: `if effort: old["effort"] = effort`
- In the `add_step` block (~line 661), add: `if effort: new_step["effort"] = effort`

**File:** `desloppify/app/cli_support/parser_groups_plan_impl.py`

Add `--effort` to the cluster update subparser with `choices=["trivial", "small", "medium", "large"]`.

### Tests
- Steps with effort field → not flagged
- Steps without effort → flagged with count
- `--effort` flag persists on step dict

## 3. Cross-cluster file overlap warning in ORGANIZE

### Problem
Clusters touch the same files without knowing it. The sequencing agent found 13 files referenced by 2+ clusters, causing potential merge conflicts and ordering hazards.

### Fix

**File:** `desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/_stage_validation.py`

Add `_cluster_file_overlaps()`:
```python
def _cluster_file_overlaps(plan: dict) -> list[tuple[str, str, list[str]]]:
    """Return pairs of clusters with overlapping file references in step details."""
    cluster_files: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
    for name, cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).items():
        if cluster.get("auto") or not cluster.get("issue_ids"):
            continue
        paths = set()
        for step in cluster.get("action_steps") or []:
            if isinstance(step, dict) and step.get("detail"):
                paths.update(_PATH_RE.findall(step["detail"]))
        if paths:
            cluster_files[name] = paths

    overlaps = []
    names = sorted(cluster_files.keys())
    for i, a in enumerate(names):
        for b in names[i + 1:]:
            shared = cluster_files[a] & cluster_files[b]
            if shared:
                overlaps.append((a, b, sorted(shared)))
    return overlaps
```

Call from `_confirm_organize()` in `confirmations.py` — **warning, not blocker**:
```python
overlaps = _cluster_file_overlaps(plan)
if overlaps:
    print(colorize(f"\n  Note: {len(overlaps)} cluster pair(s) reference the same files:", "yellow"))
    for a, b, files in overlaps[:5]:
        print(colorize(f"    {a} ↔ {b}: {len(files)} shared file(s)", "yellow"))
    print(colorize("  Consider adding depends_on_clusters or sequencing notes.", "dim"))
```

### Tests
- Two clusters referencing same file → overlap reported
- Clusters with no file overlap → clean
- Auto clusters excluded

---

## 4. Step title length cap

### Problem
Titles range from 64 to 271 characters. Long titles make the plan unreadable at a glance and unusable as commit messages.

### Fix

**File:** `desloppify/app/commands/plan/cluster_handlers.py`

In `_cmd_cluster_update()`, when setting step title (~line 661 and 681):
```python
MAX_STEP_TITLE = 150
if len(title) > MAX_STEP_TITLE:
    print(colorize(
        f"  Warning: step title is {len(title)} chars (recommended max {MAX_STEP_TITLE}).",
        "yellow",
    ))
    print(colorize("  Move implementation detail to --detail instead.", "dim"))
```

Advisory only — don't block, just warn.

### Tests
- Long title → warning printed
- Short title → no warning

## 5. Cluster dependency field support

### Problem
No way to express "do cluster A before cluster B." The sequencing agent found 8 cross-cluster dependencies that aren't documented anywhere in the plan data.

### Fix

**File:** `desloppify/app/commands/plan/cluster_handlers.py`

Add `--depends-on` argument to cluster update:
```python
depends_on: list[str] | None = getattr(args, "depends_on", None)
if depends_on is not None:
    # Validate cluster names exist
    all_clusters = set(plan.get("clusters", {}).keys())
    bad = [n for n in depends_on if n not in all_clusters]
    if bad:
        print(colorize(f"  Unknown cluster(s): {', '.join(bad)}", "red"))
        return
    cluster["depends_on_clusters"] = depends_on
```

**File:** `desloppify/app/cli_support/parser_groups_plan_impl.py`

Add `--depends-on` with `nargs="+"` to the cluster update subparser.

**File:** `desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/confirmations.py`

In `_confirm_organize()`, after the plan summary, check for dependency violations:
```python
# Check that clusters don't depend on themselves or form cycles
clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
for name, c in clusters.items():
    deps = c.get("depends_on_clusters", [])
    if name in deps:
        print(colorize(f"  Warning: {name} depends on itself.", "yellow"))
```

### Tests
- `--depends-on` persists on cluster dict
- Invalid cluster name → error
- Self-dependency → warning

## Investigation Report

### [34580232] Task.taskType is plain `string` — FALSE POSITIVE

The `Task.taskType` field is typed as `TaskType`, which is defined at line 50 of `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/types/database.ts`:

```ts
export type TaskType = KnownTaskType | (string & { readonly __taskTypeBrand?: never });
```

This is a branded-string union pattern: `KnownTaskType` is a union of ~25 string literals from the `KNOWN_TASK_TYPES` const object (lines 18-47), and the wider `string` arm allows unknown task types to pass without breaking. Task type checks can use `KNOWN_TASK_TYPES` constants. This is a deliberate, reasonable design for an extensible system where new task types are added in the backend.

### [4c9cd049] Task.params typed as Record<string, unknown> with no discriminated union — GENUINE but PARTIALLY ADDRESSED

`Task.params` is typed as `TaskParams` (line 150), which is a union of 6+ specific interfaces (lines 86-93: `IndividualTravelSegmentTaskParams`, `JoinClipsOrchestratorTaskParams`, etc.) plus the fallback `TaskParamRecord`. However, this is **not a discriminated union** — there's no discriminant field to narrow which variant you have. In practice, all the specific interfaces extend `TaskParamRecord`, so they don't actually constrain anything at the usage site. The issue is genuine but low severity since the codebase handles this via runtime narrowing helpers (`asRecord`, `asString`, etc.).

**Are [34580232] and [4c9cd049] duplicates?** No — 34580232 is about `taskType` (which is actually well-typed), and 4c9cd049 is about `params` (which genuinely lacks a usable discriminated union). They address different fields.

### [38570823] generationTransformers.ts uses 12+ unsafe `as` casts on JSONB data — FALSE POSITIVE

The file contains exactly **2** `as` casts (lines 94 and 411), not 12+. All other JSONB narrowing uses the safe runtime helpers `asRecord()`, `asString()`, and `firstString()` imported from `jsonNarrowing.ts`. These helpers perform actual type checks before returning typed values. The 2 remaining casts are:
- Line 94: `variantCountsData as Array<{...}>` — narrowing a Supabase query result whose shape is known from the `.select()` call.
- Line 411: `asRecord(shotGen.metadata) as GenerationMetadata | null` — narrowing after a runtime `asRecord` check.

Both are reasonable. The "12+" count is significantly inflated.

### [6d6fa5e4] Task payload builders return Record<string, unknown>, discarding type info — GENUINE

`buildTravelBetweenImagesPayload()` in `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/lib/tasks/travelBetweenImages/payloadBuilder.ts` (line 188) returns `Record<string, unknown>` despite constructing a well-structured object from typed input (`TravelBetweenImagesTaskInput`). Similarly, helpers in `src/shared/lib/taskCreation/payloadMapping.ts` (line 11) and `src/shared/lib/taskCreation/hiresFix.ts` (line 7) return `Record<string, unknown>`. This discards compile-time knowledge of the payload shape. It's genuine but low-priority — payloads are serialized to JSONB and the consumer is an edge function, so the type info wouldn't propagate across the boundary anyway.

### [0b9c4a0b] asRecord/asString/asStringArray helpers duplicated between taskParamsUtils.ts and task-utils.ts — FALSE POSITIVE

Both files import these helpers from the **same canonical source**: `@/shared/lib/jsonNarrowing` (defined at `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/lib/jsonNarrowing.ts`). There is no duplication of implementation. `task-utils.ts` has a local `firstString` wrapper (line 11) that just delegates to the imported `firstNonEmptyString`, which is a trivial alias, not meaningful duplication.

---

### Summary

| Issue | Verdict | Notes |
|-------|---------|-------|
| [34580232] taskType is plain string | False positive | Uses branded string union with `KnownTaskType` |
| [4c9cd049] params lacks discriminated union | Genuine, low severity | Union exists but isn't discriminated; runtime narrowing compensates |
| [38570823] 12+ unsafe `as` casts | False positive | Only 2 casts, both reasonable; rest use safe runtime helpers |
| [6d6fa5e4] payload builders return Record | Genuine, low priority | Type info lost but payloads cross a serialization boundary |
| [0b9c4a0b] helpers duplicated | False positive | Both files import from single source `jsonNarrowing.ts` |

## Investigation Report

### design_coherence Issues

**[898b3c7d] GenerationTokenPanel -- "18 individual props where a config object would be clearer"**

- **Actual prop count: 18** -- confirmed. The `GenerationTokenPanelProps` interface at lines 32-49 has exactly 18 props.
- **Is it genuine?** Partially. The props are mostly value/setter pairs (computerType/setComputerType, gpuType/setGpuType, etc.). A config object pattern could group the 4 paired settings (computer, gpu, memory, shell) plus the debug toggle, but the component is a leaf display component receiving controlled state. Grouping into a config object just moves the destructuring one level up.
- **Verdict: Low-value fix.** The props are logically coherent (hardware config + UI state). The real solution would be to push `useCommandVisibility` and `useCopyFeedback` up or have the parent pass a single settings object, but the component is 430 lines and already well-structured. This is cosmetic.

**[b634fc71] useGenerationsPaneController -- "returns 60+ values mixing pane lifecycle, filters, data, and navigation"**

- **Actual return count: 65** -- confirmed (lines 217-282, I count 65 properties).
- **Is it genuine?** Yes, this is a real problem. The hook at `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/components/GenerationsPane/hooks/useGenerationsPaneController.ts` is 283 lines and mixes pane UI state, filter state, gallery data/pagination, interaction lifecycle, modal state, and navigation. The triage doc (Task 3 in `tasks/2026-03-05-desloppify-triage.md`) already identifies this as a decomposition target.
- **Verdict: Genuine issue, decomposition plan already exists and is reasonable.** The suggested split into 4 sub-hooks is appropriate given the 5 unrelated concerns.

**[3e2233af] useAddNewPresetTabController -- "mixes form state, effect-based sync, and submission in 455 lines"**

- **Actual line count: 455** -- confirmed (file is exactly 455 lines at `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/components/PhaseConfigSelectorModal/hooks/useAddNewPresetTabController.ts`).
- **Is it genuine?** Partially. The hook does mix three concerns but already uses `useReducer` properly (lines 46-152 for the reducer, lines 153-185 for initial state factory). The "effect-based sync" (3 useEffects at lines 246-328) is the real smell -- these sync external state changes (editingPreset, currentSettings) into the reducer. The submission handler (lines 336-430) is one large callback.
- **Verdict: Genuine but overstated.** The reducer pattern is good architecture. The effects are necessary for syncing external prop changes. The submission handler could be extracted but it's a single cohesive flow. Splitting this into multiple hooks risks creating awkward inter-hook dependencies. A more targeted fix would be to extract just the submit handler into a separate function. Calling it "mixes form state, effect-based sync, and submission" makes it sound worse than it is -- the reducer IS the form state management, and it's well-structured.

**[24f8d243] Tour callback -- "uses hardcoded step indices (0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 8) instead of step identifiers"**

- **Is it genuine? No -- FALSE POSITIVE.** The code at `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/components/ProductTour/ProductTour.tsx` uses named constants from `TOUR_STEPS` (defined in `tourSteps.ts`), not hardcoded indices. For example: `TOUR_STEPS.OPEN_GALLERY`, `TOUR_STEPS.GALLERY_SECTION`, `TOUR_STEPS.GENERATE_IMAGES`, `TOUR_STEPS.HOW_IT_WORKS`, `TOUR_STEPS.OPEN_FIRST_SHOT`, `TOUR_STEPS.TASKS_PANE`. The `TOUR_STEPS` object maps semantic names to indices. This is exactly the pattern the issue suggests should be used.
- **Verdict: False positive. The code already uses step identifiers.**

**[701717ab] FinalVideoSectionDisplay -- "takes 15 props mixing display, interaction, and state concerns"**

- **Actual prop count: 15** -- confirmed. The `FinalVideoSectionDisplayProps` interface at lines 11-27 of `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/tools/travel-between-images/components/FinalVideoSectionDisplay.tsx` has exactly 15 props.
- **Is it genuine?** The component is only 155 lines total and is a straightforward presentational component with 3 render branches (skeleton, video, empty state). Many of these props are passed straight through to `VideoItem`. The "mixing display, interaction, and state" complaint is exaggerated -- the props are what you'd expect for a video display with delete capability.
- **Verdict: Low-value fix.** The component is small and clear. Grouping props into sub-objects would add indirection without improving readability. The real issue, if any, is that `VideoItem` takes too many props (it receives 12+ from this component), but that's a different finding.

**Remaining 2 design_coherence issues:** No specific hashes were provided, so I cannot investigate them.

---

### mid_level_elegance Issues

**[384b83f8] useLoraPersistence -- "takes 14 destructured args from useLoraManager"**

- **Actual arg count: 7** -- the `UseLoraPersistenceArgs` interface at lines 24-32 of `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/domains/lora/hooks/loraPersistence.tsx` takes 7 arguments: `projectId`, `shotId`, `persistenceScope`, `persistenceKey`, `disableAutoLoad`, `enableProjectPersistence`, `manager`. The `manager` is a typed object (`LoraPersistenceManagerHandle` with 8 fields), so if you count those as individual args it's 14. But that's misleading -- the hook takes a structured interface, not 14 destructured args.
- **Is it genuine?** The hook does destructure `manager` internally (line 54-63), pulling out 8 properties. But it receives them as a structured object, which is the correct pattern. The claim of "14 destructured args" is **exaggerated** -- it's 7 params with one being a structured handle.
- **Verdict: Exaggerated. The code already uses the structured-object pattern that would typically be suggested as the fix.**

**[90d25443] useAdjustedTaskDetails -- "mixes 3-level param resolution with loading-state orchestration"**

- **Is it genuine?** Partially. The hook at `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/domains/media-lightbox/hooks/useAdjustedTaskDetails.ts` (200 lines) does combine two things: (1) resolving which task params to show for a variant (lines 113-149, with 3-level fallback: matching taskDetailsData > fetched source task > variant params), and (2) computing loading state (lines 178-193). However, these are tightly coupled -- the loading state depends on whether the param resolution is complete.
- **Verdict: Genuine observation, but splitting would be over-engineering.** The param resolution and loading state are interdependent. The 3-level resolution is well-commented and the logic flow is clear. Extracting the loading-state logic into a separate hook would create awkward coupling. ## Investigation Report

### convention_outlier Issues

**[ec390340] Default exports in ~19 shared/component files while ~200+ siblings use named exports**

**Verdict: GENUINE, but inflated count.** Actual count is **15 files** with `export default` in `src/shared/components/`, out of ~691 total files (364+ use named `export function`/`export const`). The ratio is real -- default exports are a clear minority (~2%). The claim of "~19" is slightly overstated but directionally correct. **Fixable by batch script** (convert `export default X` to `export function X` / `export const X` and update imports).

**[649afc52] travel-between-images/Timeline uses default exports throughout**

**Verdict: PARTIALLY TRUE.** Only 6 of ~75 non-test files in the Timeline directory use `export default` (index.tsx, DropIndicator, PairRegion, TimelineItem, TimelineRuler, TrailingEndpoint, TimelineContainer). The rest (~69 files) use named exports. "Throughout" is an overstatement -- it's a handful of leaf-level rendering components plus the barrel file. Still a genuine inconsistency with the codebase norm. **Fixable by batch script.**

**[0fcdb613] shared/components mixes PascalCase, kebab-case, and lowercase directory names**

**Verdict: GENUINE.** Confirmed three naming conventions in `src/shared/components/`:
- PascalCase directories (majority): `GenerationsPane`, `GlobalHeader`, `MediaGallery`, `PhaseConfigSelectorModal`, etc.
- kebab-case directories: `file-input`, `generation-controls`, `hover-scrub-video`, `inline-segment-video`
- lowercase directories: `dialogs`, `lora`, `panes`, `resources`, `shots`, `theme`, `transitions`, `ui`

This is a real mix. However, the lowercase ones could be argued as "category/namespace" directories (grouping multiple components) vs PascalCase for "single component" directories, which is a defensible convention. The kebab-case ones are the true outliers. **Fixable by batch rename + import updates**, but high-risk (many import paths to update). A codemod tool would be needed.

**[0efe16fc] PhaseConfigSelectorModal uses three different type file patterns simultaneously**

**Verdict: GENUINE.** Confirmed three patterns coexist in this single component directory:
1. `types.ts` (root-level barrel)
2. `PhaseConfigVertical.types.ts` (dot-notation colocated)
3. `components/BrowsePresetsTab.types.ts`, `components/AddNewPresetTab.types.ts` (dot-notation in subdirectory)

These are three distinct type-file naming conventions. The dot-notation files belong to specific sub-components, while `types.ts` is the shared root types file. **Manual fix** -- need to decide on one convention and consolidate.

**[4e1f67e6] GlobalHeaderController.ts exports useGlobalHeaderController() but filename omits use prefix**

**Verdict: GENUINE, but this IS the codebase convention.** Looking at all Controller files: every other controller file uses the `use` prefix in both filename AND export: `useShotEditorController.ts`, `useGenerationController.ts`, `useVideoLightboxController.ts`, etc. `GlobalHeaderController.ts` is the only one that omits the `use` prefix in the filename while the export is `useGlobalHeaderController()`. This is a genuine outlier. **Trivially fixable** by renaming to `useGlobalHeaderController.ts` and updating the one import.

**Remaining 2 convention_outlier issues:** The user mentioned "Plus 2 more" but didn't provide hashes. The 5 above are the ones explicitly listed.

### ai_generated_debt Issues

**[340e2464] ShotImagesEditor/types.ts has ~20 JSDoc comments that restate property names**

**Verdict: PARTIALLY TRUE, but overstated.** The file has **47 JSDoc comments** total, not ~20. However, many are NOT simple property name restatements. Looking at the actual comments:
- Some genuinely add value: `/** Optional preloaded images (for read-only/share views) - bypasses database queries */`, `/** Maximum frame limit for timeline gaps (77 when smoothContinuations enabled, 81 otherwise) */`
- Some are borderline restating: `/** Selected shot id */` for `selectedShotId`, `/** Whether currently uploading image */` for `isUploadingImage`
- Some add context not obvious from the name: `/** Image deletion callback - id is shot_generations.id (unique per entry) */`

I count roughly **8-10** that truly just restate the property name without adding information (e.g., `/** Upload progress (0-100) */` for `uploadProgress` -- though even that adds the range). The claim of "~20 restating" is inflated. Many comments add genuinely useful context about semantics, edge cases, or valid values. **Mixed fix**: remove the truly redundant ones (~8-10), keep the informative ones. Manual review needed per comment.

**[599dd262] Heavy-rule section separators (// ====) used across 78 files**

**Verdict: GENUINE, slightly lower count.** I found **59 files** matching `^// ====` (not 78). The ShotImagesEditor/types.ts file is a clear example with two separator blocks. These are a common AI-generated pattern that adds visual noise without IDE-level benefit. **Fixable by batch script** (`sed` to remove lines matching `^// =+$`). Low risk since they're just comments.

**[a051423a] Module-level docstrings restate typed interfaces**

**Verdict: GENUINE.** Found **123 files** with module-level docstrings starting with patterns like `/** Types for...`, `/** Hook for...`, `/** Utilities for...`. The ShotImagesEditor/types.ts example is canonical: `/** * Types for ShotImagesEditor and its sub-components. */` -- this adds zero information beyond what the filename and exports already convey. However, some module docstrings in the broader set may add context not obvious from the filename. **Mostly fixable by batch script** (remove `/** ... */` blocks at file top that match `Types for|Props for|Hook for|Utilities for` patterns), but would benefit from manual review of edge cases.

usage: desloppify plan skip [-h] [--reason REASON] [--review-after N]

                            PATTERN [PATTERN ...]

options:

  --permanent       Mark as wontfix (score-affecting, requires --note and
                    --attest)
  --false-positive  Mark as false positive (requires --attest)
  --note NOTE       Explanation (required for --permanent)
  --attest ATTEST   Attestation (required for --permanent and --false-
                    positive)
  --confirm         Required when skipping more than 5 items at once

                              [--session-ttl-hours SESSION_TTL_HOURS]

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --stage {observe,reflect,organize,enrich}
                        Stage to record
  --report REPORT       Stage report text
  --complete            Mark triage complete
  --strategy STRATEGY   Strategy summary (for --complete)
  --confirm-existing    Fast-track confirmation of existing plan
  --note NOTE           Note for --confirm-existing
  --start               Manually start triage (inject triage::pending, clear
                        prior stages)
  --confirm {observe,reflect,organize,enrich}
                        Confirm a completed stage (shows summary, requires
                        --attestation)
  --attestation ATTESTATION
                        Attestation text confirming stage review (min 30
                        chars, used with --confirm)
  --confirmed CONFIRMED
                        Plan validation text for --confirm-existing (confirms
                        plan review)
  --dry-run             Preview mode
  --run-stages          Run triage stages via subagent runner
  --runner {codex}      Subagent runner type (default: codex)
  --stage-timeout-seconds STAGE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
                        Per-stage timeout in seconds (default: 1800)
  --only-stages ONLY_STAGES
                        Comma-separated list of stages to run (default: all)
  --external-start      Start a Claude external triage session
  --external-submit     Validate and submit a Claude external triage session
  --session-id SESSION_ID
                        Session ID for --external-submit
  --external-runner {claude}
                        External runner type (default: claude)
  --session-ttl-hours SESSION_TTL_HOURS
                        Session expiry in hours (default: 24)

    24→
    25→function parsePendingJoinClips(raw: string): PendingJoinClipParseResult | null {
    26→  let parsed: unknown;
    27→  try {
    28→    parsed = JSON.parse(raw);
    29→  } catch {
    30→    return null;
    31→  }
    32→
    33→  if (!Array.isArray(parsed)) {

    35→  }

    37→  const entries: PendingJoinClipEntry[] = [];
    38→  let invalidCount = 0;
    39→  for (const value of parsed) {

    41→      invalidCount += 1;
    42→      continue;
    43→    }

    47→      typeof candidate.videoUrl !== 'string'
    48→      || typeof candidate.generationId !== 'string'
    49→      || typeof candidate.timestamp !== 'number'
    50→      || !Number.isFinite(candidate.timestamp)
    51→    ) {
    52→      invalidCount += 1;
    53→      continue;
    54→    }
    55→
    56→    entries.push({
    57→      videoUrl: candidate.videoUrl,
    58→      generationId: candidate.generationId,
    59→      timestamp: candidate.timestamp,
    60→      ...(typeof candidate.thumbnailUrl === 'string' && candidate.thumbnailUrl.length > 0
    61→        ? { thumbnailUrl: candidate.thumbnailUrl }
    62→        : {}),
    63→      ...(typeof candidate.projectId === 'string' && candidate.projectId.length > 0
    64→        ? { projectId: candidate.projectId }
    65→        : {}),
    66→      ...(typeof candidate.userId === 'string' && candidate.userId.length > 0
    67→        ? { userId: candidate.userId }
    68→        : {}),
    69→    });
    70→  }
    71→
    72→  return { entries, invalidCount };
    73→}

    75→/** Create a throwaway <video> to read duration from a URL. */
    76→function getVideoDurationFromUrl(videoUrl: string): Promise<number> {
    77→  return new Promise<number>(resolve => {
    78→    const videoElement = document.createElement('video');
    79→    videoElement.preload = 'metadata';
    80→    videoElement.onloadedmetadata = () => resolve(videoElement.duration);
    81→    videoElement.onerror = () => resolve(0);
    82→    videoElement.src = videoUrl;
    83→  });

   102→async function toPendingClipActions(
   103→  entries: PendingJoinClipEntry[],
   104→  readVideoDuration: (videoUrl: string) => Promise<number>,
   105→): Promise<PendingClipAction[]> {
   106→  const actions: PendingClipAction[] = [];
   107→
   108→  for (const { videoUrl, thumbnailUrl, generationId } of entries) {
   109→    if (!videoUrl) continue;
   110→
   111→    const durationSeconds = await readVideoDuration(videoUrl);
   112→
   113→    const clip: VideoClip = {
   114→      id: generateUUID(),
   115→      url: videoUrl,
   116→      posterUrl: thumbnailUrl,
   117→      durationSeconds,
   118→      loaded: false,
   119→      playing: false,
   120→      generationId,
   121→    };
   122→
   123→    actions.push({ type: 'deferred_insert', clip });
   124→  }
   125→
   126→  return actions;
   127→}

   129→export async function consumePendingJoinClips(
   130→  options: ConsumePendingJoinClipsOptions = {},
   131→): Promise<OperationResult<PendingClipAction[]>> {
   132→  const projectId = options.projectId ?? null;
   133→  const readVideoDuration = options.readVideoDuration ?? getVideoDurationFromUrl;
   134→
   135→  try {
   136→    const userId = readUserIdFromStorage();
   137→
   138→    const inMemoryPending = consumeJoinClipsIntents({ projectId, userId });
   139→    if (inMemoryPending.length > 0) {
   140→      const now = Date.now();
   141→      const scopedRecentClips = inMemoryPending.filter(
   142→        (clip) =>
   143→          now - clip.timestamp < PENDING_CLIPS_TTL_MS
   144→          && isPendingJoinClipInScope(clip, { projectId, userId }),
   145→      );
   146→      if (scopedRecentClips.length === 0) {
   147→        localStorage.removeItem(getPendingJoinClipsStorageKey(projectId, userId));
   148→        return operationSuccess([]);
   149→      }
   150→
   151→      const actions = await toPendingClipActions(scopedRecentClips, readVideoDuration);
   152→      localStorage.removeItem(getPendingJoinClipsStorageKey(projectId, userId));
   153→      return operationSuccess(actions);
   154→    }
   155→
   156→    const pendingKeys = getPendingJoinClipsCandidateKeys({ projectId, userId });
   157→    const pendingSource = pendingKeys
   158→      .map((key) => ({ key, raw: localStorage.getItem(key) }))
   159→      .find((item) => typeof item.raw === 'string' && item.raw.length > 0);
   160→
   161→    if (!pendingSource || !pendingSource.raw) {
   162→      return operationSuccess([]);
   163→    }
   164→
   165→    const parsedPendingClips = parsePendingJoinClips(pendingSource.raw);
   166→    if (!parsedPendingClips) {
   167→      normalizeAndPresentError(new Error('Invalid pending join clips payload'), {
   168→        context: 'JoinClipsPage.pendingClipsInvalid',
   169→        showToast: false,
   170→        logData: { [REDACTED] },
   171→      });
   172→      localStorage.removeItem(pendingSource.key);
   173→      return operationFailure(new Error('Invalid pending join clips payload'), {
   174→        policy: 'degrade',
   175→        errorCode: 'pending_join_clips_invalid_payload',
   176→        message: 'Invalid pending join clips payload',
   177→        recoverable: true,
   178→        cause: { [REDACTED] },
   179→      });
   180→    }
   181→
   182→    if (parsedPendingClips.invalidCount > 0) {
   183→      normalizeAndPresentError(new Error('Dropped invalid pending join clip entries'), {
   184→        context: 'JoinClipsPage.pendingClipsPartialRecovery',
   185→        showToast: false,
   186→        logData: {
   187→          [REDACTED],
   188→          totalEntries: parsedPendingClips.entries.length + parsedPendingClips.invalidCount,
   189→          invalidEntries: parsedPendingClips.invalidCount,
   190→        },
   191→      });
   192→    }
   193→
   194→    const now = Date.now();
   195→    const recentClips = parsedPendingClips.entries.filter(
   196→      clip => now - clip.timestamp < PENDING_CLIPS_TTL_MS,
   197→    );
   198→    const scopedRecentClips = recentClips.filter((clip) =>
   199→      isPendingJoinClipInScope(clip, { projectId, userId }),
   200→    );
   201→
   202→    if (scopedRecentClips.length === 0) {
   203→      localStorage.removeItem(pendingSource.key);
   204→      return operationSuccess([], {
   205→        ...(parsedPendingClips.invalidCount > 0 ? { policy: 'degrade' } : {}),
   206→      });
   207→    }
   208→
   209→    const actions = await toPendingClipActions(scopedRecentClips, readVideoDuration);
   210→
   211→    localStorage.removeItem(pendingSource.key);
   212→    return operationSuccess(actions, {
   213→      ...(parsedPendingClips.invalidCount > 0 ? { policy: 'degrade' } : {}),
   214→    });
   215→  } catch (error) {
   216→    normalizeAndPresentError(error, { context: 'JoinClipsPage', showToast: false });
   217→    return operationFailure(error, {
   218→      policy: 'degrade',
   219→      errorCode: 'pending_join_clips_read_failed',
   220→      message: 'Failed to consume pending join clips',
   221→      recoverable: true,
   222→      cause: error,
   223→    });
   224→  }
   225→}
   226→
   227→/**
   228→ * Apply pending clip actions to an existing clips array.
   229→ * Resolves each deferred action by filling the first available empty slot,
   230→ * or appending when no empty slots remain.
   231→ */
   232→export function applyPendingClipActions(
   233→  prevClips: VideoClip[],
   234→  actions: PendingClipAction[],
   235→): VideoClip[] {
   236→  let clips = [...prevClips];
   237→  // Track which indices have been filled by previous actions in this batch
   238→  const filledIndices = new Set<number>();
   239→
   240→  for (const action of actions) {
   241→    const emptyIndex = clips.findIndex(
   242→      (clip, idx) => !clip.url && !filledIndices.has(idx),
   243→    );
   244→
   245→    if (emptyIndex !== -1) {
   246→      clips = clips.map((clip, idx) =>
   247→        idx === emptyIndex
   248→          ? {
   249→              ...clip,
   250→              url: action.clip.url,
   251→              posterUrl: action.clip.posterUrl,
   252→              durationSeconds: action.clip.durationSeconds,
   253→              loaded: false,
   254→              playing: false,
   255→              generationId: action.clip.generationId,
   256→            }
   257→          : clip,
   258→      );
   259→      filledIndices.add(emptyIndex);
   260→    } else {
   261→      clips = [...clips, action.clip];
   262→    }
   263→  }
   264→
   265→  return clips;
   266→}
